cards.name: Contains Duplicate
cards.trick: Hash set. Check if the number was already seen before adding it. (Sorting is O(n log n) time, O(1) space.)

cards.name: Valid Anagram
cards.trick: Return false if lengths differ. Count chars with +1 for s and -1 for t in one pass, then check all counts are 0.

cards.name: Two Sum
cards.trick: One pass with a hash map of value -> index. For each x, look up target - x BEFORE inserting x.

cards.name: Group Anagrams
cards.time: O(n * k) (n words, k = max word length)
cards.trick: Use the 26-letter count tuple as the hash map key, not the sorted string. Anagrams share the same key. (Sorted-string key is O(n * k log k).)

cards.name: Top K Frequent Elements
cards.trick: Bucket sort. Count frequencies, then bucket[freq] = list of nums. Walk buckets from highest frequency down until you have k. (Heap is O(n log k).)

cards.name: Encode and Decode Strings
cards.trick: Length-prefix each string: "len#string". On decode read digits up to '#', then slice exactly len chars. Works even if the string contains '#' or digits.

cards.name: Product of Array Except Self
cards.trick: Prefix then suffix pass. Fill res[i] with the product of everything left of i, then sweep right-to-left multiplying by a running suffix product. No division.

cards.name: Valid Sudoku
cards.time: O(n^2) for an n x n board (O(1) for fixed 9x9)
cards.trick: One pass with a set per row, per column and per 3x3 box. Box key is (r // 3, c // 3). Skip '.' cells.

cards.name: Longest Consecutive Sequence
cards.trick: Put all nums in a set. Only start counting from a number with no n - 1 in the set (a sequence start), then count up. Each element is visited at most twice.

cards.name: Valid Palindrome
cards.trick: Pointers at both ends moving inward. Skip non-alphanumeric chars, compare lowercased chars, return false on any mismatch.

cards.name: Two Sum II Input Array Is Sorted
cards.trick: Array is sorted, so use pointers at both ends. Sum too big: move right pointer left. Sum too small: move left pointer right.

cards.name: 3Sum
cards.trick: Sort, fix i, then run two-pointer Two Sum II on the rest looking for -nums[i]. Skip duplicate values for i, and after finding a triplet skip duplicate left values.

cards.name: Container With Most Water
cards.trick: Pointers at both ends. Area = min(height) * width. Always move the shorter side, because moving the taller one can only shrink the area.

cards.name: Trapping Rain Water
cards.trick: Water at i = min(maxLeft, maxRight) - height[i]. Two pointers with running leftMax and rightMax: process the side with the smaller max, since that side is the bottleneck. (Prefix/suffix max arrays are O(n) space.)

cards.name: Best Time to Buy And Sell Stock
cards.trick: One pass. Track the minimum price so far (left/buy pointer) and update max profit = price - minPrice at each day.

cards.name: Longest Substring Without Repeating Characters
cards.trick: Variable-size window with a set. While s[r] is already in the window, remove s[l] and advance l. Then add s[r] and update max length.

cards.name: Longest Repeating Character Replacement
cards.trick: A window is valid if (window length - count of its most frequent char) <= k. Track counts and max frequency, shrink from the left when invalid. Max frequency never needs to decrease.

cards.name: Permutation In String
cards.trick: Fixed-size window of length len(s1) over s2. Keep letter counts for both and a matches counter of letters whose counts are equal. The window is a permutation when matches == 26.

cards.name: Minimum Window Substring
cards.trick: Count the chars needed from t. Expand r and track how many distinct chars are fully satisfied (have vs need). When have == need, record the window and shrink l while it stays valid.

cards.name: Sliding Window Maximum
cards.trick: Monotonic decreasing deque of indices. Pop from the back while the new value is larger, pop from the front when the index leaves the window. The front is always the window max.

cards.name: Binary Search
cards.trick: Pointers l and r, mid = l + (r - l) // 2. If target > nums[mid] then l = mid + 1, if smaller then r = mid - 1, else return mid. Loop while l <= r.

cards.name: Search a 2D Matrix
cards.trick: Treat the matrix as one sorted array of length m * n. Index mid maps to row = mid // cols and col = mid % cols. (Binary search the row, then the column, also works.)

cards.name: Koko Eating Bananas
cards.trick: Binary search on the eating speed k from 1 to max(piles). For a candidate k, hours = sum of ceil(pile / k). Find the smallest k with hours <= h.

cards.name: Find Minimum In Rotated Sorted Array
cards.trick: Compare nums[mid] to nums[r]. If nums[mid] > nums[r] the minimum is right of mid (l = mid + 1), otherwise r = mid. Loop while l < r.

cards.name: Search In Rotated Sorted Array
cards.trick: One half around mid is always sorted. Check which half is sorted (nums[l] <= nums[mid]), see if target falls inside it, otherwise search the other half.

cards.name: Time Based Key Value Store
cards.trick: Per key keep a list of (timestamp, value) in insertion order, which is already sorted by time. On get, binary search for the largest timestamp <= the query.

cards.name: Median of Two Sorted Arrays
cards.trick: Binary search the partition of the SMALLER array so the left sides together hold half the elements. The partition is right when maxLeft of each array <= minRight of the other. The median comes from those boundary values.

cards.name: Reverse Linked List
cards.trick: Iterate with prev and curr. Save curr.next, point curr.next at prev, advance both. Return prev. (Recursive version is O(n) space.)

cards.name: Merge Two Sorted Lists
cards.trick: Dummy head node plus a tail pointer. Repeatedly attach the smaller of the two heads, then attach whichever list is left over.

cards.name: Linked List Cycle
cards.trick: Floyd's tortoise and hare. Slow moves 1 step, fast moves 2. They meet only if there is a cycle. Fast hitting null means no cycle. (Hash set of nodes is O(n) space.)

cards.name: Reorder List
cards.trick: Three steps: find the middle with slow/fast pointers, reverse the second half in place, then merge the two halves alternately.

cards.name: Remove Nth Node From End of List
cards.trick: Dummy head and two pointers n apart. Advance fast n steps, then move both until fast reaches the end. slow.next is the node to remove.

cards.name: Copy List With Random Pointer
cards.trick: Two passes with a hash map old node -> new node. Pass 1 creates every copy, pass 2 wires next and random through the map. (Weaving copies between the original nodes gets O(1) extra space.)

cards.name: Add Two Numbers
cards.trick: Digits are stored in reverse, so add node by node with a carry. Use a dummy head and keep looping while either list or the carry remains.

cards.name: Find The Duplicate Number
cards.trick: Treat the array as a linked list where i points to nums[i]. The duplicate is the cycle entrance. Floyd's: find the meeting point, then restart one pointer from index 0 and move both one step at a time until they meet. Do not modify the array.

cards.name: LRU Cache
cards.trick: Hash map key -> node plus a doubly linked list ordered by recency with dummy head and tail. Every get or put moves the node to the most-recent end. When over capacity evict the node at the least-recent end.

cards.name: Merge K Sorted Lists
cards.space: O(1) extra with divide and conquer, O(k) with a heap
cards.trick: Merge the lists pairwise in rounds, reusing Merge Two Sorted Lists (divide and conquer). A min-heap of the k current heads gives the same time.

cards.name: Reverse Nodes In K Group
cards.trick: Use a dummy head. For each group first find its k-th node (stop if fewer than k remain), reverse the group in place, then reconnect it to the previous group's tail and the next group's head. Leave a short final group untouched.

cards.name: Valid Parentheses
cards.trick: Push opening brackets. On a closing bracket the stack top must be its matching opener (use a close -> open map). Valid only if the stack is empty at the end.

cards.name: Min Stack
cards.trick: Keep a second stack of running minimums. On push store min(val, current min), on pop remove from both. getMin is the top of the min stack.

cards.name: Evaluate Reverse Polish Notation
cards.trick: Push numbers on a stack. On an operator pop b then a, push a op b. Division must truncate toward zero, so use int(a / b).

cards.name: Daily Temperatures
cards.trick: Monotonic decreasing stack of indices. When today is warmer than the temperature at the stack top, pop it and set its answer to today - popped index.

cards.name: Car Fleet
cards.trick: Sort cars by position from closest to the target. Time to arrive = (target - position) / speed. Going from the front car backwards, a car that would arrive no later than the fleet ahead joins it. Otherwise it starts a new fleet.

cards.name: Largest Rectangle In Histogram
cards.trick: Monotonic increasing stack of (start index, height). When a bar is shorter than the top, pop and compute height * (i - start), and give the new bar the popped start. After the loop flush the stack using width n - start.

cards.name: Invert Binary Tree
cards.trick: DFS: at every node swap the left and right children, then recurse into both.

cards.name: Maximum Depth of Binary Tree
cards.space: O(h) (h = tree height, O(n) worst case)
cards.trick: DFS: depth(node) = 1 + max(depth(left), depth(right)), and a null node is 0. (BFS counting levels also works.)

cards.name: Diameter of Binary Tree
cards.trick: DFS that returns each node's height. At every node the longest path through it is leftHeight + rightHeight. Track the global max while returning 1 + max(left, right).

cards.name: Balanced Binary Tree
cards.trick: Bottom-up DFS returning the height, or a sentinel like -1 as soon as a subtree is unbalanced (|left - right| > 1). This avoids the O(n^2) cost of recomputing heights.

cards.name: Same Tree
cards.trick: Recurse on both trees together. Both null is true. One null or different values is false. Otherwise both left subtrees and both right subtrees must match.

cards.name: Subtree of Another Tree
cards.trick: For every node of root run the Same Tree check against subRoot. Treat an empty subRoot as true. (Serializing both trees and using KMP gets O(m + n).)

cards.name: Lowest Common Ancestor of a Binary Search Tree
cards.trick: Walk down from the root. If both p and q are smaller go left, if both are larger go right. Otherwise the current node splits them and is the LCA.

cards.name: Binary Tree Level Order Traversal
cards.trick: BFS with a queue. For each level process exactly len(queue) nodes, collecting their values into one list, and enqueue their children.

cards.name: Binary Tree Right Side View
cards.trick: BFS by level and keep the last node of each level. (DFS that visits right before left and records the first node seen at each depth also works.)

cards.name: Count Good Nodes In Binary Tree
cards.trick: DFS carrying the max value seen on the path from the root. A node is good if its value >= that max. Recurse into children with the updated max.

cards.name: Validate Binary Search Tree
cards.trick: DFS passing an allowed range (low, high). Each node must satisfy low < val < high. Going left sets high = val, going right sets low = val. Comparing only to direct children is wrong.

cards.name: Kth Smallest Element In a Bst
cards.trick: Inorder traversal of a BST is sorted. Do it iteratively with a stack and stop at the k-th popped node.

cards.name: Construct Binary Tree From Preorder And Inorder Traversal
cards.trick: The next preorder value is the subtree root. Its index in inorder (from a value -> index hash map) splits the left and right subtrees. Recurse building left first while moving one preorder pointer.

cards.name: Binary Tree Maximum Path Sum
cards.trick: DFS returns the best downward path starting at a node: val + max(0, left, right). At each node update the global answer with val + max(0, left) + max(0, right), the best path with this node as its top.

cards.name: Serialize And Deserialize Binary Tree
cards.trick: Preorder DFS writing values and a null marker (like N) separated by commas. To deserialize consume the tokens in the same preorder order recursively. (BFS level order also works.)

cards.name: Implement Trie Prefix Tree
cards.trick: Each node holds a children map (or 26-slot array) and an end-of-word flag. Walk one char at a time. search needs the end flag, startsWith only needs the path to exist.

cards.name: Design Add And Search Words Data Structure
cards.time: addWord O(L), search O(L) without dots, up to O(26^L) with dots
cards.trick: Trie plus DFS. On a normal char follow that child. On '.' try every child recursively and succeed if any branch matches. A match needs the end-of-word flag at the last char.

cards.name: Word Search II
cards.trick: Build a trie of all words, then DFS from every cell following trie children so many words share one search. Mark cells visited, record a word at an end node, and prune finished branches from the trie.

cards.name: Subsets
cards.trick: Decision tree: for each element choose include or exclude, and record the current list at every leaf. Or loop from a start index so each subset is built once.

cards.name: Combination Sum
cards.time: O(2^(t / m)) (t = target, m = smallest candidate)
cards.trick: DFS with a start index so you never produce reorderings. An element can be reused, so recurse with the same index after picking it. Stop when the sum hits the target or exceeds it.

cards.name: Combination Sum II
cards.trick: Sort first. Each element is used at most once. At each recursion level skip a value equal to the previous one (i > start and nums[i] == nums[i - 1]) to avoid duplicate combos. Prune when the sum exceeds the target.

cards.name: Permutations
cards.trick: Backtrack, building the list one slot at a time and tracking used elements (or swapping in place). Record the list when its length reaches n.

cards.name: Subsets II
cards.trick: Sort, then in the loop over choices skip a value equal to the previous one at the same level (i > start and nums[i] == nums[i - 1]). That removes duplicate subsets.

cards.name: Generate Parentheses
cards.trick: Backtrack on counts. Add '(' while open < n. Add ')' only while close < open. Record the string when its length is 2n.

cards.name: Word Search
cards.trick: Try every cell as a start. DFS in four directions matching the next char, mark the cell visited (for example overwrite it) and restore it when backtracking.

cards.name: Palindrome Partitioning
cards.trick: Backtrack on the cut position. For each end index j from start, if s[start..j] is a palindrome add it and recurse from j + 1. Record the partition when start reaches the end.

cards.name: Letter Combinations of a Phone Number
cards.trick: Map each digit to its letters. Recurse over the digit index, appending each letter in turn, and record the string when its length equals len(digits). Return [] for empty input.

cards.name: N Queens
cards.trick: Place one queen per row. Track used columns, the diagonal r + c and the anti-diagonal r - c in sets so a conflict check is O(1). Backtrack when a row has no safe column.

cards.name: Kth Largest Element In a Stream
cards.trick: Keep a min-heap of size k. Its top is the k-th largest. Push each new value and pop whenever the size exceeds k.

cards.name: Last Stone Weight
cards.trick: Max-heap (negate values in Python's min-heap). Pop the two heaviest, push their difference if it is non-zero, and repeat until at most one stone is left.

cards.name: K Closest Points to Origin
cards.trick: Max-heap of size k keyed on squared distance (no sqrt needed). Pop the farthest whenever the size exceeds k. (Quickselect averages O(n).)

cards.name: Kth Largest Element In An Array
cards.time: O(n log k) with a heap, O(n) average with quickselect
cards.trick: Min-heap of size k: after processing everything its top is the answer. Quickselect partitions toward index n - k for O(n) average.

cards.name: Task Scheduler
cards.trick: Math. With maxFreq and countMax (how many tasks share that frequency), answer = max(len(tasks), (maxFreq - 1) * (cooldown + 1) + countMax). (A max-heap plus cooldown queue simulation also works.)

cards.name: Design Twitter
cards.time: postTweet, follow, unfollow O(1), getNewsFeed O(f + 10 log f) (f = followees)
cards.trick: Per-user tweet list with a global increasing counter as the time. For the feed, push each followee's latest tweet into a max-heap, pop the newest, then push that user's previous tweet. Repeat up to 10 times.

cards.name: Find Median From Data Stream
cards.trick: Two heaps: a max-heap for the smaller half and a min-heap for the larger half, kept within one element of each other in size. The median is the top of the bigger heap, or the average of both tops.

cards.name: Number of Islands
cards.trick: Flood fill. Scan the grid, and for each unvisited '1' run DFS or BFS marking its whole island visited, then count one island.

cards.name: Max Area of Island
cards.trick: Same flood fill, but DFS returns the area: 1 + the area from each of the four neighbors. Track the maximum over all starts.

cards.name: Clone Graph
cards.trick: DFS or BFS with a hash map old node -> clone. Reuse the existing clone when a neighbor was already seen. Otherwise create it and recurse.

cards.name: Walls And Gates
cards.trick: Multi-source BFS. Put every gate (0) in the queue at once and expand outward. The first time a room is reached is its shortest distance. Skip walls and rooms already filled.

cards.name: Rotting Oranges
cards.trick: Multi-source BFS from every rotten orange, one BFS level per minute. Count the fresh oranges first. If any are left after the BFS return -1.

cards.name: Pacific Atlantic Water Flow
cards.trick: Reverse the flow. DFS or BFS inward from each ocean's border cells moving to neighbors with height >= current. The answer is the cells reached from both oceans.

cards.name: Surrounded Regions
cards.trick: Mark every 'O' connected to the border (DFS from the border Os) as safe. Flip all other 'O' to 'X', then restore the safe cells.

cards.name: Course Schedule
cards.trick: Cycle detection in the prerequisite graph. DFS with a 'currently visiting' set (revisiting a node on the current path means a cycle), or Kahn's topological sort and check every course was processed.

cards.name: Course Schedule II
cards.trick: Topological order via DFS postorder (then reverse) or Kahn's algorithm with in-degrees. If a cycle exists return an empty list.

cards.name: Graph Valid Tree
cards.trick: A graph is a tree iff it has exactly n - 1 edges and is connected (equivalently, no cycle). Check the edge count, then DFS or Union Find reaching all n nodes.

cards.name: Number of Connected Components In An Undirected Graph
cards.time: O(V + E * alpha(V)) with Union Find
cards.trick: Union Find. Start with n components and decrement the count each time a union joins two different roots. (DFS or BFS over the adjacency list is also O(V + E).)

cards.name: Redundant Connection
cards.trick: Union Find. Process edges in order. The first edge whose two endpoints already share a root closes a cycle and is the answer.

cards.name: Word Ladder
cards.time: O(N * L^2) (N words, L word length)
cards.trick: BFS over words. Build a map from wildcard patterns (like h*t) to words so neighbors are found fast. Each BFS level adds one to the length. Return 0 if the end word is unreachable.

cards.name: Network Delay Time
cards.trick: Dijkstra's with a min-heap from node k. The answer is the largest shortest distance. Return -1 if any node is unreachable.

cards.name: Reconstruct Itinerary
cards.trick: Eulerian path with Hierholzer's algorithm. Sort each airport's destinations, DFS consuming edges, append an airport in postorder, then reverse the result.

cards.name: Min Cost to Connect All Points
cards.time: O(n^2 log n) with a heap (O(n^2) with array Prim's)
cards.space: O(n^2) with a heap (O(n) with array Prim's)
cards.trick: Minimum spanning tree over Manhattan distances. Prim's: grow from one point, always taking the cheapest edge to an unvisited point, until all n are connected. (Kruskal with Union Find also works.)

cards.name: Swim In Rising Water
cards.trick: Dijkstra-style on the grid where a path costs the MAX elevation along it. Min-heap keyed by that max: pop the cheapest cell and push neighbors with max(current, neighbor). Stop at the bottom-right. (Binary search plus BFS also works.)

cards.name: Alien Dictionary
cards.time: O(C) (C = total characters, at most 26 nodes)
cards.trick: For each adjacent word pair the first differing chars give an edge a -> b. Topologically sort the letters (DFS postorder with cycle detection, or Kahn's). If a longer word comes before its own prefix, or there is a cycle, return an empty string.

cards.name: Cheapest Flights Within K Stops
cards.trick: Bellman-Ford limited to k + 1 edges. Run k + 1 rounds, each relaxing every flight using a COPY of the previous round's prices so a round adds only one edge.

cards.name: Climbing Stairs
cards.trick: ways(n) = ways(n - 1) + ways(n - 2), which is Fibonacci. Keep only the last two values instead of a full array.

cards.name: Min Cost Climbing Stairs
cards.trick: The cost to reach step i is cost[i] plus the cheaper of the previous two steps. You can start on step 0 or 1 and finish from either of the last two, so the answer is the min of those two.

cards.name: House Robber
cards.trick: Two running values. best at i = max(best at i - 1 (skip), best at i - 2 + nums[i] (rob)).

cards.name: House Robber II
cards.trick: The street is a circle, so the first and last houses cannot both be robbed. Run House Robber on nums[:-1] and on nums[1:] and take the max. Handle a single house as a special case.

cards.name: Longest Palindromic Substring
cards.trick: Expand around each center, both odd (one char) and even (between two chars), keeping the longest. (Manacher's algorithm is O(n).)

cards.name: Palindromic Substrings
cards.trick: Expand around each of the 2n - 1 centers and count every successful expansion.

cards.name: Decode Ways
cards.trick: dp[i] adds dp[i - 1] if the last digit is 1-9, plus dp[i - 2] if the last two digits are 10-26. A lone '0' adds nothing. Only the last two values are needed.

cards.name: Coin Change
cards.trick: dp[a] = fewest coins to make a, with dp[0] = 0 and dp[a] = 1 + min(dp[a - c]) over coins c <= a. If dp[amount] is still infinity return -1.

cards.name: Maximum Product Subarray
cards.trick: Track both the max and min product ending at each index, because a negative number can flip the min into the max. Update the best answer every step and let a zero reset both.

cards.name: Word Break
cards.time: O(n * m * L) (n = len(s), m = words, L = longest word)
cards.trick: dp[i] is true if s[:i] can be built. For each word w that ends at i, dp[i] is true if s[i - len(w):i] == w and dp[i - len(w)] is true. dp[0] = true.

cards.name: Longest Increasing Subsequence
cards.trick: Keep tails[k], the smallest tail of any increasing subsequence of length k + 1. Binary search (bisect_left) each number into tails, replacing or appending. The answer is len(tails). (The O(n^2) DP is the simpler version.)

cards.name: Partition Equal Subset Sum
cards.trick: If the total is odd return false. Otherwise 0/1 knapsack: can some subset reach total / 2? Keep a set (or boolean array) of reachable sums, updating from high to low so each number is used once.

cards.name: Unique Paths
cards.trick: dp[r][c] = dp[r - 1][c] + dp[r][c - 1]. Only the previous row is needed. (Closed form: C(m + n - 2, m - 1).)

cards.name: Longest Common Subsequence
cards.trick: dp[i][j] = dp[i - 1][j - 1] + 1 if the chars match, otherwise max(dp[i - 1][j], dp[i][j - 1]).

cards.name: Best Time to Buy And Sell Stock With Cooldown
cards.trick: State machine with three states: holding, just sold (cooldown) and resting. holding = max(holding, rest - price), sold = holding_prev + price, rest = max(rest, sold_prev).

cards.name: Coin Change II
cards.trick: Count combinations. Loop over coins in the OUTER loop and amounts inside: dp[a] += dp[a - coin], with dp[0] = 1. Coins outer avoids counting the same coins in different orders.

cards.name: Target Sum
cards.trick: DP over running sums. Keep a map from sum -> number of ways after each number, trying +num and -num. The answer is the count for the target at the end. (Equivalent to counting subsets with a fixed sum.)

cards.name: Interleaving String
cards.trick: If len(s1) + len(s2) != len(s3) return false. dp[i][j] is true if s3[:i + j] interleaves s1[:i] and s2[:j]: (dp[i - 1][j] and s1[i - 1] == s3[i + j - 1]) or (dp[i][j - 1] and s2[j - 1] == s3[i + j - 1]).

cards.name: Longest Increasing Path In a Matrix
cards.trick: DFS with memoization. The best path starting at a cell is 1 + the best from any strictly larger neighbor. Cache each cell so it is computed once. Strictly increasing means no cycles, so no visited set is needed.

cards.name: Distinct Subsequences
cards.trick: dp[i][j] = number of ways s[i:] contains t[j:] as a subsequence. Always add dp[i + 1][j] (skip s[i]). If s[i] == t[j] also add dp[i + 1][j + 1]. An empty t has exactly one way.

cards.name: Edit Distance
cards.trick: dp[i][j] = dp[i - 1][j - 1] if the chars match, else 1 + min(insert dp[i][j - 1], delete dp[i - 1][j], replace dp[i - 1][j - 1]). Base cases: dp[i][0] = i and dp[0][j] = j.

cards.name: Burst Balloons
cards.trick: Interval DP thinking about the LAST balloon k to burst in (l, r): dp[l][r] = max over k of nums[l - 1] * nums[k] * nums[r + 1] + dp[l][k - 1] + dp[k + 1][r]. Pad nums with a 1 at both ends.

cards.name: Regular Expression Matching
cards.trick: DP or memo on (i, j). If the next pattern char is '*': either skip the pair (j + 2) or, if the current chars match, consume one char of s (i + 1, j). Otherwise match one char (or '.') and advance both.

cards.name: Maximum Subarray
cards.trick: Kadane's algorithm: current = max(num, current + num) at each step and track the best. (Same idea: reset the running sum to 0 when it goes negative.)

cards.name: Jump Game
cards.trick: Work backwards with a goal starting at the last index. If i + nums[i] >= goal then goal = i. The last index is reachable iff the goal ends at 0.

cards.name: Jump Game II
cards.trick: Greedy BFS by windows. Keep the current window [l, r] and the farthest index reachable from it. When you pass r, add one jump and make the new window end at the farthest.

cards.name: Gas Station
cards.trick: If sum(gas) < sum(cost) return -1. Otherwise scan once with a running tank. When it drops below 0 the start must be after this index, so reset the tank to 0 and set start = i + 1.

cards.name: Hand of Straights
cards.trick: Return false if len(hand) is not divisible by groupSize. Count the cards, then repeatedly start a group at the smallest remaining card (min-heap or sorted keys) and take the next groupSize - 1 consecutive values, each needing a count above 0.

cards.name: Merge Triplets to Form Target Triplet
cards.trick: Ignore any triplet with a value larger than the target in any position. Among the rest, check that each of the 3 target values is matched exactly by some triplet (track three flags).

cards.name: Partition Labels
cards.trick: Record the last index of each char. Sweep while keeping the end of the current partition as the max last index seen. When i reaches that end, close the partition and record its size.

cards.name: Valid Parenthesis String
cards.trick: Track the range [lo, hi] of possible open-paren counts. '(' adds 1 to both, ')' subtracts 1 from both, '*' does lo - 1 and hi + 1. Clamp lo at 0 and fail if hi < 0. Valid if lo == 0 at the end.

cards.name: Insert Interval
cards.trick: One pass over the sorted list in three phases. Add intervals that end before the new one, merge every overlapping interval into the new one (min start, max end), then add the rest.

cards.name: Merge Intervals
cards.trick: Sort by start. If the current start <= the last merged end, extend that end with max. Otherwise append a new interval.

cards.name: Non Overlapping Intervals
cards.trick: Sort by start. When two intervals overlap, remove the one that ends later (keep the smaller end) and count a removal. This is the same as keeping the maximum number of non-overlapping intervals.

cards.name: Meeting Rooms
cards.trick: Can one person attend everything? Sort by start. If any meeting starts before the previous one ends, return false.

cards.name: Meeting Rooms II
cards.trick: Sort the start times and the end times separately and sweep with two pointers. If the next start < the next end a new room is needed, otherwise a room frees up. The answer is the max rooms in use. (A min-heap of end times also works.)

cards.name: Minimum Interval to Include Each Query
cards.time: O(n log n + q log q)
cards.trick: Sort intervals by start and process queries in ascending order. Push every interval with start <= the query into a min-heap keyed by (size, end). Pop while the top ends before the query. The top's size is the answer, or -1 if the heap is empty.

cards.name: Single Number
cards.trick: XOR everything. Equal pairs cancel and only the single number is left.

cards.name: Number of 1 Bits
cards.trick: Brian Kernighan's trick: n &= n - 1 clears the lowest set bit. Count how many times you can do that before n is 0.

cards.name: Counting Bits
cards.trick: bits[i] = bits[i >> 1] + (i & 1). The count for i is the count for i with its last bit dropped, plus that last bit.

cards.name: Reverse Bits
cards.trick: Loop 32 times. Shift the result left, add the lowest bit of n (n & 1), then shift n right.

cards.name: Missing Number
cards.trick: XOR every index 0..n with every number in the array. Pairs cancel and the missing number is left. (Sum formula n(n + 1) / 2 minus the array sum also works.)

cards.name: Sum of Two Integers
cards.trick: XOR gives the sum without carries and (a & b) << 1 gives the carries. Repeat until the carry is 0. In Python mask to 32 bits and convert back for negative results.

cards.name: Reverse Integer
cards.trick: Pop digits with modulo and push them onto the result. Check for 32-bit overflow BEFORE each push. In Python truncate toward zero for negatives.

cards.name: Rotate Image
cards.trick: Rotate in place layer by layer. For each layer cycle four cells at a time: top-left -> top-right -> bottom-right -> bottom-left. (Transpose then reverse each row also works.)

cards.name: Spiral Matrix
cards.trick: Keep four boundaries (top, bottom, left, right). Walk right, down, left, up, shrinking the matching boundary after each pass. Check the boundaries before the left and up passes so a single row or column is not repeated.

cards.name: Set Matrix Zeroes
cards.trick: Use the first row and first column as markers for which rows and columns to zero, plus one extra flag for whether the first row itself must be zeroed. (Two sets of rows and columns is the O(m + n) space version.)

cards.name: Happy Number
cards.trick: Replace n by the sum of the squares of its digits until it reaches 1 (happy) or repeats (loop). Detect the loop with a visited set, or with slow/fast pointers for O(1) space.

cards.name: Plus One
cards.space: O(1) (O(n) only when all digits are 9)
cards.trick: Walk from the last digit. If the digit is below 9, increment it and return. Otherwise set it to 0 and carry on. If every digit was 9 the result is 1 followed by zeros.

cards.name: Pow(x, n)
cards.trick: Exponentiation by squaring. If n is odd multiply the result by x, then square x and halve n. For negative n compute with |n| and invert.

cards.name: Multiply Strings
cards.trick: Grade-school multiplication. The product of digit i of num1 and digit j of num2 adds into result[i + j + 1] with the carry going into result[i + j]. Strip leading zeros and return '0' if either input is '0'.

cards.name: Detect Squares
cards.time: add O(1), count O(n) (n = distinct points)
cards.trick: Store point counts in a hash map. For a query point, treat each stored point on a diagonal (|dx| == |dy| and dx != 0) as the opposite corner and add count(diagonal) * count(x1, y2) * count(x2, y1).

cards.name: Dynamic Array
cards.time: pushback O(1) amortized, get and set O(1)
cards.trick: Resizable array. When size == capacity allocate a new array of double the capacity and copy everything over. popback just decrements the size.

cards.name: Guess Number Higher or Lower
cards.trick: Binary search 1..n and use the guess() API to pick the direction (-1 means go lower, 1 means go higher, 0 means found).

cards.name: Insertion Sort
cards.trick: For each i, shift the larger elements of the sorted prefix one step right and insert nums[i] into the gap. Record the array after each pass if the problem asks for the steps.

cards.name: Merge Sort
cards.trick: Split in half, sort each half recursively, then merge the two sorted halves with two pointers. Taking from the left half on ties keeps it stable.

cards.name: Quick Sort
cards.time: O(n log n) average, O(n^2) worst
cards.trick: Pick a pivot and partition so smaller values go left and larger go right, then recurse on both sides. A random or median-of-three pivot avoids the worst case on already sorted input.

cards.name: Remove Duplicates From Sorted Array
cards.trick: Slow pointer marks the next write position and fast pointer scans. When nums[fast] differs from nums[fast - 1] write it at slow and advance slow. Return slow as the new length.

cards.name: Subarray Sum Equals K
cards.trick: Prefix sum plus a hash map of prefix -> count. At each index add count[prefix - k] to the answer, then record the current prefix. Start with count[0] = 1.

cards.name: 132 Pattern
cards.trick: Scan right to left with a decreasing monotonic stack and a variable third = the largest value popped (the '2' of the pattern). If nums[i] < third you have found a 132 (nums[i] is the '1'). (Brute force is O(n^3).)

cards.name: 2 Keys Keyboard
cards.trick: The answer is the sum of the prime factors of n (with multiplicity), since each factor f costs one copy plus f - 1 pastes. Divide out each factor from 2 upward. (DP over divisors is O(n^2).)

cards.name: 3Sum Smaller
cards.trick: Sort, fix i, then use two pointers l and r. If nums[i] + nums[l] + nums[r] < target, every index from l+1 to r also works, so add r - l and move l up. Otherwise move r down.

cards.name: 4 Keys Keyboard
cards.trick: dp[i] = max A's with i presses. Either press A (dp[i-1] + 1) or do select-all, copy, then paste j times: dp[j] * (i - j - 1) for j from 1 to i - 3. Pasting more than about 4 times is never better than re-copying.

cards.name: 4Sum
cards.trick: Sort, fix two indices with nested loops, then run two-pointer Two Sum on the rest. Skip duplicate values at every level so quadruplets are unique. Generalizes to kSum.

cards.name: Accounts Merge
cards.time: O(N log N) (N = total emails, ignoring inverse Ackermann)
cards.trick: Union-find over account indices. Map each email to the first account that owns it and union on repeats. Then group emails by root, sort each group and prepend the name.

cards.name: Add Binary
cards.trick: Walk both strings from the right with a carry. Digit = (a + b + carry) % 2 and carry = (a + b + carry) // 2. Append a final carry and reverse the result.

cards.name: Add Bold Tag in String
cards.time: O(n * w * L) (n = len(s), w = words, L = max word length)
cards.trick: Mark every character covered by any word occurrence in a boolean array (find each occurrence with startswith). Then emit at the start of each true run and at its end, which also merges overlapping and adjacent intervals. (Aho-Corasick makes matching O(n + total length).)

cards.name: Add to Array-Form of Integer
cards.trick: Treat k as the carry. From the last digit: carry += num[i], digit = carry % 10, carry //= 10. Keep going while carry remains after the array ends, then reverse.

cards.name: Add Two Numbers II
cards.trick: Push both lists' digits onto stacks so you can add from the least significant digit. Pop, add with carry, and build the result by inserting each new node at the head. (Reversing both lists is O(1) space but mutates the input.)

cards.name: Adding Spaces to a String
cards.trick: The spaces array is sorted, so keep one pointer into s and one into spaces. Before appending s[i], if i equals spaces[j] append a space and advance j. Build with a list and join, not repeated string concatenation.

cards.name: All Paths from Source Lead to Destination
cards.trick: DFS with three states per node: unvisited, visiting, done. Hitting a visiting node means a cycle (false). A node with no outgoing edges must be the destination, and the destination must have no outgoing edges. Memoize done nodes.

cards.name: All Possible Full Binary Trees
cards.trick: If n is even return empty. Otherwise memoize build(n): the root takes 1 node and the left subtree takes an odd i, the right n - 1 - i. Combine every left tree with every right tree. Subtrees can be shared across results.

cards.name: Alternating Groups II
cards.trick: Circular array: iterate i over n + k - 1 positions using i % n. Track the current run length of alternating adjacent colors (reset to 1 when two neighbors are equal). Each time the run length is at least k, count one group.

cards.name: Amount of New Area Painted Each Day
cards.trick: Keep a next-unpainted pointer per position with path compression (union-find). For each day, jump from start through unpainted cells only, painting each one once and linking it to the next. Each cell is painted at most once overall. (Line sweep with a heap is O(n log n).)

cards.name: Analyze User Website Visit Pattern
cards.time: O(n log n + sum of v^3) (v = visits per user)
cards.trick: Sort visits by timestamp and group sites per user. For each user generate every ordered triple from their list into a set (so a user counts once per pattern). Count users per pattern and pick the max count, ties broken lexicographically.

cards.name: Android Unlock Patterns
cards.trick: DFS with a visited set and a skip[a][b] table holding the middle key that must already be visited. Use symmetry: count from key 1 times 4, from key 2 times 4, from key 5 once. Sum the counts for lengths m to n.

cards.name: Append Characters to String to Make Subsequence
cards.trick: Greedy two pointers: scan s once, advancing j in t whenever s[i] == t[j]. The longest prefix of t that is a subsequence of s is j, so append len(t) - j characters.

cards.name: Apply Operations to an Array
cards.trick: Run the operations in order in place: if nums[i] == nums[i+1], double nums[i] and zero nums[i+1]. Then move nonzero values to the front with a write pointer and fill the rest with zeros.

cards.name: Apply Operations to Maximize Score
cards.time: O(n log n + M log log M)
cards.trick: Prime score per number via a smallest-prime-factor sieve. A monotonic stack gives each index its range (left: first score >= its own, right: first score > its own), so it is the chosen element in (i - l) * (r - i) subarrays. Process values in descending order, use min(count, k) times each, and multiply with fast modular exponentiation.

cards.name: Apply Substitutions
cards.time: O(L) (L = total length of text and all replacements)
cards.trick: Store replacements in a map and resolve each key at most once with memoized recursion: scan its string, and on %k% substitute the (memoized) fully expanded value of k. Then expand the text the same way.

cards.name: Arithmetic Slices II - Subsequence
cards.trick: dp[i] is a hash map diff -> count of arithmetic subsequences (length >= 2) ending at i. For each j < i with d = a[i] - a[j]: cnt = dp[j][d]; add cnt to the answer (it extends to length >= 3) and dp[i][d] += cnt + 1.

cards.name: Armstrong Number
cards.trick: Count the digits d, then sum digit^d over every digit using % 10 and // 10. The number is Armstrong if the sum equals n.

cards.name: Arranging Coins
cards.trick: Find the largest k with k * (k + 1) / 2 <= n. Binary search k in [1, n]. (Closed form k = floor((sqrt(8n + 1) - 1) / 2) is O(1).)

cards.name: Array Transformation
cards.trick: Simulate day by day from a copy of the array: an interior element smaller than both neighbors gets +1, larger than both gets -1. Stop when a day changes nothing. Values only move toward each other so it terminates in at most about V rounds.

cards.name: Array With Elements Not Equal to Average of Neighbors
cards.trick: Make the array zigzag (strict valley, peak, valley...). One pass: at odd i swap if nums[i] < nums[i-1], at even i swap if nums[i] > nums[i-1]. Values are distinct, so a peak or valley can never equal the average of its neighbors. (Sort and interleave halves is O(n log n).)

cards.name: As Far from Land as Possible
cards.time: O(n^2) for an n x n grid
cards.trick: Multi-source BFS: push every land cell at distance 0, then expand level by level into water cells. The last water cell reached has the max distance. Return -1 if the grid is all land or all water.

cards.name: Assign Cookies
cards.time: O(g log g + s log s)
cards.trick: Sort greeds and cookie sizes. Walk the cookies once with a pointer on the least greedy unsatisfied child: if the cookie is big enough, satisfy that child and advance. Smallest sufficient cookie per child wastes nothing.

cards.name: Asteroid Collision
cards.trick: Stack of survivors. A collision only happens when the top moves right and the incoming one moves left. Pop while the top is smaller; if equal pop both, and if the top is larger the incoming one dies. Push otherwise.

cards.name: Average Height of Buildings in Each Segment
cards.trick: Sweep line over sorted events: at start add (height, count 1), at end subtract. For each gap between consecutive event positions with count > 0 emit a segment with average = sum // count. Merge with the previous segment when adjacent and equal average.

cards.name: Average Waiting Time
cards.trick: Simulate with a running clock. start = max(clock, arrival), clock = start + cook time, wait += clock - arrival. Divide the total wait by n at the end.

cards.name: Backspace String Compare
cards.trick: Walk both strings from the end. Keep a skip counter per string: '#' adds one, a normal char with skip > 0 is deleted. Compare the next real char of each. (Building both results with a stack is O(n) space.)

cards.name: Bag of Tokens
cards.trick: Sort, then two pointers. Spend power on the cheapest token for +1 score; when power is too low and score > 0, trade 1 score for the most expensive token's power. Track the maximum score seen.

cards.name: Baseball Game
cards.trick: Stack of valid scores. A number is pushed, '+' pushes the sum of the top two, 'D' pushes double the top, 'C' pops the top. Answer is the sum of the stack.

cards.name: Basic Calculator II
cards.trick: Remember the previous operator while scanning numbers. On + or - push the signed number to a running sum; on * or / combine it with the last term (truncate division toward zero). Keep only the running sum and last term, no stack needed. (Stack version is O(n) space.)

cards.name: Basic Calculator III
cards.trick: Same last-term technique as Calculator II, but on '(' recurse to evaluate the sub-expression until the matching ')' and treat its value as a number. A shared index pointer or a stack of (sum, last term, op) frames handles nesting.

cards.name: Before and After Puzzle
cards.trick: Index each phrase by its first word in a hash map. For every phrase, look up phrases whose first word equals its last word (skip itself), join them without repeating the shared word, put the results in a set and sort.

cards.name: Best Meeting Point
cards.trick: Manhattan distance separates into rows and columns, and the optimal point is the median of each. Collect row indices in order and column indices by scanning column by column (so both are already sorted), take the median of each and sum the distances.

cards.name: Best Sightseeing Pair
cards.trick: Score = (values[i] + i) + (values[j] - j) for i < j. Sweep j while tracking best = max(values[i] + i) so far; ans = max(ans, best + values[j] - j), then update best.

cards.name: Best Team With No Conflicts
cards.trick: Sort by (age, score). Then it is a max-sum non-decreasing subsequence on scores: dp[i] = score[i] + max dp[j] with score[j] <= score[i]. A Fenwick tree for prefix max over compressed scores makes it O(n log n). (Plain O(n^2) DP also works.)

cards.name: Best Time to Buy and Sell Stock II
cards.trick: Unlimited transactions, so capture every upward step: add max(0, prices[i] - prices[i-1]) for each day. That equals buying at every valley and selling at every peak.

cards.name: Binary Search Tree Iterator
cards.time: O(1) amortized per next() and hasNext()
cards.trick: Controlled inorder traversal with a stack holding the left spine. next() pops a node, then pushes the left spine of its right child. hasNext() is just a non-empty stack. (Flattening to a list costs O(n) space.)

cards.name: Binary Search Tree Iterator II
cards.trick: Lazy inorder with a stack as in Iterator I, plus a list of values already returned and a pointer into it. next() reads ahead in the list if possible, else advances the stack and appends. prev() just moves the pointer back.

cards.name: Binary Searchable Numbers in an Unsorted Array
cards.trick: A value is always found iff everything left of it is smaller and everything right of it is larger. Build prefix max and suffix min arrays (or one pass for each) and count i where prefixMax[i-1] < nums[i] < suffixMin[i+1].

cards.name: Binary Subarrays With Sum
cards.trick: Count subarrays with sum exactly goal as atMost(goal) - atMost(goal - 1), where atMost uses a standard sliding window (valid because all values are non-negative). (Prefix sum plus hash map is O(n) space.)

cards.name: Binary Tree Inorder Traversal
cards.trick: Iterative with a stack: push the whole left spine, pop and visit, then move to the right child and repeat. (Morris traversal makes it O(1) space by threading the predecessor.)

cards.name: Binary Tree Longest Consecutive Sequence
cards.trick: DFS passing the parent value and current streak length down. If node.val == parent + 1 the length is length + 1, else it resets to 1. Update a global max at every node. Only parent-to-child (downward) direction counts.

cards.name: Binary Tree Longest Consecutive Sequence II
cards.trick: Post-order DFS returning (inc, dec): longest increasing and decreasing chain starting at the node going down. Extend from a child when child.val is node.val + 1 (inc) or node.val - 1 (dec). Best path through the node is inc + dec - 1.

cards.name: Binary Tree Postorder Traversal
cards.trick: Iterative: do a modified preorder (root, then push left before right so right is visited first) into a list, then reverse it to get left, right, root. (Morris traversal is O(1) space.)

cards.name: Binary Tree Preorder Traversal
cards.trick: Iterative with a stack: pop a node, visit it, push the right child and then the left child so left is popped first. (Morris traversal is O(1) space.)

cards.name: Binary Tree Upside Down
cards.trick: Walk down the left spine. For each node: its left child becomes the new parent, so set curr.left = parent's right and curr.right = parent, carrying the old pointers in temp variables. The leftmost node is the new root. (Recursive version is O(h) space.)

cards.name: Binary Tree Vertical Order Traversal
cards.trick: BFS with a (node, column) queue: left child is col - 1, right child is col + 1. BFS keeps top-to-bottom, left-to-right order inside each column. Append to a map col -> list and track min and max col so no sorting is needed.

cards.name: Binary Tree Zigzag Level Order Traversal
cards.trick: Standard BFS by level, and reverse the level list (or appendleft into a deque) on every odd level. The traversal order of the queue itself never changes.

cards.name: Bitwise AND of Numbers Range
cards.trick: The AND of a range equals the common binary prefix of left and right, with zeros after it. Shift both right until they are equal, counting shifts, then shift back left. Or clear the lowest set bit of right (right &= right - 1) while right > left.

cards.name: Bitwise XOR of All Pairings
cards.trick: Every nums1[i] pairs with all m elements of nums2, so it appears m times and cancels out if m is even (same for nums2 with n). XOR all of nums1 only if m is odd, and XOR all of nums2 only if n is odd. Combine the two.

cards.name: Boats to Save People
cards.trick: Sort, then pointers at the lightest and heaviest person. The heaviest always takes a boat; the lightest rides along if the sum fits the limit. Move the right pointer every time and the left only when paired.

cards.name: Bomb Enemy
cards.trick: Reuse counts: recompute rowHits only at the start of a row or after a wall, and colHits[j] only at the top row or when the cell above is a wall. For each empty cell, answer = max(answer, rowHits + colHits[j]).

cards.name: Boundary of Binary Tree
cards.trick: Concatenate three parts: root, left boundary (walk down preferring left, skip leaves), all leaves left to right via DFS, then right boundary (walk down preferring right, skip leaves) reversed. Handle a root with no left child separately.

cards.name: Brace Expansion
cards.time: O(m * k^m) (m = groups, k = max options per group)
cards.trick: Parse the string into a list of groups, where a group is one letter or the sorted letters inside braces. Then DFS over groups building the word one group at a time. Sorting each group yields words in lexicographic order with no final sort.

cards.name: Brick Wall
cards.trick: Count how many rows have a brick edge at each x position using running prefix sums, excluding the final edge of each row. The best vertical line crosses the fewest bricks: rows - max edge count.

cards.name: Brightest Position on Street
cards.trick: Each lamp lights [pos - r, pos + r]. Sweep line: +1 at the start and -1 just after the end, sort the events and track running brightness. Keep the smallest position with the max brightness (update only on strictly greater).

cards.name: Build a Matrix With Conditions
cards.time: O(k + r + c) (r, c = row and column conditions)
cards.trick: Run topological sort (Kahn) separately on the row conditions and the column conditions. If either has a cycle return an empty matrix. Place each number x at (its index in the row order, its index in the column order).

cards.name: Buildings With an Ocean View
cards.trick: The ocean is on the right, so scan from right to left with a running max height. A building has a view if it is strictly taller than the max so far. Reverse the collected indices at the end. (Monotonic stack version is O(n) space.)

cards.name: Bus Routes
cards.trick: BFS over routes, not stops. Build stop -> routes map. Start from all routes containing source, count buses as BFS levels, and mark both visited routes and visited stops so each is expanded once. Return when a route contains target.

cards.name: Buy Two Chocolates
cards.trick: Cheapest pair is the two smallest prices, found in one pass keeping min1 and min2. If min1 + min2 <= money return money - that sum, otherwise return money.

cards.name: Calculate Money in Leetcode Bank
cards.trick: With w = n // 7 full weeks and d = n % 7 leftover days: total = 28w + 7 * w(w-1)/2 + d * (w + 1) + d(d-1)/2. Each full week starts 1 higher than the last. (Simulation is O(n).)

cards.name: Campus Bikes
cards.trick: Manhattan distances are bounded (at most 2000), so bucket sort all (worker, bike) pairs by distance, iterating workers then bikes inside each bucket to get the tie-breaking order for free. Assign greedily if both are still free. (Heap or sort is O(wb log wb).)

cards.name: Campus Bikes II
cards.trick: Bitmask DP over used bikes. The number of set bits in mask tells which worker is next: dp[mask | bit] = min(dp[mask] + dist(worker, bike)). Answer is the min over masks with popcount equal to the worker count. (Dijkstra on masks also works.)

cards.name: Can Place Flowers
cards.trick: Greedily plant at the first possible spot: a cell is plantable if it and both neighbors are 0 (treat out-of-bounds as 0). Plant, decrement n, and stop early when n reaches 0.

cards.name: Candy
cards.trick: Single pass over runs: up counts the length of the current increasing slope, down the decreasing slope. Total = n + the sum of triangular numbers of slopes, subtracting min(up, down) so the shared peak is counted once. (Two-pass left/right arrays is O(n) space.)

cards.name: Candy Crush
cards.trick: Repeat until stable: mark runs of 3 or more in rows and columns in place (negate values so overlaps still count), then apply gravity per column with a write pointer from the bottom and zero-fill the top. Stop when no cell was marked.

cards.name: Capacity To Ship Packages Within D Days
cards.trick: Binary search on the answer in [max(weights), sum(weights)]. For a capacity, greedily simulate loading in order and count days; if days <= D it is feasible, so try smaller. Return the smallest feasible capacity.

cards.name: Car Pooling
cards.trick: Difference array over stops: +passengers at pickup, -passengers at drop-off. Prefix sum across stops and check it never exceeds capacity. (Sorting events with a heap is O(n log n).)

cards.name: Champagne Tower
cards.trick: Simulate row by row: any glass holding more than 1 passes (amount - 1) / 2 to each of the two glasses below. Keep only the current row. Answer is min(1, glass value).

cards.name: Check Completeness of a Binary Tree
cards.trick: BFS that also enqueues null children. Once you pop the first null, every remaining item in the queue must be null; any real node after a null means the tree is not complete.

cards.name: Check If a Number Is Majority Element in a Sorted Array
cards.trick: Find the first index i of target with lower-bound binary search. If target is a majority it must also be at i + n // 2, so return i + n // 2 < n and nums[i + n // 2] == target.

cards.name: Check if a Parentheses String Can Be Valid
cards.trick: Odd length is impossible. Scan left to right treating unlocked cells as '(' wildcards: a balance below zero means too many ')'. Then scan right to left treating unlocked cells as ')' wildcards with the same check. Both passes must succeed.

cards.name: Check If a String Contains All Binary Codes of Size K
cards.trick: Roll a k-bit integer window over the string (shift left, add the new bit, mask with 2^k - 1) and add each value to a set once the window is full. Return true when the set reaches 2^k distinct codes. Early exit if n - k + 1 < 2^k.

cards.name: Check If a String Is a Valid Sequence from Root to Leaves Path in a Binary Tree
cards.trick: DFS carrying an index into arr. Fail if the node is null, the index is out of range or the values differ. When the index is the last one, the node must also be a leaf.

cards.name: Check if an Array Is Consecutive
cards.trick: One pass for min and max plus a set of the values. The array is consecutive iff the set has n distinct values and max - min + 1 == n.

cards.name: Check if Array Is Sorted and Rotated
cards.trick: Count the positions where nums[i] > nums[(i + 1) % n] (wrapping around). A sorted array rotated by any amount has at most one such descent, so return count <= 1.

cards.name: Check if Grid Can Be Cut Into Sections
cards.trick: Project the rectangles onto the x axis and onto the y axis and merge overlapping intervals on each. If either axis has at least 3 disjoint merged groups, two cuts can split the grid into three sections.

cards.name: Check if Move Is Legal
cards.time: O(1) (8 directions on a fixed 8x8 board)
cards.trick: From (r, c), try each of the 8 directions. Walk while cells are the opposite color, counting them; the line is legal if you then hit your own color and walked at least one opposite cell (total length of at least 3). Stop at the board edge or an empty cell.

cards.name: Check if Number Is a Sum of Powers of Three
cards.trick: Each power of three can be used once, so n must have only digits 0 and 1 in base 3. Repeatedly take n % 3: if it is 2 return false, else divide by 3.

cards.name: Check if One String Swap Can Make Strings Equal
cards.trick: Collect the indices where the strings differ. Zero differences is true. Exactly two differences i and j is true only if s1[i] == s2[j] and s1[j] == s2[i]. Any other count is false.

cards.name: Check if String Is Decomposable Into Value-Equal Substrings
cards.trick: Split into runs of equal characters. Each run must split into 3s plus at most one 2, so run length % 3 must be 0 or 2. Exactly one piece of length 2 is allowed in the whole string, so exactly one run with length % 3 == 2.

cards.name: Check if There is a Valid Partition For The Array
cards.trick: dp[i] = the first i elements can be partitioned. Transitions: last 2 equal (dp[i-2]), last 3 equal (dp[i-3]), last 3 consecutive increasing (dp[i-3]). Only the last three dp values are needed. dp[0] = true. (Full array is O(n) space.)

cards.name: Check if Two Expression Trees are Equivalent
cards.trick: Only '+' appears, so the expression is a sum of variables and order is irrelevant. DFS each tree counting occurrences of every variable in a 26-slot array (+1 for tree 1, -1 for tree 2) and check all counts end at zero.

cards.name: Check If Two String Arrays are Equivalent
cards.trick: Use a (word index, char index) pointer for each array and compare one character at a time, advancing to the next word when a word ends. No need to join the strings. Both must finish together.

cards.name: Cherry Pickup
cards.trick: Treat the trip back as a second path going forward from (0, 0) at the same time. Both walkers are on step t, so positions are (r1, t - r1) and (r2, t - r2): dp[t][r1][r2], rolled over t. Count a shared cell once, use -inf for thorns, try the 4 move combinations, and answer is max(0, dp[end]).

cards.name: Cherry Pickup II
cards.trick: Move both robots down row by row. State is (col1, col2) in the current row; each robot has 3 moves, giving 9 transitions. Add grid[r][c1] and grid[r][c2] (only once if c1 == c2). Roll the dp over rows or run it bottom-up.

cards.name: Choose Numbers From Two Arrays in Range
cards.time: O(n * S) (S = sum range of nums1 and nums2)
cards.trick: Track the signed difference (sum from nums1 minus sum from nums2). For each end index keep a map diff -> count of choice sequences ending there: pick nums1[i] (+) or nums2[i] (-) from each earlier state, plus start a new range at i. Add the count at diff 0 to the answer, modulo 1e9 + 7.

cards.name: Circular Sentence
cards.trick: For every space at index i require s[i-1] == s[i+1] (last char of a word equals first char of the next). Then also require s[0] == s[-1] for the wraparound.

cards.name: Clear Digits
cards.trick: Stack of characters. Push letters; on a digit pop the most recent letter (the closest non-digit to its left). Join the stack. (Write pointer in place works the same way.)

cards.name: Clone N-ary Tree
cards.trick: Recursive DFS: if the node is null return null, create a new node with the same value, and set its children to the clones of each original child. No map needed since it is a tree, not a graph.

cards.name: Closest Binary Search Tree Value
cards.trick: Walk down from the root like a BST search. At each node update closest if |val - target| is smaller (ties go to the smaller value), then go left if target < val else right.

cards.name: Closest Binary Search Tree Value II
cards.trick: Build two stacks of the path: predecessors (values <= target) and successors (values > target). Then k times, pop the closer of the two tops and advance that stack to its next predecessor or successor, like merging two sorted lists. (Inorder plus sliding window or heap is O(n).)

cards.name: Closest Leaf in a Binary Tree
cards.trick: DFS to record parent pointers (or build an undirected adjacency map) and find the node with value k. Then BFS outward from it and return the first leaf reached.

cards.name: Closest Node to Path in Tree
cards.trick: The node on the path start-end closest to node is the median of the three points: take the deepest of lca(start, end), lca(start, node) and lca(end, node). Use binary lifting for O(log n) LCA. (BFS per query is O(n * q).)

cards.name: Closest Prime Numbers in Range
cards.trick: Sieve of Eratosthenes up to right, then scan the primes in [left, right] keeping the smallest gap between consecutive primes (first pair wins ties). Early exit when the gap is 1 (2 and 3) or 2.

cards.name: Coin Path
cards.trick: Go backward: dp[i] = cost[i] + min dp[j] for j in i+1..i+B, with cost -1 blocked. Iterate j ascending and update only on strictly smaller cost, so the stored next index is the smallest among ties. Then follow next pointers from index 1 for the lexicographically smallest path.

cards.name: Combination Sum IV
cards.trick: Counts ordered sequences, so loop over the target in the outer loop and numbers in the inner loop: dp[t] = sum of dp[t - num] for each num <= t, with dp[0] = 1. (Swapping the loops would count combinations instead.)

cards.name: Combinations
cards.trick: Backtrack with a start index so each combination is built in increasing order. Add i, recurse with i + 1, pop. Prune the loop to i <= n - (k - len(path)) + 1 since remaining numbers must still fill k slots.

cards.name: Concatenated Words
cards.time: O(N * L^2) (N words, L max length)
cards.trick: Word Break per word using the other words (a trie, or a hash set of shorter words, processing by length). A word qualifies if dp[len] is reachable using at least two pieces, so exclude the word itself and skip empty strings.

cards.name: Concatenation of Array
cards.trick: Allocate ans of length 2n and set ans[i] = ans[i + n] = nums[i] in one pass.

cards.name: Confusing Number
cards.time: O(log n) (n = the number, so O(d) for d digits)
cards.trick: Map each digit with 0->0, 1->1, 6->9, 8->8, 9->6. Any other digit means false. Build the rotated number by peeling digits off the right and appending the mapped digit, then check rotated != original.

cards.name: Confusing Number II
cards.time: O(5^L) (L = number of digits in n)
cards.trick: DFS that builds numbers only from digits {0,1,6,8,9}, never starting with 0 and stopping once the value exceeds n. Track the rotated value incrementally as rotated + map[d] * 10^len, and count when rotated != number.

cards.name: Connecting Cities With Minimum Cost
cards.trick: Minimum spanning tree. Kruskal: sort edges by cost and union-find merge, adding the cost on each successful union. If fewer than n - 1 edges were used the graph is disconnected, so return -1. (Prim with a heap is O(E log V).)

cards.name: Constrained Subsequence Sum
cards.trick: dp[i] = nums[i] + max(0, max of dp over the last k indices). Keep a monotonic decreasing deque of dp values for the window max, popping the front when it is older than k. Answer is max dp[i]. (Max-heap with lazy deletion is O(n log n).)

cards.name: Construct Binary Tree from Inorder and Postorder Traversal
cards.trick: Last postorder element is the root. Hash map of value -> inorder index finds the split in O(1). Walk postorder from the end and build the RIGHT subtree before the left one. (Slicing arrays or linear index search is O(n^2).)

cards.name: Construct Binary Tree from Preorder and Postorder Traversal
cards.trick: preorder[0] is the root and preorder[1] is the left child root. Find that value in postorder via a hash map; its index + 1 is the left subtree size. Recurse on index ranges. Result is not unique when a node has one child, any valid tree is accepted.

cards.name: Construct Binary Tree from String
cards.space: O(n) (O(h) of recursion plus the tree)
cards.trick: Recursive parse with a shared index. Read an optional minus sign and digits for the node value, then if the next char is '(' parse the left child, and if '(' again parse the right child. Each parse consumes its closing ')'.

cards.name: Construct K Palindrome Strings
cards.trick: Return false if k > len(s). Each palindrome can hold at most one odd-count character, so need (number of letters with odd frequency) <= k. Any extra characters can be split among k palindromes.

cards.name: Construct Quad Tree
cards.space: O(log n) (recursion, excluding the output tree)
cards.trick: Divide and conquer into four quadrants. Build the four children first, and if all are leaves with the same value, collapse into one leaf. Otherwise make an internal node. (Checking uniformity by scanning each region is O(n^2 log n).)

cards.name: Construct Smallest Number From DI String
cards.trick: Iterate i from 0 to n pushing digit i + 1 on a stack. Whenever the pattern char is 'I' or you reach the end, pop everything and append to the result. A run of D's gets reversed by the stack, giving the smallest lexicographic answer.

cards.name: Construct String from Binary Tree
cards.trick: Preorder DFS. Wrap left and right subtree strings in parentheses. Omit the parentheses for an empty right child, but if the left is empty and the right exists you must still emit '()' for the left.

cards.name: Construct String With Repeat Limit
cards.trick: Greedy with a max heap of (char, count). Take the largest char up to repeatLimit times. If it still has leftovers, take ONE of the next largest char as a separator, then push the leftovers back. If no separator exists, stop.

cards.name: Construct the Lexicographically Largest Valid Sequence
cards.time: O(n!) worst case (prunes heavily, finishes fast in practice)
cards.trick: Sequence length is 2n - 1. Fill positions left to right, trying numbers from n down to 1. Place i at pos and pos + i (for i > 1), mark used, recurse, undo on failure. The first complete fill is the lexicographically largest.

cards.name: Contains Duplicate II
cards.trick: Sliding window set of the last k elements. For each i check if nums[i] is already in the set, add it, and drop nums[i - k] once the window exceeds k. (A hash map of value -> last index also works.)

cards.name: Contiguous Array
cards.trick: Treat 0 as -1 and keep a running sum. Equal prefix sums mean a balanced subarray between them, so store the FIRST index of each sum in a map (seed sum 0 at index -1) and maximize i - first[sum].

cards.name: Continuous Subarray Sum
cards.trick: Prefix sum mod k. If the same remainder appears at two indices at least 2 apart, the subarray between sums to a multiple of k. Store only the first index of each remainder, seeded with {0: -1}. The 2-apart rule is what enforces length >= 2.

cards.name: Convert 1D Array Into 2D Array
cards.trick: If len(original) != m * n return an empty array. Otherwise row i is the slice original[i * n : (i + 1) * n].

cards.name: Convert an Array Into a 2D Array With Conditions
cards.trick: Rows are distinct values, so the k-th occurrence of a number goes into row k. Keep a count map, and for each num put it into row count[num] (creating the row if needed), then increment. Row count equals the max frequency.

cards.name: Convert Binary Search Tree to Sorted Doubly Linked List
cards.trick: In-order traversal with a prev pointer: link prev.right = node and node.left = prev, remember the first node as head. After the traversal link tail and head to make it circular. (Morris traversal gets O(1) space.)

cards.name: Convert BST to Greater Tree
cards.trick: Reverse in-order (right, node, left) visits values from largest to smallest. Keep a running sum, add it to node.val, and update the sum. (Morris reverse traversal is O(1) space.)

cards.name: Convert Sorted Array to Binary Search Tree
cards.space: O(log n) (recursion, excluding the output tree)
cards.trick: Pick the middle element as root and recurse on the left and right halves by index range. Choosing the middle keeps the tree height balanced at O(log n).

cards.name: Convex Polygon
cards.trick: For every consecutive triple of points (wrapping around) compute the cross product of the two edge vectors. The polygon is convex iff all non-zero cross products share the same sign. Track the first non-zero sign and fail on any mismatch.

cards.name: Count All Valid Pickup and Delivery Options
cards.trick: Insert orders one at a time. With 2(i - 1) slots already used, order i's pickup/delivery pair can go in (2i)(2i - 1) / 2 = i * (2i - 1) ways. Answer = product of i * (2i - 1) for i in 1..n, mod 1e9 + 7.

cards.name: Count Days Without Meetings
cards.time: O(m log m) (m = number of meetings)
cards.trick: Sort meetings by start and sweep, tracking the furthest end seen. Free days = gap before each meeting starts beyond the current end, plus the days after the last end up to total days.

cards.name: Count Nodes Equal to Sum of Descendants
cards.trick: Post-order DFS returning the subtree sum. Left sum + right sum is the sum of descendants, so if it equals node.val increment the count. Return node.val + left + right.

cards.name: Count Number of Bad Pairs
cards.trick: j - i == nums[j] - nums[i] is the same as nums[i] - i == nums[j] - j. Count GOOD pairs with a hash map of nums[i] - i, then bad = n(n - 1) / 2 - good.

cards.name: Count Number of Maximum Bitwise-OR Subsets
cards.trick: The maximum OR is the OR of the whole array. DFS include/exclude each element carrying the running OR, and count the leaves whose OR equals that max.

cards.name: Count Number of Nice Subarrays
cards.trick: Exactly k odds = atMost(k) - atMost(k - 1). atMost uses a sliding window over the odd count and adds the window length at each right end. (Prefix count of odds with a hash map is O(n) space.)

cards.name: Count Number of Teams
cards.time: O(n log n) with a Fenwick tree (O(n^2) with simple counting)
cards.trick: Fix the middle soldier j. Teams through j = (smaller on left) * (larger on right) + (larger on left) * (smaller on right). Get the left counts with a BIT over ranks, the right counts as total minus left minus equal. The simple version just counts them with two loops.

cards.name: Count Odd Numbers in an Interval Range
cards.trick: Count of odds in [1, x] is (x + 1) // 2. Answer = (high + 1) // 2 - low // 2.

cards.name: Count of Matches in Tournament
cards.trick: Every match eliminates exactly one team and one team remains, so there are n - 1 matches. (Simulating the rounds is O(log n).)

cards.name: Count of Substrings Containing Every Vowel and K Consonants II
cards.trick: Exactly k consonants = atLeast(k) - atLeast(k + 1). atLeast(k) is a sliding window with a vowel count map and a consonant count, counting windows that contain all 5 vowels and at least k consonants. Add (left index) valid starts at each right end.

cards.name: Count Pairs in Two Arrays
cards.trick: nums1[i] + nums1[j] > nums2[i] + nums2[j] is diff[i] + diff[j] > 0 with diff = nums1 - nums2. Sort diff, then two pointers: if diff[l] + diff[r] > 0 every index from l to r - 1 pairs with r, so add r - l and move r.

cards.name: Count Pairs of Equal Substrings With Minimum Difference
cards.trick: Single characters are enough: minimizing j - a means the end j in the first string should be as early as possible and the start a in the second as late as possible. For each letter compute first1[c] - last2[c], take the min across letters, and count the letters that hit it.

cards.name: Count Positions on Street With Required Brightness
cards.trick: Difference array: for each lamp add +1 at max(0, pos - range) and -1 at min(n - 1, pos + range) + 1. Prefix sum gives each position's brightness, then count positions with brightness >= requirement[i].

cards.name: Count Prefix and Suffix Pairs I
cards.time: O(total characters) (brute force with startswith/endswith is O(n^2 * L))
cards.trick: Trie keyed by character PAIRS (word[k], word[len - 1 - k]). A word that is both prefix and suffix of a longer word is a path of such pairs. Process words in order: sum the end-counts of every node on the word's path (earlier words that are both prefix and suffix), then increment the end-count at its final node. Small constraints let brute force pass too.

cards.name: Count Prefix and Suffix Pairs II
cards.trick: Trie where each step uses the pair (word[k], word[len - 1 - k]). Process words in order: walk the trie and add the end-count stored at every node on the path (earlier words that are both prefix and suffix of it), then increment the end-count at the final node. The n^2 brute force times out.

cards.name: Count Primes
cards.trick: Sieve of Eratosthenes over numbers below n. For each prime p up to sqrt(n), mark multiples starting at p * p as composite. Count the unmarked numbers from 2.

cards.name: Count Servers That Communicate
cards.trick: Count servers per row and per column. A server communicates if its row count > 1 or its column count > 1. No graph traversal needed.

cards.name: Count Square Submatrices with All Ones
cards.space: O(1) (in place) or O(n) rolling row
cards.trick: dp[i][j] = 1 + min(up, left, up-left) for a 1 cell, 0 otherwise. dp[i][j] is the side of the largest all-ones square ending there, which is also the number of squares ending there. Sum all dp values.

cards.name: Count Strictly Increasing Subarrays
cards.trick: Track the length of the current strictly increasing run. If nums[i] > nums[i - 1] increment it, else reset to 1. Each index adds run length new subarrays ending there. Total = sum of run lengths.

cards.name: Count Sub Islands
cards.trick: DFS each island of grid2 and flood-fill it. It is a sub-island only if every cell is also land in grid1, so keep a flag that goes false when a visited cell is water in grid1. Still visit the whole island before deciding.

cards.name: Count Subarrays Where Max Element Appears at Least K Times
cards.trick: Let M be the global max. Slide the window and count M's. Once count of M reaches k, every start from the left edge up to the leftmost position that still keeps k copies works, so add that many for each right end. Shrink left while the count stays >= k.

cards.name: Count Subarrays With More Ones Than Zeros
cards.trick: Map 0 to -1 and 1 to +1, then count pairs of prefix sums with later > earlier. Since the prefix moves by exactly +-1, maintain count[sum] and a running 'number of earlier prefixes below the current sum' that adjusts in O(1) per step. Mod 1e9 + 7. (BIT or merge sort is O(n log n).)

cards.name: Count Substrings with Only One Distinct Letter
cards.trick: Walk runs of equal characters. A run of length L contributes L * (L + 1) / 2 substrings, or equivalently add the current run length at every index.

cards.name: Count the Number of Complete Components
cards.trick: Find connected components (DFS or union-find). A component with v vertices is complete iff it has exactly v * (v - 1) / 2 edges. Count vertices and edges per component (or check every vertex degree == v - 1).

cards.name: Count the Number of Consistent Strings
cards.trick: Put allowed in a set or a 26-bit mask. A word is consistent if every one of its characters is allowed.

cards.name: Count the Number of Fair Pairs
cards.trick: Order does not matter for pair sums, so sort. Answer = pairsWithSum <= upper minus pairsWithSum <= lower - 1. Count each with two pointers from both ends (if nums[l] + nums[r] <= x add r - l and move l, else move r).

cards.name: Count Total Number of Colored Cells
cards.trick: Each minute adds a ring of 4 * (t - 1) cells, so the total is 1 + 4 * (1 + 2 + ... + (n - 1)) = 1 + 2n(n - 1), equivalently n^2 + (n - 1)^2.

cards.name: Count Triplets That Can Form Two Arrays of Equal XOR
cards.trick: a == b means xor of arr[i..k] is 0, so prefix[i] == prefix[k + 1], and any split point j works (k - i choices). Walk prefixes with a hash map storing count and sum of indices per prefix value, adding count * (idx - 1) - sumIdx for each match. (Brute force over pairs is O(n^2).)

cards.name: Count Triplets With Even XOR Set Bits I
cards.trick: popcount(a ^ b ^ c) parity equals parity(a) xor parity(b) xor parity(c). Count even-parity and odd-parity numbers in each array, then sum the products over parity combos whose xor is 0. (Triple loop is O(n^3).)

cards.name: Count Unguarded Cells in the Grid
cards.trick: Mark guards and walls, then do four directional sweeps (left-to-right, right-to-left, top-down, bottom-up) with a 'guarding' flag per row or column. The flag turns on at a guard, off at a wall, and marks every empty cell it crosses as guarded. Count the cells left unmarked.

cards.name: Count Univalue Subtrees
cards.trick: Post-order DFS returning whether the subtree is univalue. A node is univalue if both children are univalue (or null) and each non-null child has the same value as the node. Count each time it is true.

cards.name: Count Vowel Strings in Ranges
cards.trick: Prefix sum over words where the word starts and ends with a vowel. Each query [l, r] is prefix[r + 1] - prefix[l].

cards.name: Count Vowels Permutation
cards.trick: Track the count of valid strings ending in each of the 5 vowels and roll it forward using the allowed-follower rules (a->e, e->a/i, i->not i, o->i/u, u->a). Sum the five counts mod 1e9 + 7. (5x5 matrix exponentiation is O(log n).)

cards.name: Count Ways to Build Good Strings
cards.trick: dp[len] = dp[len - zero] + dp[len - one], with dp[0] = 1. Answer is the sum of dp[len] for len in [low, high], mod 1e9 + 7.

cards.name: Count Ways to Distribute Candies
cards.trick: Stirling numbers of the second kind: dp[i][j] = dp[i - 1][j - 1] + j * dp[i - 1][j]. Candy i either starts a new bag or joins any of the j existing bags. Roll the table to one row, mod 1e9 + 7.

cards.name: Counting Elements
cards.trick: Put all values in a set. Count every element x (duplicates included) where x + 1 is in the set.

cards.name: Counting Words With a Given Prefix
cards.time: O(n * m) (n words, m = prefix length)
cards.trick: Count the words where word.startswith(pref). A trie is not needed for a single prefix.

cards.name: Course Schedule IV
cards.trick: Precompute the transitive closure of the prerequisite graph. Run a DFS/BFS from every course (or a topological sort merging prerequisite sets, or Floyd-Warshall at O(n^3)) into a reachable[a][b] table, then answer each query in O(1).

cards.name: Cousins in Binary Tree II
cards.trick: BFS by level. For each node, its children's new value is (sum of the whole next level) - (sum of its own two children). The root becomes 0. Compute the next-level sum before assigning.

cards.name: Crawler Log Folder
cards.trick: Only the depth matters. '../' decrements depth but not below 0, './' does nothing, any other folder increments depth. Return the final depth (a real stack is not needed).

cards.name: Create Binary Tree From Descriptions
cards.trick: Hash map of value -> node, creating nodes lazily, and link parent.left or parent.right by the isLeft flag. The root is the one node that never appears as a child, so keep a set of children.

cards.name: Custom Sort String
cards.trick: Count the letters of s. Output each char of order repeated by its count (zeroing it), then append all remaining letters in any order. (Sorting with an order-index key is O(n log n).)

cards.name: Cutting Ribbons
cards.trick: Binary search on the answer length L in [1, max]. Pieces of length L = sum(r // L), feasible if >= k. Find the largest feasible L, or return 0 if even L = 1 fails.

cards.name: Data Stream as Disjoint Intervals
cards.time: O(log n) per addNum with a sorted map, O(n) per getIntervals
cards.trick: Keep disjoint intervals in a sorted structure (TreeMap, or a sorted list with bisect). On addNum find the neighbors by binary search and merge if val is adjacent to or inside them. (Python list insert makes addNum O(n).)

cards.name: Decode String
