cards.trick: Stack of (previous string, repeat count). On a digit build the number, on '[' push the current string and count and reset, on ']' pop and set current = prev + current * count.

cards.name: Defuse the Bomb
cards.trick: Circular sliding window of size |k|. For k > 0 the window starts at i + 1, for k < 0 it starts at i - |k|, k == 0 gives all zeros. Compute the first window sum, then slide by adding the incoming and removing the outgoing index modulo n.

cards.name: Delete and Earn
cards.trick: Reduce to House Robber. points[v] = v * count(v), and taking v forbids v - 1 and v + 1, so dp[v] = max(dp[v - 1], dp[v - 2] + points[v]). Only sorted distinct values matter if M is huge.

cards.name: Delete Leaves With a Given Value
cards.trick: Post-order DFS: fix the children first, then return null if the node is now a leaf with val == target. Post-order handles parents that become leaves after deletion.

cards.name: Delete N Nodes After M Nodes of a Linked List
cards.trick: Loop: advance m - 1 nodes to the last node to keep, then skip n nodes by pointing its next past them, and continue from there. Stop if the list ends early.

cards.name: Delete Node in a BST
cards.trick: Search for the key. A node with at most one child is replaced by that child. With two children copy the in-order successor (min of the right subtree) into the node and delete that successor from the right subtree.

cards.name: Delete Nodes And Return Forest
cards.trick: Post-order DFS with to_delete in a set. If a node is deleted, add its non-null children to the result and return null to its parent. After the DFS add the root if it was not deleted.

cards.name: Delete Nodes From Linked List Present in Array
cards.trick: Put nums in a set, then walk the list with a dummy head and skip any node whose value is in the set by relinking prev.next. Return dummy.next.

cards.name: Delete Tree Nodes
cards.trick: Build children lists from the parent array, then post-order DFS returning (subtree sum, node count). If a subtree sum is 0 its node count becomes 0 (the whole subtree is removed). Answer is the root's count.

cards.name: Depth of BST Given Insertion Order
cards.time: O(n) (O(n log n) with a sorted set)
cards.trick: A new value attaches under its inserted predecessor or successor, whichever is deeper, so depth = 1 + max(depth[pred], depth[succ]). With a permutation of 1..n, do it in O(n): delete values from a doubly linked list in reverse insertion order to get each one's neighbors at insertion time.

cards.name: Design a File Sharing System
cards.time: O(m log n) join (m = chunks owned), O(m) leave, O(k log k) request (k = owners of the chunk)
cards.trick: Min-heap of freed user IDs plus a counter for the next new ID, so join always returns the smallest unused ID. Map chunk -> set of owner IDs. Request returns the sorted owners, then adds the requester to the chunk's set.

cards.name: Design a Food Rating System
cards.time: O(log n) per changeRating and highestRated (amortized), O(n log n) to build
cards.trick: Per-cuisine max heap of (-rating, name) plus maps food -> rating and food -> cuisine. changeRating updates the map and pushes a NEW entry (lazy deletion). highestRated pops heap tops whose rating no longer matches the map. (A sorted set with real removal also works.)

cards.name: Design a Leaderboard
cards.time: O(1) addScore and reset, O(n log K) top(K)
cards.trick: Hash map playerId -> score. addScore adds to the map, reset sets that score to 0 (or deletes it). top(K) takes the K largest scores with a size-K min heap (or heapq.nlargest). Sorting everything is O(n log n).

cards.name: Design a Todo List
cards.time: O(n) addTask with bisect.insort (O(log n) with a tree), O(k) per get (k = matching tasks)
cards.trick: Global taskId counter. Per user keep tasks sorted by due date (insort), and per user and tag keep a sorted list of the same task objects. Mark complete via a flag or removal so getAllTasks and getTasksForTag just filter and return in order.

cards.name: Design Browser History
cards.trick: Array of URLs with a cur pointer and a separate size. visit writes at cur + 1 and sets size = cur + 1, which truncates forward history for free. back and forward just clamp cur. (Two stacks or a doubly linked list works too.)

cards.name: Design Circular Queue
cards.trick: Fixed array with a head index and a size. enQueue writes at (head + size) % k, deQueue advances head = (head + 1) % k. Track size instead of tail so full and empty are unambiguous.

cards.name: Design Compressed String Iterator
cards.time: O(1) amortized per next and hasNext
cards.trick: Parse lazily. Keep a pointer into the compressed string, the current char and its remaining count. next returns the char and decrements, loading the next letter-and-number group when the count hits 0. hasNext is count > 0 or more groups remain. (Pre-expanding can blow up memory.)

cards.name: Design Excel Sum Formula
cards.time: O(R * C) set and sum (propagate in topological order), O(1) get
cards.trick: Each cell holds a value or a sum formula (a map of cell -> count of references). Cells form a dependency graph, so on set or sum recompute the changed cell and propagate to dependents in topological order. A simpler version recomputes recursively on get but is slower.

cards.name: Design File System
cards.trick: Hash map path -> value. createPath fails if the path already exists or its parent path (everything before the last '/') is not in the map, except when the parent is the root. get is a plain lookup. (A trie of path segments also works.)

cards.name: Design HashMap
cards.time: O(1) average per operation (O(n / buckets) worst case)
cards.trick: Array of buckets (a prime like 769 or 1009) with separate chaining. hash = key % size, then scan the bucket for the key on put, get and remove. Resize when the load factor gets high to keep chains short.

cards.name: Design HashSet
cards.time: O(1) average per operation (O(n / buckets) worst case)
cards.trick: Array of buckets with separate chaining. hash = key % size, then scan the bucket on add, contains and remove, skipping duplicates on add. (With keys <= 1e6 a boolean array is O(1) worst case.)

cards.name: Design Hit Counter
cards.trick: Circular buffers of size 300 for timestamps and counts. hit(t) uses slot t % 300, resetting it if the stored timestamp differs. getHits sums slots whose timestamp is within the last 300 seconds. (A deque of timestamps works but grows with traffic.)

cards.name: Design In-Memory File System
cards.time: O(L) per path operation (L = path length), plus O(k log k) for ls on k entries
cards.trick: Trie of path segments where each node holds a children map and file content (None for a directory). Split on '/', walk or create nodes. ls on a file returns just its name, on a directory returns the sorted child names.

cards.name: Design Linked List
cards.time: O(1) addAtHead, O(n) get and index operations
cards.trick: Singly linked list with a dummy head and a size counter. To insert or delete at index i walk to the node just before it, and always bounds-check against size (index == size is valid for insert only). A tail pointer makes addAtTail O(1).

cards.name: Design Log Storage System
cards.time: O(1) put, O(n) retrieve (O(log n + k) with a sorted structure)
cards.trick: Timestamps are fixed-width strings, so truncate each to the granularity prefix length (Year=4, Month=7, Day=10, Hour=13, Minute=16, Second=19) and compare lexicographically with the truncated start and end.

cards.name: Design Most Recently Used Queue
cards.trick: Fenwick tree over n + q slots marking which slots are occupied. fetch(k) finds the k-th occupied slot by BIT descent, clears it and appends the value in a fresh slot at the end. (Sqrt decomposition is O(sqrt n), the plain list is O(n).)

cards.name: Design Parking System
cards.trick: Store the remaining slot count per car type (3 sizes). addCar decrements and returns true if the count was above 0.

cards.name: Design Phone Directory
cards.trick: Queue (or stack) of free numbers plus a boolean array of what is taken. get pops a free number and marks it used, release re-queues it only if it was in use, check reads the boolean.

cards.name: Design Search Autocomplete System
cards.time: O(p + m log m) per input char (p = prefix length, m = sentences under the prefix)
cards.trick: Trie of sentences with a hit count at the end node. Keep a pointer to the current node as chars are typed. On each char collect all sentences below the node and return the top 3 by (-count, sentence). On '#' insert the typed sentence (count + 1) and reset.

cards.name: Design Snake Game
cards.trick: Deque of body cells for the snake plus a set for O(1) collision checks. On each move pop the tail from the set FIRST (it moves away), then check wall or self collision, then push the new head. If food is eaten keep the tail instead and increment the score.

cards.name: Design SQL
cards.time: O(1) deleteRow and selectCell, O(c) insertRow (c = columns)
cards.trick: Per table keep a row map rowId -> row (a dict or list) and a next-id counter starting at 1. insertRow assigns the next id, deleteRow removes the id, selectCell is a direct lookup. Ids are never reused after deletion.

cards.name: Design Tic-Tac-Toe
cards.trick: Keep counters per row, per column, and for both diagonals. Player 1 adds +1 and player 2 adds -1. A player wins the moment any counter reaches +-n. (A full board scan per move is O(n).)

cards.name: Design Underground System
cards.space: O(n + S^2) (n = riders in transit, S = stations)
cards.trick: Two maps. checkIn: id -> (station, time). totals: (startStation, endStation) -> (total time, trip count). On checkOut remove the check-in entry and update the totals. getAverageTime is total / count.

cards.name: Design Video Sharing Platform
cards.time: O(log n) upload and remove, O(1) like, dislike, views, O(len) watch
cards.trick: Min-heap of freed video IDs: upload takes the smallest freed ID, otherwise the next new ID. Maps store id -> video string, views, likes and dislikes. watch returns the slice video[start : min(end, len - 1) + 1] and increments views. Removing pushes the ID back on the heap.

cards.name: Destination City
cards.trick: Put every starting city in a set. The destination is the end city that is not in that set (it has no outgoing path).

cards.name: Detonate the Maximum Bombs
cards.trick: Directed graph: edge i -> j if dist(i, j)^2 <= r_i^2 (compare squared integers, no sqrt). Edges are not symmetric because radii differ. Run a DFS/BFS from every bomb and take the max reachable count.

cards.name: Diameter of N-Ary Tree
cards.trick: DFS returning the height of each subtree. At each node the longest path through it is the sum of its two largest child heights (height + 1 per edge). Track the global max of that sum.

cards.name: Diet Plan Performance
cards.trick: Fixed window of size k: compute the first window sum, then slide by adding calories[i] and removing calories[i - k]. Add 1 point if the sum is above upper, subtract 1 if it is below lower.

cards.name: Different Ways to Add Parentheses
cards.trick: Divide and conquer on each operator. Split the expression at every operator, recursively compute all results of the left and right parts, then combine every pair with that operator. Memoize by substring. A bare number is the base case.

cards.name: Digit Count in Range
cards.trick: Answer = count(high) - count(low - 1), where count(n) is how many times digit d appears in 1..n. For each position p, split n into high, cur and low parts and add the contribution by cases (cur < d, cur == d, cur > d). Handle d = 0 separately so leading zeros are not counted.

cards.name: Distance to a Cycle in Undirected Graph
cards.trick: The graph is connected with exactly one cycle. Peel leaves repeatedly (degree 1, like Kahn's topological sort) so only cycle nodes keep degree 2 or more. Then run multi-source BFS from the cycle nodes to get every node's distance.

cards.name: Distinct Numbers in Each Subarray
cards.trick: Fixed-size window of length k with a hash map of counts. Add the entering number, decrement the leaving one and delete its key at 0. The answer for each window is the map size.

cards.name: Distribute Candies Among Children II
cards.trick: Inclusion-exclusion over children exceeding the limit. Total ways C(n+2, 2), minus 3 * C(n - (limit+1) + 2, 2), plus 3 * C(n - 2(limit+1) + 2, 2), minus C(n - 3(limit+1) + 2, 2), treating C of a negative n as 0. (Looping over the first child's candies is O(min(n, limit)).)

cards.name: Distribute Coins in Binary Tree
cards.trick: Post-order DFS returning each subtree's excess = coins - 1 + leftExcess + rightExcess. Every unit of excess crossing an edge is one move, so add abs(leftExcess) + abs(rightExcess) to the answer at each node.

cards.name: Divide Array Into Arrays With Max Difference
cards.trick: Sort, then cut into consecutive triples. The closest possible groups are adjacent in sorted order, so just check last - first <= k for each triple. If any triple fails, return an empty array.

cards.name: Divide Array Into Equal Pairs
cards.trick: The array splits into equal pairs iff every value occurs an even number of times. Toggle each number in a set and check the set is empty at the end. (Counting with a map is the same idea.)

cards.name: Divide Array Into Increasing Sequences
cards.trick: Input is sorted, so equal values must go to different sequences. If a value occurs f times you need at least f sequences, each of length at least k, so need maxFreq * k <= n. Find maxFreq with one scan of runs.

cards.name: Divide Chocolate
cards.trick: Binary search on the answer (the minimum piece sweetness). Feasibility check is greedy: sweep and cut each time the running sum reaches the target, then need at least k + 1 pieces. Maximize the target that still works.

cards.name: Divide Intervals Into Minimum Number of Groups
cards.trick: Answer is the maximum number of overlapping intervals. Sort starts and ends separately and sweep with two pointers (an end at the same time as a start does not free the group, so use end < start to release). (Min-heap of end times works too.)

cards.name: Divide Nodes Into the Maximum Number of Groups
cards.trick: Edges require adjacent groups to differ by exactly 1, so each component must be bipartite (else return -1). BFS from every node to get its eccentricity (number of levels), take the max per component, and sum over components.

cards.name: Divide Players Into Teams of Equal Skill
cards.trick: Sort and pair smallest with largest using two pointers. Every pair must sum to the same target (skill[0] + skill[n-1]), else return -1. Add skill[i] * skill[j] for each pair. (Counting sort makes it O(n + max).)

cards.name: Dot Product of Two Sparse Vectors
cards.time: O(n) to build, O(min(a, b)) per dotProduct (a, b = non-zero counts)
cards.trick: Store only the non-zero entries as an index -> value map. For the dot product iterate the smaller map and look each index up in the other. (Sorted index lists with two pointers is O(a + b).)

cards.name: Dota2 Senate
cards.trick: Two queues of senator indices, one per party. Compare the fronts: the smaller index acts first and bans the other, then re-enters its queue with index + n for the next round. The party whose queue empties loses.

cards.name: Elements in Array After Removing and Replacing Elements
cards.trick: The process cycles every 2n minutes, so use t mod 2n. If t' < n the array is nums[t'..n-1], so index i is nums[t' + i] when i < n - t'. Otherwise the array is nums[0..t'-n-1], so index i is nums[i] when i < t' - n. Else return -1.

cards.name: Eliminate Maximum Number of Monsters
cards.trick: Compute each monster's arrival time ceil(dist / speed) and sort. You shoot one per minute, so at minute i you survive only if arrival[i] > i; the first failure caps the count. (Bucketing arrival times gives O(n).)

cards.name: Employee Free Time
cards.trick: Flatten all employees' intervals, sort by start and merge. The gaps between merged intervals are the common free time. (A min-heap over each employee's list is O(N log k).)

cards.name: Encode and Decode TinyURL
cards.trick: Two hash maps: code -> long URL and long URL -> code. Generate the short code from an incrementing counter (or random string, retrying on collision) and prefix the base short URL. Decode strips the prefix and looks up the code.

cards.name: Encode N-ary Tree to Binary Tree
cards.trick: Left-child right-sibling representation. Binary left = first child, binary right = next sibling. Encode by chaining a node's children down the right pointers of the first child. Decode walks left once, then right across siblings.

cards.name: Encode Number
cards.trick: The encoding is the binary representation of n + 1 with its leading 1 removed. Compute bin(n + 1)[3:] (n = 0 gives the empty string).

cards.name: Encode String With Shortest Length
cards.time: O(n^3) (string ops add a constant-ish factor)
cards.trick: Interval DP: dp[i][j] is the shortest encoding of s[i..j]. Candidates are the raw substring, any split dp[i][k] + dp[k+1][j], and a repeated-pattern encoding k[dp of pattern] found via (t + t).find(t, 1) < len(t). Only encode when it is shorter than the raw form.

cards.name: Equal Tree Partition
cards.trick: Post-order compute every subtree sum and record the non-root ones in a set. Removing one edge works iff total is even and total / 2 is among the non-root subtree sums. Exclude the root, or a total of 0 gives a false positive.

cards.name: Evaluate Boolean Binary Tree
cards.trick: Post-order recursion. Leaf value 0 or 1 is the answer. Internal node value 2 is OR of the children and 3 is AND.

cards.name: Evaluate Division
cards.time: O((E + Q) * alpha(V)) (E equations, Q queries)
cards.trick: Weighted union-find: each variable stores its ratio to its root, updated during path compression. A query a / b is answerable iff same root, and equals weight[a] / weight[b]. (DFS or BFS on a graph with edges a->b = v and b->a = 1/v is O(Q * (V + E)).)

cards.name: Even Odd Tree
cards.trick: BFS by level. Even levels need odd values strictly increasing, odd levels need even values strictly decreasing. Keep the previous value per level and return false on any violation.

cards.name: Excel Sheet Column Title
cards.trick: Bijective base 26 (no zero digit). Each step do n -= 1, then the letter is chr(ord('A') + n % 26) and n //= 26. Reverse the collected letters at the end.

cards.name: Extra Characters in a String
cards.time: O(n^2) with a trie or hash set (n = len(s))
cards.trick: dp[i] = min extra characters in the first i chars. Either skip char i (dp[i-1] + 1) or take any dictionary word ending at i (dp[i - len(word)]). Looking up substrings s[j:i] in a set of words (or walking a trie) keeps it quadratic.

cards.name: Factor Combinations
cards.time: Output-bound; roughly O(sqrt(n)) work per call over all factorizations of n
cards.trick: DFS with a start factor so combos stay non-decreasing. For f from start up to sqrt(n) with n % f == 0, record path + [f, n / f], then recurse on n / f with start f. Never include n itself as a factor.

cards.name: Faulty Sensor
cards.trick: Find the first index i where the arrays differ (if none, return -1). A sensor is a defect candidate if the other array is shifted from there: sensor1[j] == sensor2[j + 1] for all j from i to n - 2 means sensor 1 dropped a value. If both or neither shifts fit, return -1.

cards.name: Filling Bookcase Shelves
cards.trick: dp[i] = min total height for the first i books. For book i, extend the last shelf backwards over books j..i while the width sum fits, tracking the max height, and take dp[j - 1] + maxHeight.

cards.name: Final Array State After K Multiplication Operations I
cards.trick: Min-heap of (value, index) so ties pick the earliest index. Pop the min, multiply it, push it back, k times. (Direct simulation scanning for the min is O(n * k), fine for the small constraints.)

cards.name: Final Prices With a Special Discount in a Shop
cards.trick: Monotonic stack of indices: next smaller-or-equal element to the right. When prices[i] is at most the price at the stack top, pop it and subtract prices[i] as its discount. Then push i.

cards.name: Find All Anagrams in a String
cards.trick: Fixed window of length len(p) with a 26-slot count array (or count diff plus a matches counter). Slide by adding the right char and removing the left one, and record the start index when the counts equal p's.

cards.name: Find All Duplicates in an Array
cards.trick: Values are in 1..n, so use the array as its own hash. For each x, flip the sign at index abs(x) - 1. If it is already negative, abs(x) is a duplicate.

cards.name: Find All Numbers Disappeared in an Array
cards.trick: Values are in 1..n. Mark presence by negating nums[abs(x) - 1] for every x. Indices that are still positive after the pass are the missing numbers i + 1.

cards.name: Find All People With Secret
cards.time: O(m log m + n + m * alpha(n))
cards.trick: Sort meetings by time and process each same-time group. Union-find the participants in the group (person 0 and firstPerson start joined), then after the group reset every participant not connected to 0 so the secret does not leak across times. Answer is everyone connected to 0.

cards.name: Find All Possible Recipes From Given Supplies
cards.trick: Topological sort (Kahn). Build edges ingredient -> recipe and set a recipe's indegree to its ingredient count. Start the queue from the supplies and decrement as items become available. Recipes that reach indegree 0 are makeable. Cycles never get made.

cards.name: Find All The Lonely Nodes
cards.trick: DFS or BFS. A node is lonely when its parent has exactly one child, so when visiting a node with only one child, add that child to the answer before recursing.

cards.name: Find Anagram Mappings
cards.trick: Hash map from value in B to an index in B (any index works for duplicates). Then for each a in A output map[a].

cards.name: Find Bottom Left Tree Value
cards.trick: BFS level order but enqueue the right child before the left. The last node dequeued is the bottom-left value. (DFS tracking the deepest depth, taking the first node seen at it, uses O(h) space.)

cards.name: Find Building Where Alice and Bob Can Meet
cards.trick: For query (a, b) with a <= b: if a == b or heights[a] < heights[b] the answer is b. Otherwise find the leftmost index greater than b with height above max(heights[a], heights[b]). Process queries offline by b descending with a monotonic stack and binary search it. (Sparse table or segment tree descent also works.)

cards.name: Find Champion II
cards.trick: In a DAG the champion has indegree 0. Count indegrees, and if exactly one node has indegree 0 return it, otherwise return -1.

cards.name: Find Closest Node to Given Two Nodes
cards.trick: Each node has at most one outgoing edge, so walk from node1 and from node2 recording distances (stop on a revisit). For every node reached by both, minimize max(d1, d2), breaking ties by smaller index.

cards.name: Find Common Characters
cards.trick: Keep a 26-slot array of minimum counts. Initialize it from the first word, then take the elementwise min with each next word's counts. Output each letter min-count times.

cards.name: Find Critical and Pseudo-Critical Edges in Minimum Spanning Tree
cards.trick: Run Kruskal for the base MST weight. For each edge: skipping it gives a larger weight (or disconnected) -> critical. Otherwise forcing it in first gives the same base weight -> pseudo-critical. (Tarjan bridges per weight group reaches about O(E log E).)

cards.name: Find Distance in a Binary Tree
cards.trick: Distance = depth(p) + depth(q) - 2 * depth(LCA). Find the LCA with one DFS, then measure the depth of each target from it. (Single DFS returning both found-flags and distances also works.)

cards.name: Find Duplicate Subtrees
cards.trick: Post-order, give each distinct subtree shape a unique integer id via a map keyed by (leftId, val, rightId). Count ids and record a node the first time its id count reaches 2. (String serialization is simpler but O(n^2).)

cards.name: Find Eventual Safe States
cards.trick: Safe nodes are those that cannot reach a cycle. Reverse the graph and run Kahn's topological sort from terminal nodes (outdegree 0). Every node that gets processed is safe. (DFS with 3-color state is equivalent.)

cards.name: Find First and Last Position of Element in Sorted Array
cards.trick: Two binary searches for lower bounds. First = lowerBound(target), last = lowerBound(target + 1) - 1. If first is out of range or nums[first] != target, return [-1, -1].

cards.name: Find First Palindromic String in the Array
cards.trick: Scan words in order and check each with two pointers from both ends. Return the first palindrome, or the empty string if none.

cards.name: Find if Array Can Be Sorted
cards.trick: Adjacent swaps are allowed only between numbers with equal popcount, so the array splits into maximal runs of the same popcount that can be sorted internally. It is sortable iff max of each run is at most the min of the next run. (Compare against a sorted copy is O(n log n).)

cards.name: Find in Mountain Array
cards.trick: Three binary searches. First find the peak (compare arr[mid] with arr[mid + 1]). Then search the increasing left side for the target, and only if not found, search the decreasing right side. Return the smallest index.

cards.name: Find K Closest Elements
cards.trick: Binary search the left edge of the size-k window over lo = 0, hi = n - k. If x - arr[mid] is greater than arr[mid + k] - x, move lo = mid + 1, else hi = mid. Return arr[lo..lo + k - 1]. (Two pointers shrinking from the ends is O(n).)

cards.name: Find K Length Substrings With No Repeated Characters
cards.trick: Fixed window of size k with a count map. Slide by adding the right char and removing the left one. Count the window when it has k distinct chars (map size equals k). Or track the last seen index and keep a left bound.

cards.name: Find K-th Smallest Pair Distance
cards.time: O(n log n + n log W) (W = max - min)
cards.trick: Sort, then binary search the distance d. Count pairs with diff at most d using a two-pointer sweep (for each right, advance left while nums[r] - nums[l] exceeds d). Find the smallest d with count at least k.

cards.name: Find Kth Bit in Nth Binary String
cards.trick: S_n = S_{n-1} + '1' + reverse(invert(S_{n-1})), length 2^n - 1, mid = 2^(n-1). If k equals mid the bit is 1. If k is less than mid recurse into S_{n-1}. Otherwise mirror k to len + 1 - k and flip the result.

cards.name: Find Largest Value in Each Tree Row
cards.trick: BFS level order and take the max per level. (DFS with a depth index and res[depth] = max(res[depth], val) works with O(h) extra space.)

cards.name: Find Leaves of Binary Tree
cards.trick: A node is removed in round height(node), where leaves have height 0 and height = 1 + max(left, right). One post-order DFS puts each node in res[height], so no tree mutation is needed.

cards.name: Find Lucky Integer in an Array
cards.trick: Count frequencies (a size-501 array since values are bounded), then return the largest value whose count equals itself, else -1.

cards.name: Find Minimum Diameter After Merging Two Trees
cards.trick: Join the two tree centers. Answer = max(d1, d2, ceil(d1 / 2) + ceil(d2 / 2) + 1), where d1 and d2 are the diameters. Get each diameter with two BFS passes (farthest node, then farthest from it) or a DFS height DP.

cards.name: Find Missing and Repeated Values
cards.trick: Let a be repeated and b missing. sum(grid) - n^2(n^2+1)/2 = a - b, and sumSquares(grid) - expectedSumSquares = a^2 - b^2 = (a - b)(a + b). Solve for a and b. (A frequency array of size n^2 is simpler with O(n^2) space.)

cards.name: Find Missing Observations
cards.trick: Missing sum = mean * (n + m) - sum(rolls). It must be between n and 6n, else return empty. Spread it evenly: every roll gets sum // n and the first sum % n rolls get 1 extra.

cards.name: Find Nearest Right Node in Binary Tree
cards.trick: BFS level by level. When you dequeue u, return the next node in the same level if there is one, else null. (Or DFS tracking the target depth and the first node seen after u at that depth.)

cards.name: Find Peak Element
cards.trick: Binary search on the slope. If nums[mid] is less than nums[mid + 1] a peak lies to the right (lo = mid + 1), else a peak is at mid or to the left (hi = mid). Works because neighbors are never equal and the ends count as minus infinity.

cards.name: Find Permutation
cards.trick: Start with 1..n+1 and reverse the segment covering each maximal run of 'D's. Runs of 'I' stay ascending, which gives the lexicographically smallest result. (A stack that pops on each 'I' does the same.)

cards.name: Find Pivot Index
cards.trick: Prefix sums with a running left sum. The pivot is index i where left == total - left - nums[i]. Return the first such i, else -1.

cards.name: Find Polygon With the Largest Perimeter
cards.trick: Sort ascending and keep a running prefix sum. A side is valid iff it is less than the sum of all smaller sides. Remember the best prefix sum + nums[i] over valid i (the last valid one is the largest), else -1.

cards.name: Find Root of N-Ary Tree
cards.trick: The root is the only node that is never a child. Sum all node values and subtract the sum of all child values (or XOR them) to get the root's value, then pick that node. Values are unique.

cards.name: Find Smallest Common Element in All Rows
cards.trick: Count occurrences in a fixed-size array across all rows (each row has distinct values). The smallest value with count equal to m is the answer. (Per-row pointers or binary search also works.)

cards.name: Find the Celebrity
cards.trick: Pass 1: candidate = 0, and for each i if knows(candidate, i) then candidate = i (a candidate who knows someone cannot be the celebrity). Pass 2: verify the candidate knows nobody and everyone knows the candidate.

cards.name: Find the City With the Smallest Number of Neighbors at a Threshold Distance
cards.trick: Floyd-Warshall for all-pairs shortest paths. For each city count cities within distanceThreshold, and pick the minimum count, breaking ties by the greater city index. (Dijkstra from each node is O(n * e log n).)

cards.name: Find the Derangement of An Array
cards.trick: D(n) = (n - 1) * (D(n - 1) + D(n - 2)) with D(0) = 1, D(1) = 0, mod 1e9 + 7. Element n swaps with one of n - 1 others, and that element either goes to n's slot (D(n-2)) or not (D(n-1)). Keep two variables.

cards.name: Find the Difference
cards.trick: XOR every char of s and t together. Paired chars cancel and the added letter remains. (Counting letters is the same time with O(1) space for 26 letters.)

cards.name: Find the Difference of Two Arrays
cards.trick: Put each array in a set and return [set1 - set2, set2 - set1]. Sets handle duplicates.

cards.name: Find the Index of the First Occurrence in a String
cards.trick: KMP. Build the longest-proper-prefix-that-is-also-suffix (lps) array for the needle, then scan the haystack and on a mismatch fall back with lps instead of restarting. (Naive slide-and-compare is O(n * m).)

cards.name: Find the Index of the Large Integer
cards.trick: Compare the sum of the left half to the sum of the right half with compareSub. The heavier half contains the larger integer, so recurse into it. For odd length, drop the middle element from both sides, and if they are equal the middle is the answer.

cards.name: Find the Kth Largest Integer in the Array
cards.time: O(n * L * log k) (L = max string length)
cards.trick: Numbers are strings, so compare by length first, then lexicographically. Keep a min-heap of size k with that comparator and return the top. (Quickselect with the same comparator is O(n * L) average.)

cards.name: Find the Length of the Longest Common Prefix
cards.trick: Put every prefix of every number in arr1 into a hash set (shrinking by x // 10). For each number in arr2, shrink it digit by digit until a prefix is in the set, and track the longest length. (A trie is equivalent.)

cards.name: Find the Longest Substring Containing Vowels in Even Counts
cards.trick: Prefix parity bitmask with one bit per vowel, toggled on each vowel. Two equal masks mean the substring between has even counts of every vowel. Store the first index of each mask (mask 0 at index -1) and maximize the distance.

cards.name: Find the Longest Valid Obstacle Course at Each Position
cards.trick: Longest non-decreasing subsequence ending at each index. Keep a tails array and use bisect_right (not bisect_left, since equal values are allowed). The insertion index plus 1 is the answer for that position.

cards.name: Find the Maximum Sum of Node Values
cards.trick: The tree shape does not matter: you can XOR with k any even-sized set of nodes. For each node take (v ^ k) if it is bigger, counting how many were flipped. If the count is odd, subtract the smallest absolute gain abs((v ^ k) - v).

cards.name: Find the Minimum and Maximum Number of Nodes Between Critical Points
cards.trick: One pass with prev, cur, next. A critical point is a strict local min or max. Track first and previous critical indices: min = smallest gap between consecutive critical indices, max = last - first. Fewer than 2 critical points gives [-1, -1].

cards.name: Find the Power of K Size Subarrays I
cards.trick: Track the length of the current run of consecutive increasing-by-1 values. For the window ending at i (when i is at least k - 1), the power is nums[i] if run length is at least k, else -1.

cards.name: Find the Punishment Number of an Integer
cards.trick: For each i in 1..n, backtrack over splits of the decimal string of i * i into contiguous pieces, checking whether some split sums to i. Prune when the running sum exceeds i. Add i * i for each success.

cards.name: Find the Safest Path in a Grid
cards.trick: Multi-source BFS from all thieves gives a safeness value per cell. Then maximize the minimum safeness along a path with Dijkstra using a max-heap (or binary search on the answer plus BFS). (Union-find over cells sorted by safeness also works.)

cards.name: Find the Town Judge
cards.trick: Net trust score per person: for each [a, b], score[a] -= 1 and score[b] += 1. The judge is the one with score n - 1 (trusted by all others, trusts nobody). Return -1 if none.

cards.name: Find the Winner of the Circular Game
cards.trick: Josephus recurrence on 0-indexed survivor: f(1) = 0, f(i) = (f(i - 1) + k) % i. Return f(n) + 1. (Queue or linked list simulation is O(n * k).)

cards.name: Find Unique Binary String
cards.trick: Cantor diagonalization. Build the answer by flipping the i-th char of the i-th string, so it differs from every input string at one position. (Backtracking with a set also works.)

cards.name: Find Valid Matrix Given Row and Column Sums
cards.trick: Fill cell (i, j) with min(rowSum[i], colSum[j]), then subtract it from both. Either the row or the column is satisfied, so the leftover sums stay consistent and every sum ends at 0.

cards.name: Find Words That Can Be Formed by Characters
cards.trick: Count the letters in chars. For each word count its letters and check every count is at most the available one. Sum the lengths of the good words.

cards.name: Finding the Number of Visible Mountains
cards.trick: Each peak (x, y) is the interval [x - y, x + y]. A mountain is hidden if its interval is contained in another. Sort by left ascending then right descending, track the max right, and count a mountain only if its right exceeds it. Duplicate mountains hide each other, so drop both.

cards.name: First Missing Positive
cards.trick: Cyclic sort in place. While 1 <= nums[i] <= n and nums[nums[i] - 1] != nums[i], swap it to its home index nums[i] - 1. The first index i with nums[i] != i + 1 gives answer i + 1, else n + 1.

cards.name: First Unique Character in a String
cards.trick: Two passes. Count letter frequencies, then scan again and return the first index whose count is 1, else -1.

cards.name: First Unique Number
cards.time: O(1) amortized per add and showFirstUnique
cards.trick: Hash map of counts plus a queue (or ordered hash set) of candidates in arrival order. On showFirstUnique pop the front while its count is above 1. Each element is popped at most once, so it is amortized O(1).

cards.name: Fixed Point
cards.trick: Array has distinct sorted ints, so arr[i] - i is non-decreasing. Binary search the first index with arr[i] - i at least 0, then check that it equals 0 (that is the smallest fixed point).

cards.name: Flatten 2D Vector
cards.time: O(1) amortized per next and hasNext
cards.trick: Keep row and column pointers. A helper advances past exhausted or empty rows before every next() and hasNext(). (Flattening into one list in the constructor costs O(n) space.)

cards.name: Flatten Nested List Iterator
cards.trick: Stack of list iterators (or a stack of the list pushed in reverse). hasNext() unwraps until the top is an integer, popping exhausted lists and pushing nested lists' contents. Lazy, so you avoid flattening upfront with O(n) space.

cards.name: Flip Columns For Maximum Number of Equal Rows
cards.trick: Two rows can become all-equal under the same column flips iff they are identical or exact complements. Normalize each row by XOR with its first element (so it starts with 0), count the normalized rows in a hash map, and return the max count.

cards.name: Flip Equivalent Binary Trees
cards.trick: Recurse: roots must have equal values, and either (left, left) and (right, right) are flip equivalent, or (left, right) and (right, left) are. Both null is true, one null or unequal values is false.

cards.name: Flip Game
cards.trick: Scan for every adjacent '++' and emit the string with that pair flipped to '--'. Each result costs O(n) to build and there are at most n - 1 of them.

cards.name: Flip Game II
cards.trick: Sprague-Grundy. Runs of '+' are independent games: g[0] = g[1] = 0 and g[L] = mex of g[i] ^ g[L - 2 - i] over i. First player wins iff the XOR of g over all runs is nonzero. (Backtracking with memo on the string is O(n * 2^n).)

cards.name: Flip String to Monotone Increasing
cards.trick: One pass with ones = count of 1s so far and flips = min cost so far. On '1' do ones += 1. On '0' set flips = min(flips + 1, ones), either flip this 0 to 1 or flip all earlier 1s to 0.

cards.name: Flood Fill
cards.trick: DFS or BFS from (sr, sc) over 4-neighbors with the original color, recoloring as you go (recoloring doubles as the visited mark). Return early if the original color already equals the new color or you loop forever.

cards.name: Freedom Trail
cards.trick: dp over key positions and ring positions: dp[j] = min steps with the ring pointing at j for the current key char. Transition from each position j to every position k of the next key char with cost min(abs(j - k), n - abs(j - k)) + 1 (the +1 is the button press). Precompute positions per letter.

cards.name: Frequency of the Most Frequent Element
cards.trick: Sort, then slide a window where the target is nums[r]. The window is valid iff nums[r] * (r - l + 1) - windowSum is at most k. Shrink from the left when it is not, and track the max window size.

cards.name: Fruit Into Baskets
cards.space: O(1) (at most 3 keys in the map)
cards.trick: Longest subarray with at most 2 distinct values. Hash map of fruit -> count over the window. When the map has 3 types, shrink from the left, deleting a type whose count hits 0.

cards.name: Furthest Building You Can Reach
cards.time: O(n log L) (n buildings, L ladders)
cards.trick: Min-heap of climbs that got a ladder. Give every climb a ladder first. When the heap exceeds L, pop the smallest climb and pay for it with bricks. Stop when bricks go negative. Ladders always cover the biggest climbs.

cards.name: Game of Nim
cards.trick: This is misere Nim (taking the last stone loses). If every pile is size 0 or 1, Alice wins iff the count of 1-piles is even. Otherwise Alice wins iff the XOR of all piles is nonzero. (Bitmask DP over game states is O(8^n).)

cards.name: Generalized Abbreviation
cards.trick: For each index choose: abbreviate it (increment a pending count) or keep the char (flush the pending count as digits, then append the char). Flush any pending count at the end.

cards.name: Get Equal Substrings Within Budget
cards.trick: Cost of position i is |s[i] - t[i]|. Find the longest window whose total cost is <= maxCost. Expand right, and shrink from the left while the running cost exceeds the budget.

cards.name: Greatest Common Divisor of Strings
cards.trick: If str1 + str2 != str2 + str1 no common divisor exists. Otherwise the answer is the prefix of length gcd(len1, len2). (Trying every prefix length is O(min(n, m) * (n + m)).)

cards.name: Greatest Common Divisor Traversal
cards.trick: Union-find. Factor each number by trial division and union its index with the first index seen for each prime (dict prime -> index). Connected iff one component remains. Special cases: n == 1 is true, any 1 with n > 1 is false.

cards.name: Grid Game
cards.trick: Prefix sums on a 2 x n grid. If robot 1 drops down at column i, robot 2 gets max(top row sum after i, bottom row sum before i). Robot 1 picks the i that minimizes that value.

cards.name: Group Shifted Strings
cards.time: O(n * k) (n strings, k = max length)
cards.trick: Hash key is the tuple of differences between adjacent chars, taken mod 26 so wraparound (like 'az' and 'ba') matches. Strings in one shift group share the key.

cards.name: Grumpy Bookstore Owner
cards.trick: Base = sum of customers when grumpy is 0. Then slide a fixed window of size minutes over customers[i] * grumpy[i] to find the max extra customers saved. Answer = base + best window.

cards.name: Guess the Majority in a Hidden Array
cards.trick: query returns 4, 2 or 0 for 4-0, 3-1, 2-2 splits. Compare each index with index 0 by swapping one element in and out of the group (0,1,2,3) and checking if the query result changes. Count indices equal to 0 vs different, return an index from the larger side (or -1 on a tie).

cards.name: Handshakes That Don't Cross
cards.trick: Catalan numbers. dp[0] = 1. Person 1 shakes hands with person j, which splits the circle into two independent groups: dp[i] = sum of dp[j] * dp[i - 2 - j] over even j. Take results mod 1e9 + 7.

cards.name: Height Checker
cards.trick: Counting sort over heights 1..100 gives the expected order without a real sort. Count positions where the expected height differs from the actual one. (Plain sort is O(n log n).)

cards.name: Hexspeak
cards.trick: Convert the number to uppercase hex, then map 0 -> O and 1 -> I. If any digit is 2-9 the result is invalid, return ERROR.

cards.name: High Five
cards.time: O(n + s log s) (n scores, s students)
cards.trick: Per student keep a min-heap of size 5: push each score and pop the smallest once the size exceeds 5. Then average the heap and output students sorted by id (floor division).

cards.name: House Robber III
cards.trick: Post-order DFS returns a pair (rob this node, skip this node). rob = val + skip(left) + skip(right). skip = max(rob, skip) of left + max(rob, skip) of right. Answer is the max of the root pair.

cards.name: House Robber IV
cards.trick: Binary search on the capability k. Check feasibility greedily: take any house with value <= k and skip the next one. If you can take at least the required number of houses, k works. Find the smallest such k.

cards.name: How Many Apples Can You Put Into the Basket
cards.trick: Sort weights ascending and take apples while the running total stays <= 5000. Lightest first maximizes the count. (Counting sort over the bounded weights is O(n + W).)

cards.name: Image Smoother
cards.space: O(1) extra (O(m * n) with a copy)
cards.trick: For each cell average the up-to-9 in-bounds neighbors, floor the result. To go in place, pack the new value into the high bits (val | avg << 8), then shift everything down at the end.

cards.name: Implement Queue Using Stacks
cards.trick: Two stacks: push onto 'in'. For pop/peek, if 'out' is empty move everything from 'in' to 'out' (reversing the order), then use out's top. Transfer only when out is empty.

cards.name: Implement Stack Using Queues
cards.trick: One queue. After pushing x, rotate the queue n - 1 times (pop front, push back) so the newest element sits at the front. Then pop and top are plain queue operations.

cards.name: Index Pairs of a String
cards.time: O(T + n * L) (T = total word chars, n = len(text), L = longest word)
cards.trick: Build a trie of the words. For each start index walk the trie along text until there is no child, recording [start, end] whenever the node marks a word end. Output is already sorted by start then end.

cards.name: Inorder Successor in BST
cards.trick: Walk down from the root. If p.val < node.val the node is a successor candidate: record it and go left. Otherwise go right. The last recorded candidate is the answer.

cards.name: Inorder Successor in BST II
cards.trick: Parent pointers, no root needed. If the node has a right child, return the leftmost node of that subtree. Otherwise climb until you arrive from a left child and return that parent (null if none).

cards.name: Insert Delete GetRandom O(1)
cards.trick: Dynamic array plus hash map of value -> index. To delete, swap the target with the last element, update the moved element's index in the map, then pop. getRandom picks a random array index.

cards.name: Insert Greatest Common Divisors in Linked List
cards.trick: Walk with cur and cur.next. Create a node holding gcd(cur.val, cur.next.val), splice it between them, then jump to the original next node.

cards.name: Insert Into a Binary Search Tree
cards.trick: Walk down iteratively: go left if val < node.val, else right, until the next child is empty, then attach the new node there. A new value is always inserted as a leaf, no rebalancing needed.

cards.name: Insert Into a Sorted Circular Linked List
cards.trick: Walk one lap with prev and curr. Insert between them if prev.val <= val <= curr.val, or at the wrap point (prev.val > curr.val) when val >= prev.val or val <= curr.val. If the lap finishes without a spot (all equal), insert anywhere. Handle the empty list.

cards.name: Insertion Sort List
cards.trick: Dummy head for the sorted part. Take each node from the input, scan the sorted part for its position and splice it in. Keeping a tail pointer and appending when node >= tail makes sorted input O(n).

cards.name: Integer Break
cards.trick: Split into as many 3s as possible. n <= 3 returns n - 1. If n % 3 == 0 return 3^(n/3), if 1 remainder use 3^(k-1) * 4, if 2 remainder use 3^k * 2. (DP over splits is O(n^2).)

cards.name: Integer to English Words
cards.trick: Process in chunks of three digits with the scale words Thousand, Million, Billion. A helper turns 0-999 into words using lookup lists for ones, teens and tens. Skip zero chunks and handle 0 as Zero.

cards.name: Integer to Roman
cards.trick: Greedy over a value table that includes the subtractive pairs: 1000, 900, 500, 400, 100, 90, 50, 40, 10, 9, 5, 4, 1. Repeatedly subtract the largest value that fits and append its symbol.

cards.name: Intersection of Three Sorted Arrays
cards.trick: Three pointers. If all three values match, record it and advance all. Otherwise advance only the pointer(s) pointing at the smallest value.

cards.name: Intersection of Two Arrays
cards.trick: Put one array in a set, then scan the other and collect values found in it, removing each from the set so results are unique. (Sort + two pointers is O(n log n) with O(1) extra.)

cards.name: Intersection of Two Linked Lists
cards.trick: Two pointers; when one reaches the end it restarts at the other list's head. Both walk n + m steps in total, so they meet at the intersection node, or both reach null if there is none.

cards.name: Interval List Intersections
cards.trick: Two pointers over both sorted lists. Overlap is [max(starts), min(ends)] if start <= end. Then advance the pointer whose interval ends first.

cards.name: IP to CIDR
cards.trick: Convert the IP to a 32-bit int. At each step the block size is capped by the lowest set bit of the current IP (ip & -ip) and by the largest power of two <= remaining n. Emit the block with prefix length 32 - log2(size), then advance the IP.

cards.name: IPO
cards.time: O(n log n + k log n)
cards.trick: Sort projects by capital needed. For each of k rounds push the profit of every project now affordable into a max-heap, then pop the best one and add it to capital. Stop early if the heap is empty.

cards.name: Is Graph Bipartite
cards.trick: 2-color with BFS or DFS from every unvisited node (the graph may be disconnected). Give neighbors the opposite color. A neighbor with the same color means an odd cycle, so return false.

cards.name: Is Subsequence
cards.trick: One pointer into s, one scanning t. Advance the s pointer only on a match. If it reaches the end of s, true. (Many queries: store index lists per char and binary search.)

cards.name: Island Perimeter
cards.trick: Each land cell adds 4, and each shared edge between two land cells removes 2. Just check the cell above and the cell to the left of every land cell and subtract 2 per land neighbor. No DFS needed.

cards.name: Isomorphic Strings
cards.trick: The mapping must be one-to-one both ways. Keep a map s -> t and a map t -> s, and fail if either contradicts the current pair.

cards.name: Jump Game VII
cards.trick: dp[i] is true if s[i] == '0' and some reachable j lies in [i - maxJump, i - minJump]. Keep a sliding count of reachable positions in that window (or prefix sums) instead of scanning it. (BFS with a furthest-visited marker is also O(n).)

cards.name: K Empty Slots
cards.trick: Invert the array: days[pos] = day the bulb at pos turns on. Slide a window [left, left + k + 1] and check every inner day is greater than both endpoint days. On a failure, jump left to the offending index. Answer is the min over valid windows of max(endpoints). (Ordered set is O(n log n).)

cards.name: K Inverse Pairs Array
cards.trick: dp[i][j] = arrays of 1..i with j inverse pairs = sum of dp[i-1][j-t] for t in 0..i-1. Use a sliding prefix sum: dp[i][j] = dp[i][j-1] + dp[i-1][j] - dp[i-1][j-i]. Roll the rows and take mod 1e9 + 7.

cards.name: K-th Smallest in Lexicographical Order
cards.trick: Treat 1..n as an implicit 10-ary trie. Count how many numbers lie under prefix cur (steps between cur and cur + 1 across levels, capped at n + 1). If k exceeds that count skip the subtree (cur += 1, k -= count), else descend (cur *= 10, k -= 1).

cards.name: K-th Symbol in Grammar
cards.trick: The symbol at position k (1-indexed) equals the parity of the number of set bits in k - 1 (Thue-Morse sequence). Recursive version: flip the parent's value when k is even.

cards.name: Kill Process
cards.trick: Build a map parent -> list of children from the ppid array. Then DFS or BFS from the killed pid and collect every node visited.

cards.name: Knight Dialer
cards.trick: dp over the 10 digits: ways[d] after each hop is the sum of ways of the digits a knight can come from. Keep only the previous row of 10 counts and mod 1e9 + 7. (Matrix exponentiation gives O(log n).)

cards.name: Kth Distinct String in an Array
cards.trick: Count frequencies in a hash map, then scan the array in original order and return the k-th string whose count is 1. Return an empty string if there are fewer than k.

cards.name: Kth Largest Sum in a Binary Tree
cards.trick: BFS and record the sum of each level. Then take the k-th largest of those sums with a size-k min-heap (or sort). Return -1 if there are fewer than k levels.

cards.name: Kth Smallest Product of Two Sorted Arrays
cards.time: O(n log m log C) (C = product range)
cards.trick: Binary search on the product value x in [-1e10, 1e10]. Count pairs with a*b <= x by binary searching nums2 for each a, flipping direction when a < 0 and handling a == 0 separately. Smallest x with count >= k. (Two pointers per sign gets O((n + m) log C).)

cards.name: Kth Smallest Subarray Sum
cards.time: O(n log S) (S = sum of nums)
cards.trick: All values are positive, so binary search on the sum s in [min, total]. Count subarrays with sum <= s using a sliding window (add r, shrink l, add r - l + 1). Smallest s with count >= k.

cards.name: Largest 3-Same-Digit Number in String
cards.trick: Scan every window of length 3 and keep the largest one where all three chars are equal. Return an empty string if none.

cards.name: Largest BST Subtree
cards.trick: Post-order DFS returning (is BST, size, min, max) for each subtree. A node forms a BST if left.max < val < right.min and both children are BSTs, then size = left + right + 1. Track the max size seen.

cards.name: Largest Color Value in a Directed Graph
cards.trick: Kahn's topological sort with dp[node][c] = max count of color c on a path ending at node. When processing an edge u -> v, update dp[v][c] = max(dp[v][c], dp[u][c] + (color[v] == c)). If fewer than n nodes are processed there is a cycle, return -1.

cards.name: Largest Combination With Bitwise AND Greater Than Zero
cards.trick: An AND is nonzero iff all chosen numbers share at least one set bit. For each bit position count how many numbers have it set. The answer is the max count over bits.

cards.name: Largest Divisible Subset
cards.trick: Sort ascending. dp[i] = longest chain ending at nums[i], with dp[i] = 1 + dp[j] for j < i where nums[i] % nums[j] == 0. Keep a parent index to rebuild the subset. Divisibility is transitive on a sorted chain, so only the last element needs checking.

cards.name: Largest Local Values in a Matrix
cards.trick: Output is (n - 2) x (n - 2). Each output cell is the max of its 3 x 3 window in the input, a constant 9 comparisons.

cards.name: Largest Number
cards.time: O(n log n * k) (k = max digits)
cards.trick: Convert to strings and sort with the comparator a + b > b + a (concatenation order decides). Join the result. If the first string is '0' return '0' to avoid leading zeros.

cards.name: Largest Odd Number in String
cards.trick: A number is odd iff its last digit is odd. Scan from the right for the first odd digit and return the prefix ending there (the whole prefix is the largest). Return an empty string if none.

cards.name: Largest Subarray Length K
cards.trick: Elements are distinct, so the largest subarray is decided by its first element. Find the max among the first n - k + 1 elements and return the length-k slice starting there.

cards.name: Largest Submatrix With Rearrangements
cards.trick: Turn each row into column heights of consecutive 1s ending at that row (h[j] += 1 or reset to 0). Sort the row's heights descending. The i-th largest height h gives a rectangle of area h * (i + 1) because columns can be reordered freely.

cards.name: Largest Substring Between Two Equal Characters
cards.trick: Store the first index of each char. On every later occurrence, candidate length = i - first[c] - 1. Take the max, or -1 if no char repeats.

cards.name: Largest Unique Number
cards.trick: Count frequencies and return the largest value whose count is exactly 1, or -1. (With values bounded to 0..1000 a fixed count array gives O(1) space.)

cards.name: Last Stone Weight II
cards.trick: Smashing stones is the same as splitting them into two groups and minimizing the difference of the sums. 0/1 knapsack: find the largest reachable subset sum <= total / 2. Answer = total - 2 * best. Use a 1-D boolean array iterated backwards.

cards.name: Leaf-Similar Trees
cards.space: O(h) with lazy generators (O(n + m) if you build both lists)
cards.trick: DFS each tree left to right and collect the leaf values (nodes with no children), then compare the two sequences. A generator per tree lets you stop at the first mismatch.

cards.name: Least Number of Unique Integers after K Removals
cards.trick: Count frequencies and remove the least frequent values first, because each removed value fully costs its count. Bucket values by frequency (counting sort) to avoid an O(n log n) sort. Answer = remaining distinct values.

cards.name: Leftmost Column with at Least a One
cards.trick: Rows are sorted, so start at the top-right corner. If the cell is 1 move left and record the column, else move down. Each step eliminates a row or column. (Binary search per row is O(m log n).)

cards.name: Lemonade Change
cards.trick: Track the count of $5 and $10 bills. For $10 give back a $5. For $20 prefer one $10 + one $5, otherwise three $5s, because $5s are more flexible. Fail if you cannot make change.

cards.name: Length of Last Word
cards.trick: Scan from the end: skip trailing spaces, then count chars until the next space or the start of the string.

cards.name: Length of Longest Fibonacci Subsequence
cards.trick: dp[j][k] = length of the longest Fibonacci-like sequence ending with arr[j], arr[k]. For each pair look up arr[k] - arr[j] in a value -> index map. If it exists at i < j then dp[j][k] = dp[i][j] + 1, else 2. Answer is the max if >= 3, else 0.

cards.name: Length of Longest Subarray With at Most K Frequency
cards.trick: Window with a hash map of counts. After adding nums[r], while its count exceeds k move left forward and decrement counts. Track the max window length.

cards.name: Letter Tile Possibilities
cards.trick: Count letters, then DFS: for each letter with count > 0, use it, count this new sequence (+1), recurse, then restore. Iterating over distinct letters (not positions) avoids duplicate sequences.

cards.name: Lexicographical Numbers
cards.trick: Iterative preorder walk of the implicit 10-ary trie. From cur: if cur * 10 <= n go deeper, else if cur >= n step up (cur //= 10), then cur += 1 and strip trailing zeros (while cur % 10 == 0: cur //= 10).

cards.name: LFU Cache
cards.trick: Map key -> (value, freq), and map freq -> ordered dict of keys (LRU order within a frequency). Track minFreq. On access move the key to freq + 1 and bump minFreq if its old bucket emptied. On eviction pop the oldest key from the minFreq bucket.

cards.name: Line Reflection
cards.trick: The line must be at x = (minX + maxX) / 2, so every point's mirror is (minX + maxX - x, y). Put all points in a set and check each mirror exists. Using the sum avoids fractions.

cards.name: Linked List in Binary Tree
cards.trick: Run KMP over the tree: build the failure table for the list values, then DFS carrying the current matched length, falling back with the table on a mismatch. Return true when the whole list is matched. (Brute force DFS from each node is O(n * min(L, h)).)

cards.name: Logger Rate Limiter
cards.trick: Hash map message -> next allowed timestamp. If timestamp >= the stored value, print it and set the value to timestamp + 10. Otherwise suppress it.

cards.name: Lonely Pixel I
cards.trick: First pass: count black pixels per row and per column. Second pass: a black pixel is lonely when its row count and column count are both 1.

cards.name: Lonely Pixel II
cards.trick: Count black pixels per column and count identical rows via a hash of each row string. A black pixel at (r, c) counts if row r has exactly N blacks, column c has exactly N blacks, and the row pattern occurs N times (so all those rows are identical).

cards.name: Longest Common Prefix
cards.trick: Vertical scan: for each index i compare strs[0][i] with every other string, stopping at the first mismatch or when any string ends. Return the prefix up to that index.

cards.name: Longest Common Subsequence Between Sorted Arrays
cards.trick: Each array is strictly increasing, so a value appears at most once per array. Count occurrences across all arrays and keep the values whose count equals the number of arrays. Order is by value.

cards.name: Longest Continuous Subarray With Absolute Diff Less Than or Equal to Limit
cards.trick: Sliding window with two monotonic deques: one decreasing for the window max and one increasing for the window min. While max - min > limit, advance left and pop deque fronts whose index fell out. (Two heaps with lazy deletion is O(n log n).)

cards.name: Longest Happy String
cards.trick: Max-heap of (count, char). Take the most frequent char unless it would make three in a row. In that case use the second most frequent. If there is none, stop. Push back with the decremented count.

cards.name: Longest Ideal Subsequence
cards.trick: dp[c] = longest ideal subsequence ending in letter c. For each char x, new = 1 + max(dp[c]) over letters with |c - x| <= k, then dp[x] = max(dp[x], new). Answer is the max of dp.

cards.name: Longest Line of Consecutive One in Matrix
cards.trick: For each cell track four run lengths ending there: horizontal, vertical, diagonal, anti-diagonal. Each extends the neighbor's run in its direction (left, up, up-left, up-right) when the cell is 1. Keep only the previous row. Answer is the max over all.

cards.name: Longest Nice Subarray
cards.trick: Keep the OR of the window. A subarray is nice iff all elements have disjoint bits. While window & nums[r] != 0, remove nums[l] with XOR (bits are disjoint so XOR undoes the OR) and advance l. Then OR in nums[r].

cards.name: Longest Palindrome
cards.trick: Count chars. Every char contributes count // 2 * 2 to the length. Add 1 if any char has an odd count, since one can sit in the middle.

cards.name: Longest Palindromic Subsequence
cards.trick: dp[i][j] on s[i..j]: if the ends match then dp[i+1][j-1] + 2, else max(dp[i+1][j], dp[i][j-1]). Single chars give 1. Only the previous row is needed. (Same as LCS of s and reversed s.)

cards.name: Longest Palindromic Subsequence II
cards.trick: Like the palindromic subsequence DP but with a third dimension for the last matched outer char. dp[i][j][c] = best good palindrome in s[i..j] whose outermost char is not c. If s[i] == s[j] != c take 2 + dp[i+1][j-1][s[i]], else skip i or j. Even length and no two adjacent equal chars are enforced by the c check.

cards.name: Longest Repeating Substring
cards.trick: If a repeated substring of length L exists, so does one of length L - 1, so binary search on L. Check a length with a rolling hash (or a set of substrings) over all windows, looking for a duplicate. (DP is O(n^2).)

cards.name: Longest Strictly Increasing or Strictly Decreasing Subarray
cards.trick: One pass tracking the current increasing run and the current decreasing run. Extend a run when the adjacent comparison matches its direction, otherwise reset it to 1. Answer is the max of either run.

cards.name: Longest String Chain
cards.trick: Sort words by length. dp[word] = 1 + max dp[pred] over every predecessor made by deleting one char, looked up in a hash map. Answer is the max dp value.

cards.name: Longest Subarray With Maximum Bitwise AND
cards.trick: AND never exceeds its smallest operand, so the max possible AND equals the max element. The answer is the longest run of consecutive elements equal to that max.

cards.name: Longest Substring With At Most K Distinct Characters
cards.trick: Window with a hash map of char -> count. When the map holds more than k keys, shrink from the left, deleting a key when its count reaches 0. Track the max window length.

cards.name: Longest Substring With At Most Two Distinct Characters
cards.trick: Same as the at-most-k version with k = 2: hash map of counts over the window, shrink from the left while there are 3 distinct chars.

cards.name: Longest Turbulent Subarray
cards.trick: Compare the sign of each adjacent difference with the previous one. If the signs alternate extend the window, if the difference is 0 reset to 1, otherwise restart the window at the last pair (length 2). Track the max.

cards.name: Longest Word With All Prefixes
cards.trick: Insert all words into a trie marking word ends. A word qualifies if every node on its path is a word end. Keep the longest, ties broken lexicographically smallest. (Sort + set of built-up prefixes works too.)

cards.name: Lowest Common Ancestor of a Binary Tree
cards.trick: Recurse: return the node if it is None, p or q. If both left and right recursive calls return non-null, the current node is the LCA. Otherwise return whichever side is non-null.

cards.name: Lowest Common Ancestor of a Binary Tree II
cards.trick: p or q may be missing from the tree. Do a post-order DFS without returning early on a match, so both subtrees are fully explored, and count how many of p and q were found. Return the LCA only if the count reaches 2, else null.

cards.name: Lowest Common Ancestor of a Binary Tree III
cards.trick: Nodes have parent pointers, so this is Intersection of Two Linked Lists. Move a and b up, and when one hits null restart it at the other's start. They meet at the LCA. (A set of ancestors is O(h) space.)

cards.name: Lowest Common Ancestor of a Binary Tree IV
cards.trick: Put the k target nodes in a set. Same recursion as LCA I: return the node if it is in the set. If both sides return non-null the current node is the LCA of all targets, otherwise pass up the non-null side.

cards.name: Lucky Numbers in a Matrix
cards.trick: A lucky number is the min of its row and the max of its column. Distinct values mean there is at most one, and it equals both max(row minimums) and min(column maximums). Compute both and return the value if they match.

cards.name: Magic Squares In Grid
cards.trick: Check every 3 x 3 window. The center must be 5, the window must contain exactly the values 1-9, and all rows, columns and both diagonals must sum to 15. The center-is-5 test prunes most windows.

cards.name: Majority Element
cards.trick: Boyer-Moore voting. Keep a candidate and a count: same value count++, different count--, and when count hits 0 take the current value as the new candidate. The majority element always survives. (Hash map count is O(n) space.)

cards.name: Majority Element II
cards.trick: Boyer-Moore with two candidates and two counts, since at most 2 values can appear more than n/3 times. A value matching neither candidate decrements both counts. Run a second pass to verify the real counts exceed n/3.

cards.name: Make a Positive Array
cards.trick: Greedy scan keeping prefix sums. A bad subarray of length >= 3 ending at i exists when prefix[i] - min(prefix up to i - 3) <= 0. Then replace nums[i] with a huge value, count one operation and reset the tracked prefixes, since that fixes every bad subarray through i.

cards.name: Make Array Non-decreasing or Non-increasing
cards.trick: Slope trick with a max heap. For each x push x, and if the heap top > x add top - x to the cost, pop it and push x again. Run once for non-decreasing and once on the reversed array for non-increasing, take the min. (DP over compressed values is O(n^2).)

cards.name: Make Lexicographically Smallest Array by Swapping Elements
cards.trick: Sort the values and split them into groups wherever adjacent sorted values differ by more than limit. Each group is freely rearrangeable. Give each group's sorted values to that group's sorted original indices.

cards.name: Make Sum Divisible by P
cards.trick: Let need = total % p. Find the shortest subarray whose sum % p == need. Keep a map of prefix % p -> latest index, and at each index look up (prefix - need) % p. If the shortest equals n return -1.

cards.name: Make The String Great
cards.trick: Stack of chars. If the top and the current char are the same letter in different case (abs(ord difference) == 32), pop. Otherwise push. The stack is the answer.

cards.name: Make Two Arrays Equal by Reversing Subarrays
cards.trick: Reversals can reach any permutation, so the arrays are convertible exactly when they have the same multiset. Compare frequency counts. (Sorting both is O(n log n) time.)

cards.name: Making A Large Island
cards.time: O(n^2) for an n x n grid
cards.trick: Label each island with DFS or BFS and store size by label. For each 0 cell, add 1 plus the sizes of the distinct labels among its 4 neighbors (use a set so one island is not counted twice). Handle the all-ones grid separately.

cards.name: Match Alphanumerical Pattern in Matrix I
cards.time: O(m * n * p * q) (matrix m x n, pattern p x q)
cards.trick: Try every top-left corner and check each cell. A digit in the pattern must equal the cell exactly. A letter must map consistently to one digit with two maps (letter -> digit and digit -> letter) so different letters get different digits.

cards.name: Matchsticks to Square
cards.trick: Return false if the sum is not divisible by 4 or the longest stick exceeds the side. Bitmask DP where dp[mask] = length filled mod side, adding a stick only if it fits in the current side. (Backtracking over 4 sides with sticks sorted descending is O(4^n) but prunes well.)

cards.name: Matrix Diagonal Sum
cards.time: O(n) for an n x n matrix
cards.trick: Sum mat[i][i] + mat[i][n-1-i] for every row. If n is odd the center cell was counted twice, so subtract mat[n//2][n//2].

cards.name: Max Chunks To Make Sorted
cards.trick: The array is a permutation of 0..n-1. Track the running max. Whenever running max == index i, the prefix holds exactly 0..i so a chunk can end here. Count those positions.

cards.name: Max Consecutive Ones
cards.trick: One pass with a running count. Increment on 1, reset to 0 on 0, and update the best after each element.

cards.name: Max Consecutive Ones II
cards.trick: Sliding window that holds at most one 0 (flip allowed once). When the zero count exceeds 1 move left forward until it drops back. Works on a stream since left only moves forward and nothing is stored.

cards.name: Max Consecutive Ones III
cards.trick: Window with at most k zeros. Expand right, counting zeros. While zeros > k advance left, decrementing the count when it passes a 0. Best = max window length.

cards.name: Max Points on a Line
cards.trick: For each point as an anchor, count other points by slope in a hash map. Store slope as a reduced (dy, dx) pair using gcd with a normalized sign, never as a float. Answer is the max count in any bucket + 1.

cards.name: Max Stack
cards.time: O(1) top and peekMax, O(log n) push, pop and popMax
cards.trick: Doubly linked list for stack order plus a sorted map value -> list of nodes. popMax grabs the last node for the max value and unlinks it from the middle of the list in O(1). (Two stacks makes popMax O(n).)

cards.name: Maximal Score After Applying K Operations
cards.trick: Max heap. k times: pop the largest x, add it to the score, push ceil(x / 3). Always taking the current max is optimal since each pick is independent. Heapify first for O(n) build.

cards.name: Maximal Square
cards.trick: dp[i][j] = side of the largest all-1 square with bottom-right corner at (i, j) = 1 + min(up, left, up-left) if the cell is 1, else 0. Answer is max side squared. Keep only the previous row for O(n) space.

cards.name: Maximize Score After N Operations
cards.trick: Bitmask DP over which elements are used. The operation number is popcount(mask) / 2 + 1, so it needs no extra state. dp[mask] = max over unused pairs (i, j) of dp[mask | bits] + op * gcd. Precompute pair gcds.

cards.name: Maximize the Beauty of the Garden
cards.trick: Keep the first and last flower equal in value, with everything in between kept only if positive. Prefix sum of positive values, and a map value -> first index. At each j with a seen value v at i, candidate = 2v + pos[j] - pos[i + 1] (the 2v counts even if v is negative).

cards.name: Maximize Y Sum by Picking a Triplet of Distinct X Values
cards.trick: Greedy. For each distinct x keep only its max y in a hash map. Take the 3 largest of those maxima. Return -1 if there are fewer than 3 distinct x values.

cards.name: Maximum Absolute Sum of Any Subarray
cards.trick: Run Kadane twice, once for the max subarray sum and once for the min subarray sum, and return max(maxSum, abs(minSum)). Equivalent: max prefix - min prefix (with the empty prefix 0 included).

cards.name: Maximum Alternating Subarray Sum
cards.trick: Kadane with two states per index. plus = best sum of a subarray ending here where nums[i] has a + sign = max(nums[i], minus_prev + nums[i]). minus = plus_prev - nums[i]. Answer is the max over every plus and minus seen.

cards.name: Maximum Alternating Subsequence Sum
cards.trick: Two states. even = best sum with an even count of picked elements so far, odd = with an odd count. For each x: even = max(even, odd - x), odd = max(odd, even + x) (use the old values). Answer is odd. Equivalent: sum of every rise between local valley and peak.

cards.name: Maximum Ascending Subarray Sum
cards.trick: One pass with a running sum. If nums[i] > nums[i - 1] add it, otherwise restart the running sum at nums[i]. Track the max running sum.

cards.name: Maximum Average Subarray II
cards.trick: Binary search on the answer avg. To test mid, subtract mid from every element and check for a subarray of length >= k with sum >= 0, using prefix sums and the min prefix among indices <= i - k. Stop when the range is below the 1e-5 tolerance.

cards.name: Maximum Average Subtree
cards.trick: Post-order DFS returning (sum, count) for each subtree. Compute each node's average from its children's results and keep a global max.

cards.name: Maximum Beauty of an Array After Applying Operation
cards.trick: Each value becomes any number in [x - k, x + k], so a set can share a value if max - min <= 2k. Sort and slide a window while nums[right] - nums[left] <= 2k. Answer is the largest window.

cards.name: Maximum Candies Allocated to K Children
cards.time: O(n log M) (M = max pile size)
cards.trick: Binary search on the candies per child m in [1, max pile]. Feasible if sum(pile // m) >= k, which is monotone. Return the largest feasible m, or 0 if none.

cards.name: Maximum Cost of Trip With K Highways
cards.trick: Bitmask DP dp[mask][last] = best cost of a path visiting the set mask and ending at last. Start from every city, extend along highways to an unvisited city, and answer is the max over states with popcount == k + 1. Return -1 if none.

cards.name: Maximum Difference Between Even and Odd Frequency I
cards.trick: Count character frequencies. Answer = max odd frequency - min even frequency over letters that appear.

cards.name: Maximum Distance in Arrays
cards.trick: Each array is sorted, so only its first and last element matter. Keep the global min and max seen over earlier arrays. For each new array try abs(last - min) and abs(max - first), then update min and max after, so both ends never come from the same array.

cards.name: Maximum Element After Decreasing and Rearranging
cards.trick: The answer is at most n. Counting sort with values capped at n, then walk v = 1..n keeping cur = min(cur + count[v], v). Final cur is the answer. (Sort then arr[i] = min(arr[i], arr[i - 1] + 1) is O(n log n).)

cards.name: Maximum Employees to Be Invited to a Meeting
cards.trick: Functional graph (each node points to its favorite). Two cases: one big cycle of length L, or the sum over all 2-cycles of 2 + the longest chain feeding each of the two nodes. Kahn topological sort from in-degree 0 nodes gives chain depths, and the leftover nodes are the cycles. Answer is the max of both cases.

cards.name: Maximum Frequency After Subarray Operation
cards.trick: Adding x to a subarray can turn any one value v into k. Answer = count of k + max over v != k of the best subarray sum where v is +1 and k is -1 (Kadane per v, empty allowed). The k's outside the chosen subarray stay counted.

cards.name: Maximum Frequency Stack
cards.trick: Map value -> count, a map freq -> stack of values, and a maxFreq variable. Push appends x to the stack for its new frequency. Pop takes from the stack at maxFreq and drops maxFreq when that stack empties. Ties resolve by recency automatically.

cards.name: Maximum Length of a Concatenated String with Unique Characters
cards.trick: Turn each word into a 26-bit mask and drop words with repeated letters. DFS over include or skip, only including a word when mask & cur == 0. Track the max popcount.

cards.name: Maximum Length of Pair Chain
cards.trick: Interval scheduling greedy. Sort pairs by end value, then take a pair whenever its start > the end of the last chosen pair. (DP after sorting by start is O(n^2).)

cards.name: Maximum Matrix Sum
cards.trick: Flipping two adjacent cells lets you move a negative sign anywhere. Sum the absolute values and count negatives. If the count is odd, one sign must stay negative, so subtract 2 * the smallest absolute value. Zeros absorb the sign for free.

cards.name: Maximum Nesting Depth of the Parentheses
cards.trick: No stack needed, just a counter. Increment on '(' and decrement on ')', tracking the max value reached.

cards.name: Maximum Number of Accepted Invitations
cards.trick: Maximum bipartite matching with Kuhn's augmenting paths. For each boy run a DFS that tries each liked girl, and if she is taken, tries to re-route her current match, using a visited set per DFS. (Hopcroft-Karp is O(m * n * sqrt(m + n)).)

cards.name: Maximum Number of Balloons
cards.trick: Count the letters of the text. Each balloon needs b, a, n once and l, o twice, so the answer is min(b, a, n, l // 2, o // 2).

cards.name: Maximum Number of Fish in a Grid
cards.trick: Flood fill each unvisited water cell (value > 0) with DFS or BFS, summing the fish of its connected component. Answer is the largest component sum, or 0.

cards.name: Maximum Number of K-Divisible Components
cards.trick: DFS from any root, returning each subtree sum mod k. If a subtree's sum is divisible by k, cut the edge to its parent and count a component. The total is divisible by k, so the last component is always valid. Answer = number of cuts + 1.

cards.name: Maximum Number of Ones
cards.trick: Only the top-left side x side tile matters since it repeats. Each tile cell repeats across the matrix a number of times that takes only 4 distinct values (floor or ceil of width / side times floor or ceil of height / side). Put the maxOnes ones on the highest-count cells. (Sorting all side^2 counts is O(side^2 log side).)

cards.name: Maximum Number of People That Can Be Caught in Tag
cards.trick: Two pointers, one over the catchers (1s) and one over the runners (0s). If |i - j| <= dist, catch and advance both. Otherwise advance whichever pointer is behind (smaller index).

cards.name: Maximum Number of Points From Grid Queries
cards.time: O(m * n * log(m * n) + q log q)
cards.trick: Sort queries ascending. Run a min-heap Prim-style flood from (0, 0): while the heap top is < the current query, pop it, count a point and push its unvisited neighbors. The count after each query is its answer, reusing earlier work.

cards.name: Maximum Number of Points with Cost
cards.trick: Row DP where new[j] = points[i][j] + max over k of (prev[k] - |j - k|). Compute the max with a left-to-right sweep (left[j] = max(prev[j], left[j - 1] - 1)) and a right-to-left sweep. That drops the inner loop from O(n) to O(1). (Naive is O(m * n^2).)

cards.name: Maximum Number of Removable Characters
cards.time: O(n * log r) (n = len(s), r = len(removable))
cards.trick: Binary search on k, the number of removals. Removing more only makes p harder to match, so it is monotone. To check k, mark the first k removable indices and test whether p is still a subsequence of s skipping them.

cards.name: Maximum Number of Vowels in a Substring of Given Length
cards.trick: Fixed-size window of length k. Add the vowel status of the entering char and subtract that of the char leaving, tracking the max count. Stop early if you hit k.

cards.name: Maximum Odd Binary Number
cards.trick: Count the ones. To be odd the last bit must be 1, so put one 1 at the end, the other ones - 1 at the front for the biggest value, and zeros in between.

cards.name: Maximum of Minimum Values in All Subarrays
