cards.trick: Monotonic stack to find, for each nums[i], the nearest smaller element on both sides. nums[i] is the min of windows up to length len = right - left - 1, so ans[len] = max(ans[len], nums[i]). Then fill from the right with ans[len] = max(ans[len], ans[len + 1]) since any larger window's answer also works for a smaller one.

cards.name: Maximum Performance of a Team
cards.trick: Sort engineers by efficiency descending so the current efficiency is the team minimum. Keep a min-heap of the k best speeds with a running speed sum. After adding each engineer (dropping the smallest speed if size > k) candidate = sum * current efficiency.

cards.name: Maximum Points You Can Obtain from Cards
cards.trick: Taking k cards from the two ends leaves a contiguous middle window of n - k cards. Minimize that window's sum with a fixed sliding window and return total - minWindow. (Or start with the first k and shift cards from the left side to the right.)

cards.name: Maximum Product Difference Between Two Pairs
cards.trick: The best pairs are the two largest and the two smallest values. Track max1, max2, min1, min2 in a single pass and return max1 * max2 - min1 * min2. (Sorting is O(n log n).)

cards.name: Maximum Product of the Length of Two Palindromic Subsequences
cards.trick: Bitmask every subsequence and precompute pal[mask] = length if that subsequence is a palindrome. Then for each palindromic mask loop over submasks of its complement and maximize pal[a] * pal[b]. Disjoint masks mean no shared characters.

cards.name: Maximum Profit From Trading Stocks
cards.trick: 0/1 knapsack. Weight = present[i], value = future[i] - present[i], skipping stocks with non-positive profit. Use a 1-D dp over budget, iterating the budget downward so each stock is used at most once.

cards.name: Maximum Profit in Job Scheduling
cards.trick: Sort jobs by end time. dp[i] = max(dp[i - 1], profit[i] + dp[j]) where j is the last job ending <= start[i], found with binary search over the sorted end times.

cards.name: Maximum Score After Splitting a String
cards.trick: Start with right = total ones. Sweep split points over indices 0..n-2, adding a zero to left or removing a one from right as each char moves over, and track the max left + right. Both halves must be non-empty.

cards.name: Maximum Score From Removing Substrings
cards.trick: Greedy: remove the higher-value pair ('ab' or 'ba') first with a stack, then remove the other pair from what is left. Taking the pricier pair first never costs more than it gains.

cards.name: Maximum Score of a Good Subarray
cards.trick: Start with l = r = k and the running min = nums[k]. Always expand toward the side with the larger next value, update min, and score = min * (r - l + 1). Keeping the min as high as possible for as long as possible is optimal.

cards.name: Maximum Score Words Formed by Letters
cards.time: O(2^n * L) (n words, L = max word length)
cards.trick: Backtrack include or skip for each word using a 26-slot letter budget. Include a word only if every letter count is still available, subtract on the way in and restore on the way out. Precompute each word's score.

cards.name: Maximum Size Subarray Sum Equals k
cards.trick: Prefix sum with a hash map of prefix -> FIRST index it appeared at. At each i, if prefix - k is in the map, length = i - map[prefix - k]. Never overwrite an existing key, and seed with {0: -1}.

cards.name: Maximum Subarray Min-Product
cards.trick: Prefix sums plus a monotonic increasing stack of indices. When a smaller element pops index i, the subarray where nums[i] is the min spans from the new stack top + 1 to the current index - 1. Candidate = nums[i] * range sum. Take the max and apply the modulo only at the end.

cards.name: Maximum Subarray Sum After One Operation
cards.trick: Kadane with two states. noSq = best sum ending here with no square used, withSq = best sum ending here with exactly one element squared. withSq = max(noSq_prev + x^2, withSq_prev + x, x^2). Answer is the max withSq.

cards.name: Maximum Subsequence Score
cards.trick: Sort pairs by nums2 descending so the current nums2 is the min of the chosen set. Keep a min-heap of the k largest nums1 values with a running sum. Once the heap holds k items, candidate = sum * current nums2.

cards.name: Maximum Sum Circular Subarray
cards.trick: Run Kadane for max and min subarray in one pass. A wrapping subarray is total - minSubarray. Answer is max(maxSub, total - minSub), but if all elements are negative (maxSub < 0) return maxSub.

cards.name: Maximum Sum of 3 Non-Overlapping Subarrays
cards.trick: Compute all length-k window sums. Build left[i] = best window start in [0, i] and right[i] = best window start in [i, end]. Fix the middle window j and combine sum[left[j - k]] + sum[j] + sum[right[j + k]]. Pick the earliest index on ties for lexicographic order.

cards.name: Maximum Sum of Distinct Subarrays With Length K
cards.trick: Fixed window of size k with a frequency map and running sum. When the map has k distinct keys (window of all unique values), update the best sum.

cards.name: Maximum Sum Score of Array
cards.trick: Score at i is max(prefix sum through i, suffix sum from i). Compute total, then sweep with a running prefix and suffix = total - prefix + nums[i], and take the max of both at each index.

cards.name: Maximum Swap
cards.trick: Record the last index of each digit 0-9. Scan left to right, and at position i look for a larger digit (9 down to nums[i] + 1) whose last index is after i. Swap with that last occurrence and stop. Using the last occurrence gives the biggest result.

cards.name: Maximum Total Importance of Roads
cards.trick: A city's importance contribution is value * degree, so give the largest values to the highest-degree cities. Count degrees, sort them ascending (counting sort keeps it linear) and sum degree * (rank + 1).

cards.name: Maximum Transactions Without Negative Balance
cards.trick: Process in order, adding each amount to the balance. Push negative amounts into a min-heap. When the balance drops below 0, pop the most negative amount from the heap (skip that transaction) and add it back. Answer is n minus the number skipped.

cards.name: Maximum Twin Sum of a Linked List
cards.trick: Find the middle with slow and fast pointers, reverse the second half in place, then walk both halves together summing paired nodes. Track the max. (Storing values in an array is O(n) space.)

cards.name: Maximum Vacation Days
cards.trick: DP over weeks: dp[c] = max vacation days if you spend the current week in city c. For each week, new[c] = days[c][week] + max(dp[p]) over cities p where p == c or flights[p][c] == 1. Start with only city 0 reachable and answer is the max at the end.

cards.name: Maximum Value of K Coins From Piles
cards.time: O(k * m) (m = total number of coins)
cards.trick: Knapsack over piles with prefix sums. dp[j] = best value using j coins from piles so far. For each pile try taking t = 0..min(len, k) top coins, giving dp[j] = max(dp[j - t] + prefix[t]). Iterate j downward to reuse a single array.

cards.name: Maximum Width of Binary Tree
cards.trick: BFS with heap-style indices (left = 2i, right = 2i + 1) and width = last index - first index + 1 per level. Subtract the level's first index from every index to avoid overflow.

cards.name: Maximum Width Ramp
cards.trick: Build a decreasing stack of indices from the left (only candidates for the left end of a ramp). Then sweep j from the right end and while nums[stack top] <= nums[j] pop it and update width = j - popped index. Popped left ends will not do better later.

cards.name: Maximum XOR for Each Query
cards.trick: The prefix XOR of the whole array is X. The best k < 2^b is X ^ (2^b - 1), which flips every bit within the width. After each query drop the last element by XORing it out of X, and answer from the end of the array backwards.

cards.name: Meeting Rooms III
cards.time: O(m log m + m log n) (m meetings, n rooms)
cards.trick: Sort meetings by start. Two heaps: a min-heap of free room ids and a min-heap of (end time, room) for busy rooms. Before each meeting free every room with end <= start. If none is free, take the earliest-ending room and delay the meeting by its remaining time. Count uses per room.

cards.name: Meeting Scheduler
cards.time: O(n log n + m log m)
cards.trick: Sort both people's slots by start and use two pointers. Overlap = [max(starts), min(ends)]. If its length >= duration return the first duration of it. Otherwise advance the pointer whose slot ends earlier.

cards.name: Merge In Between Linked Lists
cards.trick: Walk list1 to the node before index a and the node after index b. Link the first to the head of list2, walk to the tail of list2 and link it to the node after b.

cards.name: Merge Nodes in Between Zeros
cards.trick: Single pass keeping a running sum. On each 0 after the start, write the sum into the node, link it to the output and reset to 0. Reuse the existing nodes in place and drop the trailing zero.

cards.name: Merge Sorted Array
cards.trick: Fill nums1 from the back with three pointers (end of each array's data and the write index). Place the larger of the two tails each time. Writing from the back never overwrites unread data, and any leftover nums2 values get copied over.

cards.name: Merge Strings Alternately
cards.trick: One index walking both strings, appending word1[i] then word2[i] while either has chars left. When one runs out, append the rest of the other.

cards.name: Merge Two 2D Arrays by Summing Values
cards.trick: Both lists are sorted by id, so merge with two pointers. If ids match, add the values and advance both. Otherwise take the smaller id and advance that pointer. Append any leftovers.

cards.name: Merge Two Binary Trees
cards.trick: Recursive DFS. If either node is null return the other (reusing the whole subtree). Otherwise add the values into one node and merge the left and right children.

cards.name: Middle of the Linked List
cards.trick: Slow moves one step and fast moves two. When fast reaches the end slow is at the middle. Loop while fast and fast.next exist, which returns the second middle for even lengths.

cards.name: Minimize Deviation in Array
cards.time: O(n log n * log M) (M = max value)
cards.trick: First double every odd number so each element can only decrease by halving from then on (an odd can be doubled once, an even halved). Max heap with a tracked min. Repeatedly halve the max while it is even, update min and deviation, and stop when the max is odd.

cards.name: Minimize Max Distance to Gas Station
cards.trick: Binary search on the answer D over a real range. For each gap of length g you need ceil(g / D) - 1 new stations. D is feasible if the total needed <= k. Stop when the range is within the 1e-6 tolerance. (Max heap greedy is O(k log n).)

cards.name: Minimize Maximum of Array
cards.trick: Values can only move left to earlier indices, so the answer is the max over i of ceil(prefix_sum[i] / (i + 1)). It is the best you can do for each prefix by spreading evenly. (Binary search on the answer is O(n log M).)

cards.name: Minimize Product Sum of Two Arrays
cards.trick: Rearrangement inequality. Sort one array ascending and the other descending, so large values pair with small ones, then sum the products. (Counting sort gives O(n + V).)

cards.name: Minimize Rounding Error to Meet Target
cards.trick: Floor every price and sum. If sum of floors > target or sum of ceils < target return -1. You must ceil exactly k = target - floorSum prices, so ceil the ones with the largest fractional parts (cheapest error increase, error goes from f to 1 - f). Sum the errors.

cards.name: Minimize the Maximum Difference of Pairs
cards.time: O(n log n + n log M)
cards.trick: Sort. Binary search on the max allowed difference d. Greedily scan and pair adjacent elements whenever nums[i + 1] - nums[i] <= d (then skip both). Feasible if pairs >= p.

cards.name: Minimize XOR
cards.trick: Let c = popcount(num2). Fill x from the highest set bits of num1 first (they cancel in the XOR) up to c bits. If bits remain, set the lowest unset bits. That minimizes the XOR.

cards.name: Minimized Maximum of Products Distributed to Any Store
cards.time: O(m * log M) (m product types, M = max quantity)
cards.trick: Binary search on x, the max products per store. Each product type with quantity q needs ceil(q / x) stores. x is feasible if the sum <= n. Find the smallest feasible x.

cards.name: Minimum Add to Make Parentheses Valid
cards.trick: Counter instead of a stack. Track open count. On ')' with open > 0 decrement it, otherwise count an unmatched close (one added '('). Answer = unmatched closes + leftover opens.

cards.name: Minimum Array End
cards.trick: Every element must contain all set bits of x. The smallest increasing sequence enumerates the 'free' zero bit positions of x as a counter, so write the bits of (n - 1) into the zero bits of x from low to high. The result is the last element.

cards.name: Minimum Bit Flips to Convert Number
cards.trick: XOR the two numbers so differing bits become 1, then count set bits. Use x &= x - 1 to clear the lowest set bit each loop.

cards.name: Minimum Changes To Make Alternating Binary String
cards.trick: Only two target strings exist, 0101... and 1010.... Count the mismatches c against 0101... and the other target needs n - c. Answer is min(c, n - c).

cards.name: Minimum Cost For Tickets
cards.time: O(D) (D = last travel day, at most 365)
cards.trick: dp[d] = min cost to cover travel through day d. If d is not a travel day dp[d] = dp[d - 1]. Otherwise dp[d] = min(dp[d - 1] + c1, dp[d - 7] + c7, dp[d - 30] + c30) with indices clamped at 0.

cards.name: Minimum Cost to Connect Sticks
cards.trick: Huffman-style greedy. Min-heap: pop the two smallest sticks, add their sum to the cost and push the sum back. Repeat until one stick remains. Merging small ones first keeps them from being re-counted.

cards.name: Minimum Cost to Convert String I
cards.trick: Only 26 letters, so build a 26 x 26 cost matrix from the rules (keeping the cheapest edge for a pair) and run Floyd-Warshall. Then sum dist[source[i]][target[i]] over positions and return -1 if any pair is unreachable.

cards.name: Minimum Cost to Cut a Stick
cards.trick: Interval DP. Sort cuts and add 0 and n as endpoints. dp[i][j] = min over k in (i, j) of dp[i][k] + dp[k][j] + (cuts[j] - cuts[i]), where k is the LAST cut made on that segment.

cards.name: Minimum Cost to Hire K Workers
cards.trick: Sort workers by wage/quality ratio. Sweeping up, the current ratio is the group's pay rate. Keep a max-heap of the k smallest qualities (pop the largest when size > k). Cost = ratio * sum of heap qualities.

cards.name: Minimum Cost to Make at Least One Valid Path in a Grid
cards.trick: 0-1 BFS with a deque. Moving along the cell's arrow costs 0 (push front), any other direction costs 1 (push back). Equivalent to Dijkstra with only two edge weights.

cards.name: Minimum Cost to Reach City With Discounts
cards.trick: Dijkstra on the state (city, discounts used). From each state either pay the full toll or, if discounts remain, pay toll // 2 and use one. Answer is the min cost over all discount counts at the destination.

cards.name: Minimum Cost to Separate Sentence Into Rows
cards.time: O(n * k) (n words, k = row width)
cards.trick: dp[i] = min cost to place words i..end. Extend a row word by word while length (with single spaces) <= k, cost (k - len)^2 + dp[next]. The last row costs 0, so if the rest fits in one row dp[i] = 0.

cards.name: Minimum Cost Walk in Weighted Graph
cards.trick: A walk can reuse edges, and AND only decreases, so the best cost is the AND of ALL edge weights in the connected component. Union-find, AND every edge into its root, answer each query as that value (0 if s == t, -1 if different components).

cards.name: Minimum Deletions to Make Character Frequencies Unique
cards.trick: Count frequencies. For each, while its count is > 0 and already used, decrement it and add one deletion. Mark the final count as used. (Sorting frequencies descending also works.)

cards.name: Minimum Deletions to Make String Balanced
cards.trick: One pass. Track countB (b's seen) and res. On 'b' increment countB. On 'a', either delete this a (res + 1) or delete all earlier b's (countB): res = min(res + 1, countB).

cards.name: Minimum Difference Between Highest and Lowest of K Scores
cards.trick: Sort, then the best k scores are a contiguous window. Answer = min over i of nums[i + k - 1] - nums[i].

cards.name: Minimum Difference Between Largest and Smallest Value in Three Moves
cards.trick: If n <= 4 return 0. Otherwise sort and change 3 values total by removing some from the small end and the rest from the large end. Answer = min over i in 0..3 of nums[n - 4 + i] - nums[i]. (Keeping the 4 smallest and 4 largest via a heap is O(n).)

cards.name: Minimum Difficulty of a Job Schedule
cards.time: O(n * d) with a monotonic stack (O(n^2 * d) with the plain DP)
cards.trick: If n < d return -1. dp[day][i] = min cost to finish the first i jobs in day days. Plain version scans backwards for the last day's max difficulty. The fast version keeps a monotonic stack of (max, best dp) per day.

cards.name: Minimum Distance Between BST Nodes
cards.trick: Inorder traversal of a BST visits values in sorted order, so the minimum difference is between adjacent nodes. Keep the previous value and update the min at each node.

cards.name: Minimum Factorization
cards.trick: Greedy: for d from 9 down to 2, divide a by d while divisible, collecting digits. If a ends > 1 return 0. Reverse the digits for the smallest number. Return 0 if the result exceeds 2^31 - 1. Handle a < 10 directly.

cards.name: Minimum Falling Path Sum
cards.space: O(1) (in place) or O(n) with a row array
cards.trick: Go row by row. matrix[r][c] += min of the three cells above it (c - 1, c, c + 1 in bounds). Answer is the min of the last row.

cards.name: Minimum Falling Path Sum II
cards.trick: For each row, the best previous cell in a different column is the row's smallest value unless you are in that column, then it is the second smallest. Track only the two smallest values (and the column of the smallest) per row. (Naive DP is O(n^3).)

cards.name: Minimum Fuel Cost to Report to the Capital
cards.trick: DFS from city 0 returning subtree size. Every edge from a child to its parent carries size people, needing ceil(size / seats) car trips, so add that to the answer for each non-root node.

cards.name: Minimum Health to Beat Game
cards.trick: Use the armor on the level with the largest damage, saving min(armor, maxDamage). Answer = sum(damage) - min(armor, max(damage)) + 1. The +1 is because health must stay above 0.

cards.name: Minimum Height Trees
cards.trick: Peel leaves layer by layer, like topological sort on degree 1 nodes. The last 1 or 2 nodes remaining are the centers of the tree. Handle n <= 2 up front. (Rerooting DFS from every node is O(n^2).)

cards.name: Minimum Increment to Make Array Unique
cards.trick: Sort, then walk left to right. If nums[i] <= nums[i - 1], raise it to nums[i - 1] + 1 and add the difference to the answer. (Counting sort over values gives O(n + max).)

cards.name: Minimum Index of a Valid Split
cards.trick: The array has exactly one dominant element, which must also dominate both sides of any valid split. Find it with Boyer-Moore voting and count its total. Scan split points keeping a prefix count, and check count * 2 > length on both sides.

cards.name: Minimum Knight Moves
cards.trick: BFS from the origin with a visited set. Use symmetry: take abs(x) and abs(y) so you only explore the first quadrant (allow a small margin like -1 or -2 below zero). Shortest path in an unweighted graph is BFS.

cards.name: Minimum Length of String After Deleting Similar Ends
cards.trick: Pointers l and r. While l < r and s[l] == s[r], strip every run of that character from both ends (move l right and r left while they match). Answer is r - l + 1. Stop as soon as the ends differ.

cards.name: Minimum Length of String After Operations
cards.trick: Each operation removes a pair of the same letter (one left, one right of a middle one), so each letter reduces by 2 until at most 2 remain. Count frequencies: a letter with odd count leaves 1, with even positive count leaves 2.

cards.name: Minimum Limit of Balls in a Bag
cards.trick: Binary search the answer (max bag size) from 1 to max(nums). Operations needed for a limit x is sum((num - 1) // x). Feasible if that is <= maxOperations. Find the smallest feasible x.

cards.name: Minimum Number of Arrows to Burst Balloons
cards.trick: Sort by end coordinate. Shoot at the first balloon's end, then every balloon starting at or before that point is burst. A balloon starting after it needs a new arrow at its own end. Compare with <= for touching ends.

cards.name: Minimum Number of Changes to Make Binary String Beautiful
cards.trick: A beautiful string is made of even-length runs of equal chars, which means every aligned pair (2i, 2i + 1) must match. Count the pairs where s[2i] != s[2i + 1]. Each needs exactly one flip.

cards.name: Minimum Number of Days to Disconnect Island
cards.time: O(m * n) with articulation points (O((m * n)^2) trying every cell)
cards.trick: Answer is only 0, 1 or 2. If the grid is not exactly one island, 0. If there is one land cell that is an articulation point (or only 1 land cell), 1. Otherwise 2. Brute force: remove each land cell and recount islands.

cards.name: Minimum Number of Days to Eat N Oranges
cards.trick: Memoized recursion. Only two useful moves are halving or thirding, with single-orange eats just to fix the remainder: f(n) = 1 + min(n % 2 + f(n // 2), n % 3 + f(n // 3)). Only O(log^2 n) distinct states are reached.

cards.name: Minimum Number of Flips to Make the Binary String Alternating
cards.trick: Type-1 rotations are free, so double the string (s + s) and slide a window of length n. Keep mismatch counts against '0101...' and '1010...' patterns, update as the window moves, and take the min over all windows and both patterns.

cards.name: Minimum Number of Increments on Subarrays to Form a Target Array
cards.trick: Each time target rises above the previous element, you must start new increments for the difference. Answer = target[0] + sum of max(0, target[i] - target[i - 1]).

cards.name: Minimum Number of K Consecutive Bit Flips
cards.space: O(1) (mark flips in place) or O(n)
cards.trick: Greedy left to right: if the current bit, after the flips covering it, is 0, you must flip the window starting here. Track the number of active flips with a running parity that drops off after k positions. If a flip would run past the end return -1.

cards.name: Minimum Number of Keypresses
cards.trick: 9 keys, 26 letters. Sort letter frequencies descending: the top 9 need 1 press, the next 9 need 2, the rest need 3. Sum freq * presses.

cards.name: Minimum Number of Lines to Cover Points
cards.trick: n <= 10, so bitmask DP. Precompute, for each pair (i, j), the mask of all points on their line (cross product check). dp[mask] = min lines: take the lowest unset point i, then either use a line through i and each j, or a line through i alone.

cards.name: Minimum Number of Moves to Seat Everyone
cards.trick: Sort seats and students, then match the i-th smallest to the i-th smallest. Answer = sum of |seats[i] - students[i]|. (Counting sort makes it O(n + max).)

cards.name: Minimum Number of Operations to Make Array Continuous
cards.trick: Duplicates must be replaced, so dedupe and sort. A continuous array fits in a value range of length n. Slide a window on the unique sorted values with max - min <= n - 1. Answer = n - (max unique values kept in a window).

cards.name: Minimum Number of Operations to Make Array Empty
cards.trick: Count frequencies. A count of 1 is impossible (return -1). Otherwise any count >= 2 can be split into 2s and 3s with ceil(count / 3) operations. Sum those.

cards.name: Minimum Number of Operations to Move All Balls to Each Box
cards.trick: Two passes. Moving from box i to i + 1 adds one move for every ball on the left (ballsLeft) side. Sweep left to right accumulating moves += ballsSoFar, then right to left the same way, adding into the answer.

cards.name: Minimum Number of Operations to Sort a Binary Tree by Level
cards.trick: BFS by level. For each level the min swaps to sort the values is (length - number of cycles) in the permutation to the sorted order. Get the target positions by sorting and map values to indices (values are unique).

cards.name: Minimum Number of Pushes to Type Word II
cards.trick: 8 keys, so the top 8 most frequent letters cost 1 push, the next 8 cost 2, and so on. Sort frequencies descending and add freq * (rank // 8 + 1).

cards.name: Minimum Number of Removals to Make Mountain Array
cards.time: O(n log n) (O(n^2) with the simple DP)
cards.trick: Compute the LIS ending at i (left) and the LDS starting at i (right). A valid peak i needs left[i] > 1 and right[i] > 1. Answer = n - max(left[i] + right[i] - 1) over valid peaks.

cards.name: Minimum Number of Swaps to Make the String Balanced
cards.trick: Scan with an open-bracket counter. A ']' with no open to match is unmatched (count it). Each swap fixes two unmatched pairs, so answer = (unmatched + 1) // 2.

cards.name: Minimum Number of Vertices to Reach All Nodes
cards.trick: In a DAG every node with indegree 0 must be a starting point, and those alone reach everything. Return all nodes that never appear as an edge target.

cards.name: Minimum Obstacle Removal to Reach Corner
cards.trick: 0-1 BFS with a deque: stepping into an empty cell costs 0 (push front), into an obstacle costs 1 (push back). Distance to the bottom-right corner is the answer. (Dijkstra is O(m * n log(m * n)).)

cards.name: Minimum One Bit Operations to Make Integers Zero
cards.trick: The sequence of states is the reflected Gray code, so the answer is the inverse Gray code of n: res = n; res ^= res >> 1; res ^= res >> 2; ... (or XOR all prefix shifts). Recursive form: f(n) = 2^(k+1) - 1 - f(n - 2^k) for the top bit k.

cards.name: Minimum Operations to Make a Uni-Value Grid
cards.trick: Flatten. If any two values differ by a non-multiple of x, return -1. Otherwise the best target is the median (minimizes sum of absolute differences). Answer = sum of |v - median| / x. (Quickselect gives O(m * n).)

cards.name: Minimum Operations to Make Binary Array Elements Equal to One I
cards.trick: Left to right, the first 0 can only be fixed by flipping the 3-window starting there. Flip it and count. If a 0 remains in the last two positions at the end return -1. A running flip parity avoids re-touching the window.

cards.name: Minimum Operations to Reduce X to Zero
cards.trick: Removing from the ends leaves a contiguous middle subarray. Find the LONGEST subarray with sum total - x using a sliding window (all values positive). Answer = n - that length, or -1 if none.

cards.name: Minimum Operations to Remove Adjacent Ones in Matrix
cards.time: O(E * sqrt(V)) with Hopcroft-Karp (V = m * n cells)
cards.trick: Treat adjacent 1s as edges. The grid is bipartite by (r + c) parity, so the minimum vertex cover equals the maximum matching (Konig's theorem). Answer = max bipartite matching.

cards.name: Minimum Path Sum
cards.trick: dp[r][c] = grid[r][c] + min(dp[r - 1][c], dp[r][c - 1]). First row and column only have one predecessor. Keep a single row to save space.

cards.name: Minimum Penalty for a Shop
cards.trick: Prefix-sum scan over closing times. Start at closing hour 0 (penalty = number of 'Y'). Moving the closing time past hour i changes the penalty by -1 for a 'Y' and +1 for an 'N'. Track the running value and return the earliest index with the minimum.

cards.name: Minimum Recolors to Get K Consecutive Black Blocks
cards.trick: Fixed-size window of length k. Count the white blocks ('W') inside it, since each one must be recolored. Answer is the minimum white count over all windows.

cards.name: Minimum Remove to Make Valid Parentheses
cards.trick: Stack of indices of unmatched '('. On ')', pop if the stack is non-empty, otherwise mark that index for removal. Leftover indices on the stack are also removed. Rebuild the string skipping marked indices.

cards.name: Minimum Score of a Path Between Two Cities
cards.trick: A path may revisit nodes and edges, so any edge in the connected component of city 1 is usable. Run BFS/DFS (or union-find) from 1 and return the smallest edge weight in that component.

cards.name: Minimum Size Subarray Sum
cards.trick: All values are positive, so grow the right end, and while the window sum >= target record its length and shrink from the left. Return 0 if never reached. (Prefix sums + binary search is O(n log n).)

cards.name: Minimum String Length After Removing Substrings
cards.trick: Stack. For each char, if the stack top plus this char forms 'AB' or 'CD', pop instead of pushing. Answer is the final stack size.

cards.name: Minimum Sum of Squared Difference
cards.trick: Only d_i = |a_i - b_i| matters and you have k = k1 + k2 total reductions. Always shrink the largest differences. Bucket counts by value and lower the top level down level by level, spending k, then sum squares. (A max-heap is O(k log n), too slow.)

cards.name: Minimum Swaps to Group All 1's Together
cards.trick: Let ones = total number of 1s. Slide a fixed window of length ones and find the window holding the most 1s. Swaps needed = ones - max ones in a window.

cards.name: Minimum Swaps to Group All 1's Together II
cards.trick: Same as the linear version, but the array is circular. Slide a window of length ones over the array with indices taken mod n (or doubled). Answer = ones - max ones in any window.

cards.name: Minimum Time Difference
cards.trick: Convert times to minutes. If n > 1440 there is a duplicate, return 0. Mark the minutes in a 1440 array, scan for adjacent differences, and also check the wraparound first + 1440 - last.

cards.name: Minimum Time for K Virus Variants to Spread
cards.time: O(n log n * log C) (C = max coordinate)
cards.trick: Binary search the day d. Each point covers a Manhattan diamond of radius d, which becomes a square after rotating coordinates to (x + y, x - y). Check if any point is covered by >= k squares with a sweep line plus a segment tree or difference array over compressed coordinates.

cards.name: Minimum Time to Build Blocks
cards.trick: Huffman-style merging with a min-heap. Pop the two smallest blocks a <= b, merge them into one block of cost split + b (the two workers split first, then the longer one dominates). Repeat until one value remains.

cards.name: Minimum Time to Collect All Apples in a Tree
cards.trick: DFS from node 0. For each child, if its subtree has any apple (or the child itself does), add 2 for the edge to and from it, plus the child's cost. Subtrees with no apples are skipped.

cards.name: Minimum Time to Make Rope Colorful
cards.trick: In every run of the same color keep the balloon with the largest removal time and remove the rest. Per run cost = run sum - run max. One pass, comparing each balloon to the previous.

cards.name: Minimum Time to Repair Cars
cards.trick: Binary search the total time t. A mechanic with rank r fixes floor(sqrt(t / r)) cars. Feasible if the sum across mechanics is >= cars. Upper bound is min(rank) * cars^2.

cards.name: Minimum Time to Visit a Cell in a Grid
cards.trick: Dijkstra on arrival time. You cannot wait in place, so you can bounce between two cells to burn time in pairs. Arrival at a neighbor = max(t + 1, grid[nr][nc]), bumped by 1 if its parity differs from (t + 1). If both cells next to the start are > 1, return -1.

cards.name: Minimum Unique Word Abbreviation
cards.time: O(2^m * (m + n)) (m = target length, n = dictionary size)
cards.trick: Only dictionary words with the same length matter. Represent each as a bitmask of positions where it matches the target. An abbreviation is a mask of kept letters, and it is unique if no dictionary word's match mask contains it. Try masks and keep the shortest abbreviation length.

cards.name: Minimum Window Subsequence
cards.trick: Scan s forward matching t's characters in order until all matched at end index e. Then scan backward from e matching t in reverse to find the tightest start. Record the window and continue from start + 1. (DP over positions is also O(n * m).)

cards.name: Missing Element in Sorted Array
cards.trick: missing(i) = nums[i] - nums[0] - i counts missing numbers before index i, and it is non-decreasing. Binary search the last index with missing(i) < k, then the answer is nums[idx] + k - missing(idx).

cards.name: Missing Number in Arithmetic Progression
cards.trick: The common difference is d = (last - first) / n. Binary search for the first index where arr[i] != first + i * d. The missing value is first + i * d. (Expected sum formula is O(n).)

cards.name: Missing Ranges
cards.trick: Walk through nums with prev = lower - 1. If num - prev >= 2, the range [prev + 1, num - 1] is missing. Update prev = num. After the loop do the same check against upper + 1. Format a single-number range as just that number.

cards.name: Monotonic Array
cards.trick: One pass with two flags, increasing and decreasing. Any rise clears decreasing, any fall clears increasing. Monotonic if either flag survives.

cards.name: Most Beautiful Item for Each Query
cards.trick: Sort items by price and turn beauty into a running prefix max. For each query, binary search the last item with price <= query and read its prefix max beauty (0 if none).

cards.name: Most Profitable Path in a Tree
cards.trick: First DFS/BFS from Bob (node bob) up to the root to record Bob's arrival time at each node on his path. Then DFS from node 0 tracking Alice's time. Add full amount if Alice arrives earlier, half if tied, none if later. Answer is the best leaf sum.

cards.name: Move Zeroes
cards.trick: Write pointer w for the next non-zero slot. Scan with r, and when nums[r] != 0 swap nums[w] and nums[r] and advance w. Order of non-zeros is preserved.

cards.name: Moving Average From Data Stream
cards.trick: Queue of the last size values plus a running sum. On each value add to the sum, push, and if the queue is over size pop the front and subtract it. Average = sum / queue length.

cards.name: My Calendar I
cards.time: O(log n) per book with a sorted structure (O(n) with a plain list)
cards.trick: Half-open intervals [start, end) overlap iff start < other_end and end > other_start. Keep bookings in a sorted order (balanced BST or sorted list with bisect) and only compare the new event with its neighbors.

cards.name: My Calendar II
cards.trick: Keep two lists: all bookings and double-booked overlaps. A new event fails if it overlaps any existing double booking. Otherwise add the overlap with every booking to the overlaps list, then add the event.

cards.name: N-ary Tree Postorder Traversal
cards.trick: Iterative: stack, pop a node, append its value, push its children left to right. That gives root, right...left order, so reverse the result at the end. Recursive version is also O(n) time, O(h) stack.

cards.name: N-Queens II
cards.trick: Place one queen per row. Track used columns and the two diagonals (r - c and r + c) in sets or bitmasks. Count a solution when all n rows are filled. No need to build boards.

cards.name: N-th Tribonacci Number
cards.trick: Keep only the last three values and roll them forward: next = a + b + c. Base cases T0 = 0, T1 = 1, T2 = 1. (Matrix exponentiation is O(log n).)

cards.name: Naming a Company
cards.time: O(n * L) (L = max word length; the 26 x 26 letter loop is constant)
cards.trick: Group suffixes (word minus first letter) by first letter. For each pair of letters (a, b), count suffixes shared between the groups. Valid pairs = 2 * (|A| - shared) * (|B| - shared). A swap is valid only if neither new word is already in the set.

cards.name: Neighboring Bitwise XOR
cards.trick: Every original element appears in exactly two derived values (wrapping around), so XOR of all derived values must be 0. A valid original array exists iff that XOR is 0.

cards.name: Nested List Weight Sum
cards.trick: DFS with a depth parameter starting at 1. An integer adds value * depth, a nested list recurses with depth + 1.

cards.name: Nested List Weight Sum II
cards.trick: Weights are inverted (leaves weigh 1). BFS level by level keeping a running unweighted sum of all integers seen so far, and add it to the total after each level. Each integer is thus counted once per level at or below its depth.

cards.name: New 21 Game
cards.trick: dp[i] = probability of reaching score i. dp[i] = (sum of dp[i - maxPts .. i - 1] restricted to scores < k) / maxPts. Maintain that as a sliding window sum. Answer = sum of dp[k..n]. If k == 0 or n >= k + maxPts - 1 return 1.

cards.name: Next Closest Time
cards.trick: Only the 4 given digits may be used. Scan from the last digit to the first and replace each with the next larger allowed digit if the time stays valid (hour < 24, minute < 60), filling the later positions with the smallest digit. If none works, wrap to the smallest digit everywhere.

cards.name: Next Greater Element I
cards.trick: Monotonic decreasing stack over nums2. When a bigger number arrives, pop smaller ones and record next_greater[popped] = current in a hash map. Then answer each query from nums1 by map lookup (default -1).

cards.name: Next Palindrome Using Same Digits
cards.trick: A palindrome is determined by its first half. Run next permutation on the first n // 2 digits, and return an empty string if there is none. Mirror the new half (keep the middle digit if n is odd).

cards.name: Next Permutation
cards.trick: Find the rightmost i with nums[i] < nums[i + 1]. Swap nums[i] with the rightmost element greater than it, then reverse the suffix after i. If no such i exists, just reverse the whole array.

cards.name: Non-decreasing Array
cards.trick: On the first violation nums[i - 1] > nums[i], prefer lowering nums[i - 1] to nums[i] if i < 2 or nums[i - 2] <= nums[i]. Otherwise raise nums[i] to nums[i - 1]. A second violation means false.

cards.name: Number of Atoms
cards.trick: Stack of count maps. '(' pushes a new map. ')' reads the following multiplier, multiplies the top map, and merges it into the one below. Parse names (uppercase + lowercase) and numbers. Finally sort atoms alphabetically for output.

cards.name: Number of Closed Islands
cards.trick: First flood fill every 0 (land) touching the border so those cannot be closed. Then count connected components of remaining 0s with DFS/BFS.

cards.name: Number of Corner Rectangles
cards.time: O(m^2 * n) (transpose so m is the smaller side)
cards.trick: For each pair of rows, count the columns where both have a 1, call it c. Those columns form c * (c - 1) / 2 rectangles. (Or per row, count 1-column pairs in a hash map, adding the old count as you go.)

cards.name: Number of Days in a Month
cards.trick: Lookup table of month lengths. February has 29 days iff the year is a leap year: divisible by 4 and (not divisible by 100 or divisible by 400).

cards.name: Number of Dice Rolls With Target Sum
cards.time: O(n * target) (O(n * k * target) without the window trick)
cards.trick: dp[d][t] = ways to reach sum t with d dice = sum of dp[d - 1][t - f] for f in 1..k. Use a rolling sum or prefix sums so each cell is O(1). Keep only the previous row. Everything mod 1e9 + 7.

cards.name: Number of Distinct Islands
cards.trick: DFS each island and record its shape as the cells' coordinates relative to the first cell (or a direction path string with backtrack markers). Add to a set. The set size is the answer.

cards.name: Number of Distinct Islands II
cards.trick: Same as Distinct Islands, but shapes equal under rotation or reflection. For each island generate all 8 transforms (swap, negate x/y), sort cells, translate so the smallest is at the origin, and take the lexicographically smallest as the canonical form.

cards.name: Number of Distinct Substrings in a String
cards.time: O(n) with a suffix automaton (O(n^2) with a trie of all suffixes)
cards.trick: Distinct substrings = number of paths in the suffix automaton, which is the sum over states of len[v] - len[link[v]]. Simple version: insert every suffix into a trie and count nodes. (Suffix array + LCP gives n(n + 1)/2 - sum(LCP).)

cards.name: Number of Divisible Triplet Sums
cards.trick: Fix the middle index j and iterate k > j, looking up how many earlier i < j have nums[i] % d == (-(nums[j] + nums[k])) % d in a frequency map. After finishing j, add nums[j] % d to the map. (Brute force is O(n^3).)

cards.name: Number of Enclaves
cards.trick: Flood fill from every land cell on the border (multi-source DFS/BFS) and mark them visited. Count the land cells that were never reached.

cards.name: Number of Equal Count Substrings
cards.trick: For each number of distinct letters u from 1 to 26, the substring length is fixed at u * count. Slide that window with a frequency array and track how many letters have exactly count occurrences. If that equals u, it is a valid substring.

cards.name: Number of Flowers in Full Bloom
cards.trick: Sort start times and end times separately. Flowers in bloom at time t = (# starts <= t) - (# ends < t) = bisect_right(starts, t) - bisect_left(ends, t). (Sweep line with a sorted queries list also works.)

cards.name: Number of Good Leaf Nodes Pairs
cards.trick: Post-order DFS returning an array cnt[i] = number of leaves at distance i below this node. At each node, for every pair (i, j) with i + j <= d count left[i] * right[j]. Then shift distances by 1 for the parent. A leaf returns cnt[0] = 1.

cards.name: Number of Good Pairs
cards.trick: Hash map of counts. For each x, add the number of times x has been seen before to the answer (each earlier equal element forms a pair), then increment its count.

cards.name: Number of Good Paths
cards.trick: Union-find, processing nodes by increasing value. For each node v, union with neighbors whose value <= vals[v]. Then in each component count how many nodes with value vals[v] it holds, k. New good paths = k * (k - 1) / 2, plus n single-node paths.

cards.name: Number of Islands II
cards.time: O(k * alpha(m * n)), about O(k) for k land operations
cards.trick: Union-Find over the m x n grid. For each addLand, skip it if already land (duplicate position), otherwise count +1 island, then union with each land neighbor and subtract 1 for every union that actually merged two roots.

cards.name: Number of Laser Beams in a Bank
cards.trick: Count the 1s in each row and skip rows with zero devices. Beams = sum of count(prev nonzero row) * count(current nonzero row) over consecutive nonzero rows.

cards.name: Number of Longest Increasing Subsequence
cards.trick: For each i keep len[i] (LIS length ending at i) and cnt[i] (how many such LIS). For j < i with nums[j] < nums[i]: if len[j] + 1 > len[i] take len and copy cnt[j]; if equal add cnt[j]. Sum cnt over i where len[i] equals the global max. (Fenwick/segment tree is O(n log n).)

cards.name: Number of Music Playlists
cards.trick: dp[i][j] = playlists of length i using exactly j distinct songs. Last song is new: dp[i-1][j-1] * (n - j + 1). Last song is a repeat: dp[i-1][j] * max(j - k, 0), since only songs outside the last k are replayable. Answer dp[goal][n] mod 1e9+7.

cards.name: Number of Pairs of Interchangeable Rectangles
cards.time: O(n) with a float ratio key (O(n log M) with gcd reduction)
cards.trick: Hash map of width/height ratio -> count. Each new rectangle adds the current count of its ratio to the answer (pairs formed), then increments it. Reduce by gcd to avoid float issues.

cards.name: Number of People That Can Be Seen in a Grid
cards.trick: Monotonic stack, run once along every row (left to right) and once along every column (top to bottom), like Number of Visible People in a Queue. Each person pops shorter people (each counted as seen) and sees the first taller-or-equal one left on the stack; skip duplicate equal heights so a pair is counted once.

cards.name: Number of Provinces
cards.trick: Connected components on an n x n adjacency matrix. DFS or BFS from each unvisited city marking everything reachable, count the starts. (Union-Find gives the same bound.)

cards.name: Number of Senior Citizens
cards.trick: Age sits at fixed positions 11 and 12 of each 15-char detail string. Parse int(s[11:13]) and count those greater than 60.

cards.name: Number of Ships in a Rectangle
cards.time: O(S * log(max(W, H))) for S ships
cards.trick: Divide and conquer: if hasShips(rectangle) is false return 0, if it is a single point return 1, else split into 4 quadrants and recurse. Pruning empty quadrants limits calls since each ship lives in only one rectangle per level.

cards.name: Number of Single Divisor Triplets
cards.time: O(n + V^3) with V = 100, effectively O(n)
cards.trick: Values are only 1..100, so count occurrences, then loop over value triples a <= b <= c with count multiplicities (a == b, b == c cases use choose-2 and similar). A triple qualifies if the sum is divisible by exactly one of its three values.

cards.name: Number of Spaces Cleaning Robot Cleaned
cards.trick: Simulate the robot: move forward if in bounds and empty, otherwise turn right. Track visited (row, col, direction) states and stop when a state repeats. Count distinct cells cleaned, at most 4 states per cell.

cards.name: Number of Students Unable to Eat Lunch
cards.trick: Order of the queue does not matter, only counts of each preference. Walk the sandwich stack: if no student wants the top sandwich, stop and return the students still left. Otherwise decrement that count.

cards.name: Number of Sub-arrays of Size K and Average Greater than or Equal to Threshold
cards.trick: Fixed-size window of k with a running sum. Compare the sum to k * threshold to avoid division. Add the new element and subtract the one leaving.

cards.name: Number of Sub-arrays With Odd Sum
cards.trick: Prefix sum parity. A subarray sum is odd when its two prefix parities differ, so at each index add the count of earlier prefixes with the opposite parity. Start with one even prefix (empty). Mod 1e9+7.

cards.name: Number of Submatrices That Sum to Target
cards.time: O(m^2 * n) (choose the smaller dimension as m)
cards.trick: Build row-wise prefix sums. Fix a pair of rows (or column pair), collapse to a 1-D array of column sums, then run Subarray Sum Equals K with a hash map of prefix -> count. Initialize count[0] = 1 for every row pair.

cards.name: Number of Subsequences That Satisfy the Given Sum Condition
cards.trick: Order does not matter for subsequences, so sort. Two pointers l, r: if nums[l] + nums[r] <= target, nums[l] is the min and any subset of the r - l elements between works, add 2^(r-l) and l++; else r--. Precompute powers of 2 mod 1e9+7.

cards.name: Number of Substrings Containing All Three Characters
cards.trick: Track the last index of a, b, c. At each r, once all three have appeared, every start index from 0 to min(last_a, last_b, last_c) gives a valid substring ending at r, so add min(last) + 1. (Shrinking-window version is also O(n).)

cards.name: Number of Unique Flavors After Sharing K Candies
cards.trick: Count all flavors, then slide a window of size k that is the candies given away: removing a candy decrements its count (unique -1 if it hits 0), the leaving candy increments it back. Max unique over all windows.

cards.name: Number of Valid Subarrays
cards.trick: Valid means the first element is <= all others. Keep an increasing monotonic stack: pop while top > nums[i], push nums[i], and add stack size to the answer (each stack element is a valid start ending at i).

cards.name: Number of Visible People in a Queue
cards.trick: Scan from the right with a decreasing monotonic stack. Each person pops every shorter person (each one visible), then if the stack is still non-empty add 1 for the first taller person. Push the current height.

cards.name: Number of Ways to Arrive at Destination
cards.trick: Dijkstra that also counts shortest paths. When a strictly shorter dist to v is found set ways[v] = ways[u]; when an equal dist is found add ways[u]. Mod 1e9+7. Use long for distances.

cards.name: Number of Ways to Build House of Cards
cards.trick: A row of t triangles uses 3t - 1 cards, and rows must have strictly decreasing triangle counts upward. So pick distinct t values whose card costs sum to exactly n: 0/1 knapsack where dp[c] += dp[c - (3t - 1)] for t = 1..n/3, iterating c downward. dp[0] = 1.

cards.name: Number of Ways to Build Sturdy Brick Wall
cards.time: O(R^2 * height) where R = valid row patterns
cards.trick: Backtrack to enumerate every row pattern of bricks summing to the width and store each as a bitmask of crack positions. Two rows can stack if their masks share no bit. dp[h][row] = sum of dp[h-1][compatible rows]. Width is at most 10 so R is small.

cards.name: Number of Ways to Divide a Long Corridor
cards.trick: Each section needs exactly 2 seats, so the seat count must be even and nonzero. Between seat 2k and seat 2k+1 (the gap between sections) every plant position is a possible divider spot. Answer = product of (plants in that gap + 1) over those gaps, mod 1e9+7.

cards.name: Number of Ways to Form a Target String Given a Dictionary
cards.time: O(W * L + L * T) for W words of length L and target length T
cards.trick: Precompute cnt[col][ch] over all words. dp[i][j] = ways to build the first i target chars using the first j columns: dp[i][j-1] (skip column) + dp[i-1][j-1] * cnt[j-1][target[i-1]] (use it). Roll the table to one array.

cards.name: Number of Ways to Rearrange Sticks With K Sticks Visible
cards.trick: Think about placing the tallest stick or the shortest one last. dp[n][k] = dp[n-1][k-1] (shortest stick placed first and visible) + (n - 1) * dp[n-1][k] (shortest hidden in any of n - 1 non-front slots). These are unsigned Stirling numbers of the first kind. Mod 1e9+7.

cards.name: Number of Ways to Split Array
cards.trick: Total sum first, then a running left prefix. Count split points i in 0..n-2 where left >= total - left.

cards.name: Number of Ways to Stay in the Same Place After Some Steps
cards.trick: dp[s][p] = ways to be at p with s steps left = dp[s-1][p-1] + dp[s-1][p] + dp[s-1][p+1]. Only positions up to steps / 2 can ever return to 0, so cap the width at min(arrLen, steps / 2 + 1). Roll to two rows. Mod 1e9+7.

cards.name: Number of Zero-Filled Subarrays
cards.trick: Track the current run length of zeros. Each new zero at the end of a run of length r adds r subarrays ending there, so add the running count to the answer; reset to 0 on a nonzero.

cards.name: One Edit Distance
cards.trick: Make s the shorter string (swap if needed) and return false if the lengths differ by more than 1. Find the first mismatch: equal length means the rest must match after skipping both chars, length diff 1 means the rest must match after skipping the longer string char. No mismatch means true only if lengths differ by exactly 1.

cards.name: Ones and Zeroes
cards.time: O(L * m * n) for L strings
cards.trick: 0/1 knapsack with two capacities. dp[i][j] = max strings using at most i zeros and j ones. For each string with z zeros and o ones, update dp[i][j] = max(dp[i][j], dp[i-z][j-o] + 1) iterating i and j downward so each string is used once.

cards.name: Online Stock Span
cards.trick: Monotonic decreasing stack of (price, span). On a new price pop every entry with price <= it, summing their spans into the new span (starting at 1), then push. Each entry is pushed and popped once.

cards.name: Open the Lock
cards.time: O(10^4 * 4 * 2) states and edges (O(10^N * N) for N wheels)
cards.trick: BFS from 0000 where each state has 8 neighbors (each wheel +1 or -1 with wrap). Put deadends in the visited set up front; if 0000 is a deadend return -1. Return the BFS depth when target is reached.

cards.name: Operations on Tree
cards.time: O(1) lock and unlock, O(n) upgrade
cards.trick: Store parent array, children lists and an array of who locked each node. Upgrade needs: node unlocked, no locked ancestor (walk up parents), and at least one locked descendant (DFS down, unlocking them as you go). Only commit the unlocks and lock after all three checks pass.

cards.name: Optimal Account Balancing
cards.time: O(n * 2^n) for n people with nonzero balance
cards.trick: Net each person's balance and drop zeros. Settling a zero-sum group of size k needs k - 1 transfers, so maximize the number of disjoint zero-sum groups: dp[mask] = max over removed bit of dp[mask without bit], plus 1 if sum[mask] == 0. Answer = n - dp[full]. (DFS pairing a debtor with a creditor is O(n!) worst case.)

cards.name: Optimal Partition of String
cards.trick: Greedy: extend the current substring until a character repeats, then start a new substring there. Track the chars in the current piece with a set or bitmask and count the partitions.

cards.name: Optimize Water Distribution in a Village
cards.time: O((n + m) log(n + m)) for n houses and m pipes
cards.trick: Add a virtual node 0 and an edge from 0 to house i with cost wells[i-1]. Then the answer is the minimum spanning tree of this graph (Kruskal with Union-Find or Prim with a heap).

cards.name: Out of Boundary Paths
cards.trick: dp[move][r][c] = ways to be at (r, c) after move steps. For each step push counts to the 4 neighbors; a neighbor outside the grid adds to the answer instead. Mod 1e9+7. Use two m x n layers.

cards.name: Output Contest Matches
cards.trick: Start with strings 1..n. Each round pair the i-th with the (len - 1 - i)-th as '(a,b)' to form the next list, halving it until one string is left. Total output is O(n) per round over log n rounds.

cards.name: Paint Fence
cards.trick: Track same (last two posts same color) and diff. same_new = diff, diff_new = (same + diff) * (k - 1). Total = same + diff. Equivalent: ways[i] = (k - 1) * (ways[i-1] + ways[i-2]). Handle n = 1 as k.

cards.name: Paint House
cards.trick: Keep the min cost of finishing each house in each of 3 colors. cost[i][c] += min of the other two colors' totals from the previous house. Answer is min of the last row, can update costs in place.

cards.name: Paint House II
cards.trick: Per house only the smallest and second smallest totals from the previous house matter. For color c use min1 if c is not the color that gave min1, else min2. Scanning k colors per house, no inner k loop needed. (Naive is O(n * k^2).)

cards.name: Painting the Walls
cards.trick: Knapsack. Choosing wall i for the paid painter costs cost[i] and also covers time[i] free walls, so it covers time[i] + 1 walls in total. dp[j] = min cost to cover j walls: dp[j] = min(dp[j], dp[max(0, j - time[i] - 1)] + cost[i]), iterating j downward. Answer dp[n].

cards.name: Palindrome Linked List
cards.trick: Find the middle with slow/fast pointers, reverse the second half in place, then compare it to the first half node by node. (Optionally reverse again to restore the list. Array copy is O(n) space.)

cards.name: Palindrome Number
cards.trick: Negatives and numbers ending in 0 (except 0) are false. Reverse only the second half of the digits while reversed < remaining x, then check x == rev or x == rev / 10 for odd length. Avoids overflow and string conversion.

cards.name: Palindrome Permutation
cards.trick: A permutation can be a palindrome iff at most one character has an odd count. Toggle each char in a set (add if absent, remove if present) and check the final set size is <= 1.

cards.name: Palindrome Permutation II
cards.trick: Count chars; if more than one has an odd count return empty. Put half of each char count into a multiset and backtrack over its distinct permutations (loop over distinct chars with count > 0, so no duplicates). Each half h becomes h + middle + reverse(h).

cards.name: Palindrome Removal
cards.trick: Interval DP. dp[i][j] = min moves to clear arr[i..j]. Options: remove arr[i] alone (1 + dp[i+1][j]); if arr[i] == arr[i+1] then 1 + dp[i+2][j]; for each k with arr[i] == arr[k], dp[i+1][k-1] + dp[k+1][j] (arr[i] and arr[k] go with the last removal of the inner part).

cards.name: Parallel Courses
cards.trick: Kahn's topological sort by levels. Each BFS layer of zero in-degree courses is one semester. If the number of courses taken is less than n there is a cycle, so return -1.

cards.name: Parallel Courses III
cards.trick: Topological order (Kahn) with DP: finish[v] = time[v] + max(finish of its prerequisites). Process in topo order pushing finish[u] to dependents as start time. Answer = max finish over all courses (longest path in a DAG).

cards.name: Parsing A Boolean Expression
cards.trick: Push every char except ',' on a stack. On ')' pop until '(' collecting t/f values, pop the operator and apply it: '!' flips the one value, '&' is all true, '|' is any true. Push the result back. Final stack top is the answer.

cards.name: Partition Array According to Given Pivot
cards.trick: Stable three-way split: collect elements less than pivot, equal to pivot, and greater than pivot in order into three lists and concatenate.

cards.name: Partition Array for Maximum Sum
cards.trick: dp[i] = best sum for the first i elements. Try a last block of length j = 1..k ending at i, tracking the running max of the block: dp[i] = max(dp[i - j] + j * blockMax).

cards.name: Partition List
cards.trick: Two dummy-headed lists: one for nodes < x and one for nodes >= x, appending in original order to keep stability. Link the tail of the small list to the head of the big list, and set the big tail's next to null to avoid a cycle.

cards.name: Partition to K Equal Sum Subsets
cards.trick: If sum % k != 0 or max > target return false. Bitmask DP: dp[mask] = current bucket fill (sum of mask mod target) or -1 if unreachable. Add an unused num if the fill + num <= target. True if dp[full] is reachable. (Plain bucket backtracking is exponential, sort descending to prune.)

cards.name: Pascal's Triangle
cards.trick: Each row starts and ends with 1. Interior element = prev[j-1] + prev[j] from the previous row. Build row by row.

cards.name: Pascal's Triangle II
cards.trick: Row k is the binomial coefficients C(k, j). Build iteratively: C(k, j+1) = C(k, j) * (k - j) / (j + 1), with integer division after the multiply. (In-place right-to-left row updates are O(k^2).)

cards.name: Path Crossing
cards.trick: Walk the path from (0, 0), storing every visited coordinate in a set. Return true as soon as a move lands on a visited point.

cards.name: Path Sum
cards.trick: DFS subtracting the node value from the target. At a leaf (no children) return whether the remaining target is 0. A null node returns false, and a node counts only if it is a real leaf.

cards.name: Path Sum IV
cards.trick: Decode each 3-digit number into depth d, position p, value v and store map[(d, p)] = v. DFS from (1, 1) with a running sum; children are (d+1, 2p-1) and (d+1, 2p). When neither child exists it is a leaf, add the running sum to the total.

cards.name: Path With Maximum Gold
cards.time: O(m * n * 3^k) where k = number of gold cells (at most 25)
cards.trick: DFS backtracking from every nonzero cell. Mark the current cell visited by setting it to 0, explore 4 neighbors, take the max, then restore the value. Branching factor is at most 3 after the first step.

cards.name: Path With Maximum Minimum Value
cards.trick: Dijkstra-like with a max-heap keyed by the path's minimum so far. Pop the best cell, push unvisited neighbors with min(current score, neighbor value). First time you pop the bottom-right cell is the answer. (Binary search + BFS or sorted Union-Find also work.)

cards.name: Path with Maximum Probability
cards.trick: Dijkstra with a max-heap on probability, multiplying edge probabilities along the path (multiplying by values <= 1 only shrinks, so greedy is valid). Return 0 if end is unreachable. (Bellman-Ford is O(V * E).)

cards.name: Path With Minimum Effort
cards.trick: Dijkstra where the cost of a path is its max absolute height difference so far: new effort = max(current effort, |h diff|). Min-heap on effort; first pop of the bottom-right cell is the answer. (Binary search on effort + BFS is O(m * n * log H).)

cards.name: Paths in Maze That Lead to Same Room
cards.trick: A confusion score of 3 means counting triangles. Build adjacency sets; for each edge (u, v) with u < v count common neighbors w > v (or orient edges toward the higher-degree node) so each triangle is counted exactly once.

cards.name: Perfect Squares
cards.time: O(sqrt n) with the four-square theorem (O(n * sqrt n) for the DP)
cards.trick: Lagrange: the answer is at most 4. Return 1 if n is a perfect square; 4 if n reduces to the form 8b + 7 after dividing out all factors of 4; 2 if n = a^2 + b^2 for some a; else 3. Standard DP: dp[i] = 1 + min(dp[i - s^2]).

cards.name: Perform String Shifts
cards.trick: Shifts compose, so net = sum(amount) with left as + and right as -. Take net mod n and rotate the string once (s[net:] + s[:net]).

cards.name: Permutations II
cards.trick: Sort first, then backtrack with a used[] array. Skip nums[i] if it equals nums[i-1] and nums[i-1] is not used in the current path, so equal values are always taken in left-to-right order. (Count map backtracking is equivalent.)

cards.name: Plus One Linked List
cards.trick: Add a dummy 0 head. Find the last node that is not 9, increment it, and set every node after it to 0. Return the dummy if it became 1, else dummy.next. No reversal or recursion needed.

cards.name: Populating Next Right Pointers in Each Node
cards.trick: Perfect binary tree, so use the next pointers already built. Walk level by level from the leftmost node: node.left.next = node.right, and node.right.next = node.next.left if node.next exists. (BFS with a queue is O(n) space.)

cards.name: Pour Water
cards.time: O(V * n) for V units of water
cards.trick: Simulate each drop at index k. Walk left while the next height is not higher, remembering the lowest (nearest to k on ties) position that is strictly lower than the start; if found, drop there. Else do the same to the right. Else drop stays at k.

cards.name: Pour Water Between Buckets to Make Water Levels Equal
cards.trick: Binary search on the final level L (a float). Buckets above L give up (b - L) water but only (1 - loss%) of it arrives; buckets below L need (L - b). L is feasible if total received >= total needed. Move up if feasible, else down.

cards.name: Power of Four
cards.trick: n > 0, n has a single set bit (n & (n - 1) == 0), and that bit is at an even position: n & 0x55555555 != 0.

cards.name: Power of Two
cards.trick: A power of two has exactly one set bit, so n > 0 and n & (n - 1) == 0. The n > 0 check rules out 0 and negatives.

cards.name: Prime Subtraction Operation
cards.time: O(M log log M + n log M) with M = max(nums)
cards.trick: Sieve primes up to M. Go left to right keeping prev; for each nums[i] subtract the largest prime p < nums[i] with nums[i] - p > prev (binary search the prime list), or none if nothing fits. Subtracting as much as possible keeps the most room for later elements. Fail if nums[i] <= prev.

cards.name: Print Immutable Linked List in Reverse
cards.space: O(n) recursion (O(sqrt n) with block decomposition)
cards.trick: Recurse to the end then print on the way back, using only the allowed getNext and printValue. Follow-up: split into sqrt(n) blocks, keep block heads on a stack, and reverse-print each block recursively for O(sqrt n) space. (Repeated traversal is O(1) space but O(n^2) time.)

cards.name: Process Tasks Using Servers
cards.trick: Two min-heaps: free servers by (weight, index) and busy servers by (free time, weight, index). At each time t = max(i, ...) release all busy servers whose time <= t. If no server is free, jump t to the earliest busy finish time. Assign task i to the best free server.

cards.name: Product of Two Run-Length Encoded Arrays
cards.trick: Two pointers over the encoded arrays. Take freq = min of the current frequencies, product = val1 * val2, subtract freq from both, and advance whichever hit 0. If the product equals the last output value just add to its frequency to keep it merged.

cards.name: Profitable Schemes
cards.time: O(L * n * minProfit) for L crimes
cards.trick: 0/1 knapsack with two dimensions. dp[members][profit] with profit capped at minProfit. For each crime update members from n down to its group size: dp[j][min(minProfit, p + profit)] += dp[j - group][p]. Answer sum of dp[j][minProfit] over j. Mod 1e9+7.

cards.name: Pseudo-Palindromic Paths in a Binary Tree
cards.trick: A path is pseudo-palindromic iff at most one digit has an odd count. DFS with a 10-bit mask, XOR the node's digit bit. At a leaf count 1 if mask & (mask - 1) == 0.

cards.name: Push Dominoes
cards.trick: Force array. Left to right: R gives a big force that decays by 1 per step, L resets it to 0. Right to left: L gives a negative force that decays. Sum the two and the sign decides each domino (+ R, - L, 0 stays). (Two pointers between non-dot chars is O(1) extra space.)

cards.name: Put Boxes Into the Warehouse I
cards.trick: Boxes enter from the left, so room i is effectively capped by the min height from the entrance to i. Compute prefix mins, sort boxes ascending, then scan rooms from the deepest (smallest cap) and match the smallest unplaced box if it fits.

cards.name: Put Boxes Into the Warehouse II
cards.time: O(n log n + m log m)
cards.trick: Boxes can enter from either end, so the effective cap of room i is max(min height from the left up to i, min height from the right up to i). Sort the caps and boxes and greedily match the smallest boxes with the smallest caps they fit.

cards.name: Put Marbles in Bags
cards.trick: Splitting into k bags means choosing k - 1 cut points, each costing w[i] + w[i+1]. Sort all adjacent pair sums; max score - min score = (sum of the largest k - 1) - (sum of the smallest k - 1). (Quickselect or heaps avoid the full sort.)

cards.name: Random Pick with Weight
cards.time: O(n) init, O(log n) per pick
cards.trick: Prefix sums of the weights. Pick a random int in [1, total] (or float in [0, total)) and binary search for the first prefix >= it. Index i gets a slice of size w[i], so the probability is proportional to w[i].

cards.name: Range Addition
cards.trick: Difference array: for each update add inc at start and subtract inc at end + 1. A final prefix sum over the difference array yields all values.

cards.name: Range Sum of BST
cards.trick: DFS with BST pruning. If node.val < low only the right subtree can contain valid values, if node.val > high only the left. Otherwise add node.val and visit both sides.

cards.name: Range Sum of Sorted Subarray Sums
cards.time: O(n log S) where S = total sum
cards.trick: Binary search on a value x and use two pointers over positive numbers to get the count and sum of all subarray sums <= x. The sum of the k smallest = sum(<= x) + (k - count) * x for the smallest x with count >= k. Answer = f(right) - f(left - 1). (Heap k-way merge or sort is O(n^2 log n).)

cards.name: Range Sum Query 2D - Immutable
cards.time: O(m * n) build, O(1) per query
cards.trick: 2-D prefix sum with an extra zero row and column. pre[i][j] = a + pre[i-1][j] + pre[i][j-1] - pre[i-1][j-1]. Query = pre[r2+1][c2+1] - pre[r1][c2+1] - pre[r2+1][c1] + pre[r1][c1] (inclusion-exclusion).

cards.name: Range Sum Query 2D - Mutable
cards.time: O(log m * log n) per update and query, O(m * n * log m * log n) build
cards.trick: 2-D Binary Indexed Tree (Fenwick). update(r, c, delta) loops i += i & -i over rows and the same over columns. Prefix query is the mirror with i -= i & -i, then use inclusion-exclusion for the rectangle. Update stores delta = val - current.

cards.name: Range Sum Query - Immutable
cards.trick: Prefix sum array with a leading 0. sumRange(l, r) = pre[r + 1] - pre[l].

cards.name: Ransom Note
cards.trick: Count the letters in magazine, then for each char in ransomNote decrement its count and fail if it would go below 0.

cards.name: Read N Characters Given Read4
cards.trick: Loop calling read4 into a 4-char temp buffer, copying min(count, n - total) chars to buf each time. Stop when read4 returns less than 4 (end of file) or n chars were read.

cards.name: Read N Characters Given Read4 II - Call Multiple Times
cards.trick: Keep a persistent 4-char buffer plus a read pointer and a count of valid chars across calls. read() first drains leftovers, and calls read4 only when the buffer is empty. Leftover chars from the previous call are never lost.

cards.name: Rearrange Array Elements by Sign
cards.trick: Allocate a result array with two write indices: positives at 0, 2, 4, ... and negatives at 1, 3, 5, .... One pass over nums puts each value at its pointer and advances it by 2, preserving relative order.

cards.name: Rearrange String k Distance Apart
cards.time: O(n log A) for alphabet size A, about O(n)
cards.trick: Count frequencies, max-heap by count. Pop the most frequent char, append it, decrement it and park it in a cooldown queue; once the queue length reaches k release the front back to the heap. If the heap is empty before the string is built return an empty string.

cards.name: Recover a Tree From Preorder Traversal
cards.trick: Parse the string into (depth = count of dashes, value) pairs. Keep a stack of the current root-to-node path: pop until stack size equals depth, then attach the new node as left child if the parent has none, else right. Push it.

cards.name: Recover Binary Search Tree
cards.trick: Inorder of a BST is sorted, so two swapped nodes create one or two descents. First descent (prev > cur): first = prev. Last descent: second = cur. Swap the two values. Morris traversal keeps extra space at O(1).

cards.name: Redistribute Characters to Make All Strings Equal
cards.trick: Characters can be moved freely, so count each letter over all words. Every letter count must be divisible by the number of words.

cards.name: Regions Cut By Slashes
cards.trick: Union-Find on the (n + 1) x (n + 1) grid points: border points are pre-unioned to one root, and each slash unions its two endpoints. If a slash joins two points already connected it closes a loop, adding a region (regions start at 1). (Upscale each cell to 3 x 3 and count components is an alternative.)

cards.name: Relative Sort Array
cards.time: O(n + m + R) for value range R (0..1000)
cards.trick: Counting sort. Count arr1 by value, emit each value of arr2 in order count times, then emit the remaining values in ascending order. (Custom key sort is O(n log n).)

cards.name: Remove 9
cards.trick: Numbers without a digit 9 are exactly the numbers in base 9 read as decimal. The n-th such number is n written in base 9: repeatedly take n % 9 and n // 9 to build the digits.

cards.name: Remove All Adjacent Duplicates in String II
cards.trick: Stack of (char, run count). For each char, if it matches the top increment the count, else push (char, 1). When a count reaches k pop it. Rebuild the string from the stack.

cards.name: Remove All Ones With Row and Column Flips
cards.trick: Possible iff every row is either identical to the first row or its exact complement (flipping rows and columns preserves this). Compare each row to row 0: either every cell is equal or every cell differs.

cards.name: Remove All Ones With Row and Column Flips II
cards.trick: Grid has at most 15 cells, so encode it as a bitmask. dp[mask] = 1 + min over each set cell of dp[mask with that cell's whole row and column cleared], dp[0] = 0. Memoized DFS or BFS over masks.

cards.name: Remove Colored Pieces if Both Neighbors Are the Same Color
cards.trick: Moves never interact: a move removes a middle piece of a run of 3+ of the player's own color, so a run of length L gives L - 2 moves. Count total moves for A and B; Alice wins iff her count is strictly greater.

cards.name: Remove Covered Intervals
cards.trick: Sort by start ascending, end descending, so a covering interval always comes first. Track the max end so far: an interval with end <= maxEnd is covered, otherwise count it and update maxEnd.

cards.name: Remove Duplicates From an Unsorted Linked List
cards.trick: Two passes. First pass counts value frequencies in a hash map. Second pass uses a dummy head and deletes every node whose value has count > 1 (all copies are removed, not just extras).

cards.name: Remove Duplicates From Sorted Array II
cards.trick: Write pointer w starts at 2. Copy nums[i] to nums[w] only if nums[i] != nums[w - 2], then advance w. Comparing with the slot two behind allows each value at most twice.

cards.name: Remove Duplicates From Sorted List
cards.trick: Walk with cur. While cur.next exists and has the same value, skip it with cur.next = cur.next.next; otherwise advance cur. Sorted order means duplicates are adjacent.

cards.name: Remove Element
cards.trick: Slow write pointer and fast read pointer. Copy nums[fast] to nums[slow] whenever it is not val, then advance slow. Return slow. (Swapping with the last element when order does not matter does fewer writes.)

cards.name: Remove Interval
cards.trick: One pass over the sorted disjoint intervals. If no overlap, keep it. Otherwise keep the left remainder [start, remove.start) if start < remove.start and the right remainder [remove.end, end) if end > remove.end.

cards.name: Remove K Digits
cards.trick: Monotonic increasing stack. While k > 0 and the top digit is greater than the current digit, pop it. After the loop pop the remaining k from the end, strip leading zeros, return '0' if empty.

cards.name: Remove Linked List Elements
cards.trick: Dummy node before head so removing the head needs no special case. Use prev/cur: if cur.val == val set prev.next = cur.next, else move prev forward.

cards.name: Remove Max Number of Edges to Keep Graph Fully Traversable
cards.trick: Two union-finds (Alice, Bob). Add type 3 edges first (shared, count one if it merges in either), then type 1 for Alice and type 2 for Bob. Every edge that fails to merge is removable. If either DSU is not one component return -1.

cards.name: Remove Nodes From Linked List
cards.trick: Reverse the list, walk it keeping a running max and delete any node smaller than the max, then reverse back. (Monotonic decreasing stack or recursion is O(n) space.)

cards.name: Remove Sub-Folders From the Filesystem
cards.time: O(n * L) (n folders, L = max path length)
cards.trick: Insert paths into a trie keyed by path component and mark end nodes. Stop descending past a marked end node, so only top-level folders are kept. (Sort lexicographically and skip paths starting with prev + '/' is O(n * L log n).)

cards.name: Remove Vowels From a String
cards.trick: Single pass with a set of 'aeiou'. Append each char not in the set to the result and join at the end.

cards.name: Removing Stars From a String
cards.trick: Use a stack of chars. Push letters; on '*' pop the top (the closest non-star char on its left). Join the stack at the end.

cards.name: Reorder Routes to Make All Paths Lead to the City Zero
cards.trick: Treat the tree as undirected, storing each edge with a flag for its original direction. DFS/BFS from city 0; every edge traversed away from 0 whose original direction also points away from 0 must be reversed, so count those.

cards.name: Reorganize String
cards.trick: Impossible iff max count > (n + 1) / 2. Otherwise place the most frequent char at indices 0, 2, 4, ... then fill the rest of the even slots and then odd slots in frequency order. (Max-heap popping the two most frequent each step is O(n log 26).)

cards.name: Repeated DNA Sequences
cards.trick: Slide a fixed window of length 10 and keep a seen set plus a result set. Add the substring to the result when it is already in seen. Encode with 2 bits per base (rolling hash) to avoid O(10) substring cost.

cards.name: Replace Elements With Greatest Element on Right Side
cards.trick: Scan right to left with a running max starting at -1. At each index save the old value, write the running max, then update max = max(max, old value).

cards.name: Restore IP Addresses
cards.trick: Backtrack over 4 segments, each 1 to 3 digits. A segment must be <= 255 and have no leading zero (except '0' itself). Prune if the remaining digits cannot fill the remaining segments, and record when 4 segments use all digits.

cards.name: Reveal Cards in Increasing Order
cards.trick: Sort the deck ascending. Simulate the reveal on a deque of indices 0..n-1: pop the front index and assign the next smallest card to it, then move the new front index to the back. Repeat until empty.

cards.name: Reverse Linked List II
cards.trick: Dummy head, walk to the node just before position left. Then repeat right - left times: take cur.next and insert it right after that pre node (head insertion). One pass, no extra memory.

cards.name: Reverse Odd Levels of Binary Tree
cards.trick: Tree is perfect, so DFS two mirrored nodes at once: dfs(left, right, level). If level is odd, swap their values. Recurse with (left.left, right.right) and (left.right, right.left). (BFS reversing each odd level is O(n) space.)

cards.name: Reverse String
cards.trick: Pointers at both ends, swap and move inward until they meet.

cards.name: Reverse Substrings Between Each Pair of Parentheses
cards.trick: First pass with a stack pairs each '(' with its ')'. Second pass walks the string with a direction flag: on any parenthesis jump to its partner and flip direction, otherwise emit the char. (Stack of strings reversing on ')' is O(n^2).)

cards.name: Reverse Words in a String II
cards.trick: On the char array, reverse the whole array first, then reverse each word in place (scan to the next space, reverse that span). Reversing twice restores each word's letter order.

cards.name: Reverse Words in a String III
cards.space: O(n) (O(1) on a mutable char array)
cards.trick: Scan for word boundaries at spaces and reverse each word with two pointers, keeping word order. Spaces stay in place.

cards.name: Robot Bounded in Circle
cards.trick: Run the instructions once. The robot is bounded iff it is back at the origin or not facing north. A non-north heading means after at most 4 cycles it returns to the start.

cards.name: Robot Collisions
cards.trick: Sort robot indices by position. Stack holds right-moving robots. A left-moving robot fights the stack top: equal health removes both, otherwise the weaker dies and the stronger loses 1 health. Output survivors in original index order.

cards.name: Robot Room Cleaner
cards.time: O(N) (N = open cells, 4 moves tried per cell)
cards.trick: DFS on relative coordinates with a visited set. Clean, then for each of 4 directions try to move; after recursing, backtrack physically (turn 180, move, turn 180) and turn right to try the next direction.

cards.name: Roman to Integer
cards.trick: Map symbols to values. If a symbol is smaller than the one after it, subtract it, otherwise add it (handles IV, IX, XL, etc.).

cards.name: Rotate Array
cards.trick: Set k %= n. Reverse the whole array, then reverse the first k elements, then reverse the rest. (Copying into a new array at (i + k) % n is O(n) space.)

cards.name: Rotate List
cards.trick: Find the length n and tail, link the tail to the head to make a circle. Then walk n - (k % n) steps from the head to the new tail, set the new head to its next and cut the link.

cards.name: Rotating the Box
cards.trick: Apply gravity per row first: scan right to left keeping the next empty slot; a stone moves to that slot, an obstacle resets the slot to just left of it. Then rotate 90 degrees clockwise: res[j][m - 1 - i] = box[i][j].

cards.name: Russian Doll Envelopes
